News.title: Blood-soaked epidemic of £100 hitmen crippling South Africa’s streets as 140 slaughtered in one year
News.content:
Next

AS mother-of-three Johannah Phenya was making breakfast she heard gun shots ring out in a wealthy Johannesburg suburb – and was instantly consumed with fear.

Just a few weeks earlier the South African IT company director and her husband Eric received threats to their life for uncovering an alleged corrupt government contract.



Running towards the sounds of the ambulance just a few blocks away, Johannah spotted the silver foil covering a body on the ground.

Her husband had not answered his phone and her fears were soon confirmed.



Eric, 57, died in a hail of bullets fired by at least two assassins as he sat at the traffic lights in Roodepoort in October 2022, while returning from dropping their young children at school.

He was one of 141 targeted killings in South Africa in the same year.



The hitmen are not highly trained professionals, instead they are desperate men paid as little as £125 to end a life.

Even though they have no idea who their ultimate employer is, many of them end up dead in order to prevent these murderers from revealing any information.

Now a Channel 4 Unreported World documentary titled South Africa’s Whistleblower Hitmen has spoken to one of the secretive assassins.

The unidentified killer says: “In my name I have done about eight jobs. People go down for three grand to five grand (£125 to £200).



“It’s all about how we solve problems for rich people, that’s what we do. When you are in that job I don’t consider you human.

“You are a thing. You are the trouble and I have to solve that problem. I don’t humanise them. There are no feelings needed. I needed that money.”

The fee is so low because it is a “buyers’ market.”

In South Africa’s poverty stricken townships there are plenty of young men willing to kill for cash.

The Global Initiative Against Transnational Organised Crime says that in the ten years to 2024 contract killings increased by 108 percent.



Who the target is matters little to the assassins.

Eric and Johannah were just business people with a sense of civic duty.

While their company Foursight IT Business Solutions was working for the Department of Home Affairs they spotted an alleged dodgy deal.

They reported the irregularities to officials within the government department, unknowingly putting their lives in danger.

That became clear as they celebrated their 21st wedding anniversary while on holiday in Greece.



A man rang Johannah on the phone and told her “a hit has been taken out on you or your husband. We also know the whereabouts of where you drop off your kids.”

Whichever parent was caught in the crosshairs first was dead.

Now Johannah has an armed private bodyguard with her wherever she goes and her children are unable to attend school, go out with friends or even go to the cinema.



She says: “You don’t know who is following you, who is behind you, you have to be vigilant all the time. It’s heartbreaking.”

Four years on from her husband’s murder only one suspect has appeared in court.

Minenhle Mthembu is accused of conspiracy to commit Eric’s murder.

Another man linked to the case, Bongani Maocuana, was killed in a nightclub shooting.

Whoever ordered Eric to be shot has not been charged by the police, although they are reportedly known to detectives.



Private detectives IRS Forensic Investigations believe they have uncovered their identities.

They said: “What is distressing is the fact that we are almost 100 percent certain as to who ordered the hit, yet despite the linkages, these people remain free.

“This is why we see emboldened criminals ordering hits – because there are no consequences to their actions.”



For the hitmen it is a very risky business.

Darshna Soni, Channel 4’s Communities Editor, who spoke to the hitman, says: “They’re killed themselves when they’re no longer useful.”

The hitman, who hides his identity behind shades and a hood, admits to be haunted by the lives he’s taken.

He says: “I don’t sleep at night. They keep haunting me. Sometimes I have flashbacks.”

South Africa’s murder rate dropped by almost ten percent last year, but 58 people were still killed every day in the most recent figures.



It is ranked 81st out of 182 countries in the perceived corruption index and some areas face a lack of running water due to creaking infrastructure.

There have been calls for a major anti-corruption clean up in South Africa’s largest city Johannesburg, which is known as the “city of Gold.”

That’s going to be difficult when anyone who raises the alarm faces being killed.



The death toll is so high that an organisation called Public Interest SA holds annual events to honour murdered whistleblowers.

Among 2026’s Posthumous Fallen Heroes of Integrity Awards was brave auditor Mpho Mafole.

The 47-year-old father-of-three reported irregularities in an £18million deal to provide chemical toilets in townships lacking sanitary facilities in the city of Ekurhuleni.



It was Mpho’s job to report those concerns and he did so.

Three days later, in June 2025, the car he was driving was riddled with bullets, leaving his dead body slumped in his bloodied seat.

One suspect has been questioned by the police and another is on the run.

But the family hired their own detectives to find out who was involved in the plot because they were frustrated by the slow pace of the police investigation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His dad Keikelame Mafole concludes: “We want justice. We want to know who did it.”



Unreported World: South Africa’s Whistleblower Hitmen is on Channel 4 at 7.30pm on November 6.

News.title: ‘Frankenstein’ killer who butchered young sailors jailed again for sexually assaulting four men while working in Navy
News.content:
BEAST CAGED ‘Frankenstein’ killer who butchered young sailors jailed again for sexually assaulting four men while working in Navy







Next

A “FRANKENSTEIN” killer who butchered two young sailors has been jailed for sexually assaulting four men while working in the Navy.

Allan Grimson lured two young recruits back to his flat in Portsmouth then brutally murdered them when they spurned his advances.



He first slaughtered Nicholas Wright, 18, on December 12, 1997 – before murdering Sion Jenkins, 20, exactly 12 months later.

The former petty officer – dubbed the “Royal Navy‘s Dennis Nilsen” – is feared to have killed up to 20 people.



He has also been named as the prime suspect in the disappearance of Simon Parkes – an 18-year-old Royal Navy sailor who was last seen in December 1986 in Gibraltar, where Grimson was stationed at the time.

Grimson has now been jailed for a further 22 years after he was convicted of sexually assaulting three young men in the Navy and one teenager around the same time as he killed Sion and Nicholas.

Chillingly, he abused the victims in the same flat in Portsmouth where he murdered the pair.

The fiend was also found guilty of 11 counts of indecent assault, one count of rape and one count of taking indecent photographs of a child.



Winchester Crown Court heard he could have been released on parole while serving his life sentence – until he was charged with the historic offences.

Grimson preyed on the victims between February 1994 and November 1999.

He told police one of the men was “lucky to be alive”, before adding: “If you’re going to rape somebody, to get away with it, kill it.”

One of his sex attack victims said he could only open up about the horror after Grimson was jailed in 2001 because he then felt “safe”.

Grimson served in the Royal Navy and in 1999 he was a serving Petty Officer Marine Engineering Mechanic and an instructor at the Royal Navy Firefighting School in Horsea Island, Portsmouth.



The prosecution said that this brought Grimson, a “big, powerful man” into contact with a lot of young men in their late teens.

Hulking Grimson – known as the “Frankenstein” killer – struck fear into the heart of the Royal Navy in the 1990s as he targeted sailors to butcher in a depraved reign of terror.

He first targeted Nicholas, 18, who was bludgeoned with a baseball bat after he rejected Grimson’s sexual advances.

The monster then sliced his ear off with a diving knife.

Once Nicholas was too hurt to defend himself, the brute slit his throat.



The next day, Grimson wrapped his naked body up – later telling police he’d felt a “tingling” sensation while doing so.

He then dumped the naval rating’s mutilated body in a ditch.

Exactly one year later, Grimson attacked and raped Sion in his house of horrors before tying him up and putting him in a bathtub.

As the 20-year-old begged to go home, the killer beat him to death with a bat before dumping his body by the side of the A32.

Grimson confessed to his sadistic crimes in excruciating detail – leading one expert to brand him the most dangerous psychopath of the 250 he had examined.



He was jailed in 2001 at Winchester Crown Court for life with a minimum of 22 years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sentencing him at the time, Mr Justice Cresswell told him: “You are a serial killer in nature if not in number.

“You are a highly dangerous serial killer who killed two young men in horrifying circumstances.”

News.title: ‘Unlucky’ dad whose only ever prize was a dead goldfish scoops £4m country mansion with its own lake – and £250k cash
News.content:
Next

AN “UNLUCKY” dad whose only ever prize was a dead goldfish has now bagged a £4million country mansion.

Malcolm Disson, 58, now owns a Grade II listed six-bedroom home with its own lake, tennis court and two-bedroom cottage.



The lucky father-of-two who grew up in London has won the Omaze Million Pound House Draw plus £250,000 in cash.

Malcolm says the only thing he can remember winning before was a goldfish at Hampstead Heath fair when he was 12.



He won it by bouncing ping pong balls into goldfish bowls but it was already dead when he opened the bag.

Two weeks ago, he won £8 on a lottery, so he thought his “luck was finally starting to turn”.

Malcolm’s stunning new home in Little Ouseburn in Yorkshire comes mortgage-free, with all stamp duty and legal fees covered, as well as £155,000 worth of furnishings.

His winning entry cost £30 as part of his Omaze subscription.

Malcolm said: “I’ve never really thought of myself as a lucky person.

”For years, the only thing I’d ever won was a goldfish at Hampstead Heath fair.

‘And when I opened the bag it was already dead! That set the tone for the next 46 years as I didn’t win a sausage after that.



“Then two weeks ago I won £8 on a lottery and thought my luck was finally changing. I thought I’d peaked with that.

”I certainly didn’t expect to go all the way from a dead goldfish to a £4 million mansion with its own lake… full of fish that are alive and well!”

Malcolm has two daughters, Lilly, 22, and Daisy, 18.

Thirty-five years ago, he lived in a three-bedroom terraced house in Watford.

He has lived in Newbury for the past 18 years and currently lives in a semi-detached house.



Malcolm co-founded The British Shop, a specialist fine art and antiques packing and international shipping company based near Heathrow, in 2004.

He remortgaged his house to get it off the ground, but struggled to afford the payments for the first couple of years and says the risk almost ruined him.

A keen cook, Malcolm is planning to bring the family together at the house for Christmas.

Malcolm had never been to Yorkshire before visiting his new home. He has since enjoyed looking around York and is looking forward to trying the local pubs.

A friend has already nicknamed him the Earl of Tetley, in a joking nod to the tea brand founded in Yorkshire.



On settling in, he said: “I’d never been to Yorkshire before – what a way to visit for the first time, coming to your own £4 million house! I can’t wait to try the local pubs, and beers!

“I had tennis lessons as a kid and played quite a bit around 40 years ago, so I’ll have to dust off my backhand and work on my serve.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

”I can’t believe I’ve got a potting shed and a library too – I haven’t had much time to read, but I’ll make time now. That’s what this win will give me, more time to spend with family and loved ones.”

As well as making Malcolm a multi-millionaire, the Omaze Million Pound House Draw, Yorkshire, raised money to support Blood Cancer UK.

News.title: Strict new ban plotted across swimming pools and changing rooms after Wetherspoons crackdown
News.content:
Next

A NEW ban may be coming to swimming pools and changing rooms across the UK in a government crackdown.

This comes after Wetherspoons barred those wearing the technology from recording in its venues.

Plans to restrict the use of smart glasses in swimming pools and changing rooms are being consulted on by ministers, as the controversial technology continues to be criticised over privacy concerns.



The devices, which can record video, photos and audio without drawing the attention of those being filmed, have been condemned over potential harms to women and girls.



Although a small LED in the corner of the glasses indicates when the camera is active, instances have already occurred of people being accidentally recorded in intimate spaces, including gym changing rooms and bathrooms, by those wearing the tech.

Now, Liberal Democrat MP and culture spokesperson, Anna Sabine, said that “women are reporting waking up after nights out to find that videos of them, filmed without their knowledge or consent by men wearing smart glasses, have gone viral online.

“To me these devices not only have the potential to erode safety and privacy in public spaces, but raise really important questions about consent,” she added.

Conservative MP, Shivani Raja, also noted that “camera-enabled smart glasses allow covert recording to take place at eye level, completely disguised as regular human eye-to-eye contact.

“For many women who are already navigating public spaces with extra vigilance, that creates real unease.”

If plans go ahead, swimming pools and changing rooms would become the latest area to ban the smart technology in the UK.

Wetherspoon already introduced a policy in August prohibiting people from wearing Meta glasses inside its more than 800 pubs over fears that customers and employees could be recorded without their consent.



Later that month, the UK Cinema Association (UKCA) also announced that many cinemas would be “introducing policies to prohibit and/or restrict the wearing of camera-enabled smart glasses” in their venues.

However, it is unclear how many cinemas have banned the technology in their venues since.

In response to criticism at the time, a Meta spokeswoman said: “People use our glasses because they’re helpful and let them stay in the moment, from listening to music to live translation or hands-free calls.

“They also provide critical new technology for people in the blind and low vision community and limiting how people can use this technology would be a major step backwards.

News.title: Shocking moment car rams building & fireworks launched at cops – as police blast ‘misinformation’ after several injured
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a car rams a building and fireworks are launched at cops on Bonfire Night.

Chaos unfolded in in North Shields, Tyneside on Thursday evening as several cops were left injured in “shocking scenes” of violence.



Emergency services descended on the scene just before 8pm after trouble flared on the Meadow Well estate.

In shocking footage circulating on social media, groups of hooded yobs can be seen recording on their phones as a motor reverses and slams into a wall.



One clip shows thugs unleashing a barrage of fireworks at the building with a number officers injured in scenes of carnage.

Cops also said five police cars and three fire engines were damaged during the disorder as they were targeted with bricks and missiles.

It is understood the building was targeted in the mistaken belief it would be used as a a house of multi-occupancy (HMO)

Instead, the site is planned for use as a supermarket with flats above for private rent as cops slammed “misinformation”.



Northumbria Police has now arrested two men – aged 25 and 27 – a 27-year-old woman, and three teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of violent disorder and remain in custody.

Area commander for North Tyneside Chief Superintendent Daniel Whyte said: “The shocking scenes we witnessed last night in the Meadow Well were completely unacceptable.

“Our officers and firefighters were met with violence, including fireworks and bricks being thrown at them and their vehicles.

“I want to recognise their commitment and professionalism and the ongoing support we have received from our partners.”

Mr Whyte said: “We believe the disorder relates to misinformation that the building is going to be used as a house of multi-occupancy – which is not accurate.



“The site is planned for use as a supermarket with flats above for private rent.

“We are sharing this information to stop speculation in the community.”

The senior officer said: “Quite simply, the disorder, violence and damage which has occurred will not be tolerated.



“Our response has been swift and robust with a full investigation ongoing to identify those responsible.

“We have already arrested six people in connection with what happened – but we haven’t stopped there.

“Anyone involved should be expecting a knock on the door.”

Deputy chief fire officer Lynsey McVay said: “Our firefighters are there to help people and keep communities safe, so it is deeply disappointing that emergency service personnel responding to the incident were met with violence and unacceptable behaviour while carrying out their duties.

“Three fire appliances were damaged whilst dealing with a life-critical incident, highlighting the dangerous nature of these actions and the risks posed to those working to protect the public.



“As a result, these appliances weren’t available to respond to life-critical incidents, impacting our ability to protect and support the community.”

North Tyneside’s elected mayor Karen Clark said: “What happened in Meadow Well last night was appalling and completely unacceptable.

“There is no excuse for this kind of violence and disorder, particularly when emergency services are being attacked simply for doing their jobs.”

The Meadow Well estate was the scene of riots in the early 1990s.

Elsewhere, cops made 11 arrests for eight incidents during the Lewes Bonfire celebrations in East Sussex last night.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sussex Police said the incidents included assault, drunk and disorderly behaviour, possession of an offensive weapon, and criminal damage.

By 1am, paramedics had treated 52 people with four raced to hospital for further treatment.

News.title: Married couple drown in river while kayaking after desperate husband yelled ‘my wife can’t swim’ in haunting 911 call
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

KAYAK TRAGEDY Married couple drown in river while kayaking after desperate husband yelled ‘my wife can’t swim’ in haunting 911 call







Next

A MARRIED couple have drowned in a river after a shock kayaking accident.

The desperate husband shouted in a haunting 911 call that his wife could not swim after the pair ended up in the water, police said.



Cindy Bowers, 68, and her husband Anthony Beringer, 58, drowned in Salt River, Arizona, on Halloween.

Their weekend getaway turned into tragedy after their inflatable kayak capsized.



Anthony desperately yelled for help, calling 911 to try and save his drowning wife.

But Cindy went underwater.

Anthony drowned soon afterwards, seemingly as he attempted to save her.

Investigators said the couple was sharing a single kayak and neither of them wore life jackets.



Cindy’s body was found by a police helicopter around 2.11pm on Saturday.

Her husband’s remains were discovered around 50 minutes later, the Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office said.

Paul Gleason, from Mesa, wrote on Facebook that Cindy was his cousin and confirmed that the couple lived together in Chandler, Phoenix.

After the double drowning, Maricopa County Sheriff’s Office urged people to stay away from the Lower Salt River.

It warned to stay alert as the “Salt River Project (SRP) releases higher-than-normal water levels”.



“Increased flows can create dangerous currents and rapidly changing conditions.”

Flash flooding swept across Arizona at the weekend, after an atmospheric river dropped huge amounts of rain on the state.

It comes as floods struck Florida this week, where a dad-of-four died after becoming submerged in his truck in Palm Bay.

Joshua Bennett, 34, had gone to buy coffee on Monday when he got caught in powerful, riverlike floodwaters.

His heartbroken wife Stacy has revealed his final words to her.



Stacy said: “He called me on FaceTime, and he was just crying like, ‘I don’t know what to do, I don’t know what to do’.

“He said he’s in the middle of a river, and his car was submerged with water all around.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joshua sobbed as Stacy frantically urged him to smash through his truck window to escape.

But the call suddenly dropped and police found his body not long after.

News.title: Singer who starred in TV show ran £1m rogue dog breeding business for eight years with fraudster boyfriend
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PET SCAM Singer who starred in TV show ran £1m rogue dog breeding business for eight years with fraudster boyfriend







Next

A SINGER who won a TV competition ran a £1million rogue dog breeding business with her boyfriend.

Sara Pritchard Davies, 29, hid the scam when she appeared on X Factor-style competition Cân i Gymru – Song For Wales.



She was described as a Welsh version of Alicia Keys after her performance on the 2024 show.

But her budding career is now in ruins after it emerged she was behind the eight-year dog breeding scam.



Davies’ offending included hiding the true identity and origin of dogs which were being sold.

She also provided false or misleading documentation and information and operating without a licence.

Prosecutor Owen Edwards KC told the court the business was worth about £1million, with profits approaching the same amount.

Davies admitted knowingly taking part in a fraudulent business between March 2015 and November 2023.



She pleaded guilty to one charge of being involved in a fraudulent business relating to illegal dog breeding and another of acquiring £33,629 from criminal conduct.

The case was brought by Ceredigion County Council’s trading standards team.

Former boyfriend Thomas John Jones, 28, earlier also pleaded guilty to participating in a fraudulent dog breeding business between March 2015 and November 2023.

Swansea Crown Court heard Davies was no longer “associated romantically” with Jones and that the former couple had “parted ways”.

Defence barrister Ieuan Rees KC said Davies was of “pleasing character” and worked as a part-time teacher.



The singer will be sentenced on December 14.

Nerys Wyn Davies, 56, previously pleaded guilty to charges relating to illegal dog breeding.

Rebecca Ellen Bailey, 31, admitted “making an article in the commission of fraud” and providing false information in relation to nine dachshund puppies at Castle House Veterinary Practice.

News.title: Former Miss Thailand, 50, arrested over charity donation scandal as cops raid beauty queen’s house
News.content:
FALLEN QUEEN Former Miss Thailand, 50, arrested over charity donation scandal as cops raid beauty queen’s house







Next

A FORMER Miss Thailand is accused of siphoning off £22 million from her charity to buy luxury homes.

Panadda “Boom” Wongphudee, 50, was arrested outside her home in the Bueng Kum district of Bangkok over allegations of misusing donations.



Police snatched her as she exited her house to make a statement to the reporters who had gathered outside her residence.

“I’m willing to enter the legal process. I’m sorry, everyone,” the ex-beauty queen allegedly told the crowd.



Since being crowned in 2000, she has worked as an actress, a model and a presenter, becoming a household name – but has now fallen from grace.

Panadda faces charges of public fraud, money laundering and offences under Thailand’s Computer Crime Act.

Her husband, fitness influencer and businessman Atip Anantawan, who also faced a warrant, surrendered to police.

The investigation centres around allegations made that donations to her Do Good Organisation Foundation were used for non-charitable activities like buying multiple properties, including a pool villa in Phuket.

The couple also faces mounting public anger over allegations that relief goods were abandoned in a warehouse instead of being distributed to victims of floods.

Earlier this week, reporters visited two sites packed with bottled water, soap, clothing and bedding.



Videos that Panadda shared on Instagram, where she has over 2 million followers, show her braving murky floodwaters as her team delivered aid to victims.

Pictures also show her consoling people who had lost their livelihood in the disaster in Thailand.

“I came to cheer up. I visited Bang Ban area for seven years. Many people have left. Many people still have to fight,” she wrote in the caption.



Dr Khongkwan Fujinirun is one of the donors who have openly criticised Panadda.

He filed a police complaint after having donated around £2,220 to her foundation, the South China Morning Post reported.

“We’re talking about a thief dressed up as a saint, someone who betrayed the faith of people across the whole country,” he said.

“The victims are all the Thai people who transferred money to donate.”

Authorities are now examining the couple’s financial transactions and all assets, and have searched four locations linked to the case.

News.title: Should e-bikes be banned? Have your say after government announces clampdown
News.content:
Should e-bikes be banned? Have your say after government announces clampdown

A nationwide clampdown on 'nuisance' E-bikes will see fines handed out irresponsible riders and new penalties on firms who fail to stop pile-ups blocking pavements

View Image Mirror readers are debating what the government should do about E-bikes (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

Ministers are set to bring in new rules on E-bikes in a bid to stamp out irresponsible riding.

‌



‌



Plans outlined in a new consultation by the Department for Transport would introduce fines on cyclists who ride on pavements, take to the pedals while drunk, or jump red lights.

‌



Meanwhile, companies that offer the hire bikes will be required to limit fleet sizes and ensure bays are being used appropriately to eliminate "nuisance" parking on footpaths.

‌



Another proposal would bring in mandatory insurance, meaning people can claim compensation if they’re hit by someone on a shared cycle.

The government is also consulting on whether regional mayors should have extra powers, including setting fees and requiring operators to share data.

‌



Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "E-bikes can make getting around that bit easier, but when they block pavements or are used irresponsibly, they can be a real frustration.

"I want to sort that by giving communities more control over where they are parked and making sure companies and riders play by the rules.

‌



"While making the big, long-term changes to make transport better and more affordable for people across the country, this is a small but important everyday fix to make our streets safer."

It follows warnings from charities that pavements in Britain's towns and cities are being clogged by 'street clutter', causing huge problems for people with mobility issues and parents with prams.

‌



Tanya Braun, Director of External Affairs at Living Streets, said: "Our pavements are for people and should be safe and accessible for everyone to use.

"Discarded e-bikes obstruct our pavements, which is dangerous for everyone but especially for wheelchair users, those who are blind or partially sighted or families with young children.

‌



"This can prevent people from enjoying the many health and social benefits of walking and wheeling."

Currently, rules on E-bikes are set by local councils, though these vary widely by area and are not always enforced.

‌



Lime and Forest - two of the largest E-bike hire firms - said they welcomed the move towards consistent national standards.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said: "Shared e-bike schemes have revolutionised the way people travel around our towns and cities. They are easy to use, get us active and help reduce emissions, but we need to make sure they work with the communities where they operate.

Article continues below

"That’s why we are taking decisive action to give local leaders the power to stop nuisance parking, tackle antisocial behaviour and make journeys safer."

News.title: Double killer serving life for two murders jailed for a further 22 years over string of sex attacks

Double killer serving life for two murders jailed for a further 22 years over string of sex attacks

Former Royal Navy petty officer Allan Grimson - jailed for the brutal murders of Nicholas Wright, 18, and Sion Jenkins, 20 - was found guilty of sexually assaulting four males including a 14-year-old boy in the 1990s

Sentencing Grimson - who smirked in the dock - Judge Paul Dugdale said: "It won't surprise anyone to know I have made a finding of dangerousness." He explained: "I have assessed you remain dangerous as defined by section 308 of the Sentencing Act in that you still pose a significant risk to members of the general public of serious harm.

‌

"This was clearly evident in the late 1990s and its consequences so extreme that you will always pose such an underlying risk to the public. It's difficult to envisage anyone who would not assess you as dangerous having heard the comments you made in the interviews in 2000 and what nearly happened to these men.

"It's extremely difficult for any court to take the risk you no longer pose a danger to the public given the clear comments you made and past offending." He added: "You won't be released on life licence until the parole board consider it safe for you to do so and if they do not do so, you will remain in custody for life."

‌



The judge explained that Grimson would not eligible for parole until he had served 13 years of this sentence, which would be three months before his 80th birthday. Grimson was also found guilty of 11 counts of indecent assault, one count of rape and one count of taking indecent photographs of a child.

The prosecution said that this brought Grimson, a “big, powerful man” into contact with a lot of young men in their late teens.

News.title: '40 minutes' on special mattress could 'clear Alzheimer’s plaques from brain'
News.content:
'40 minutes' on special mattress could 'clear Alzheimer’s plaques from brain'

Experts have said it's like the brain is taking out its own trash

View 2 Images A report suggests it could "clear" your brain of "Alzheimer's plaques" (Image: Getty | Franziska & Tom Werner)

Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia in the UK. There are many risk factors associated with it, and while the exact cause of the disease is not yet fully understood, a 40-minute habit could help "clear" your brain of "Alzheimer's plaques."

‌



‌



The Scientific Report shared a study that was published on November 3, 2026, explaining "40 minutes on a vibrating mattress triggers the body to clear Alzheimer's plaques from the brain". But the study didn't just use a mattress; participants also took a pill.

‌



It explains that a team at the University of Oulu in Finland tested it on 29 dementia-free adults. During the test, a nitric oxide pill was placed under the tongue, then the adults spent 40 minutes on a gently vibrating mattress, with a second pill halfway through.

‌



It explains: "Afterwards, blood levels of beta-amyloid 42 jumped 35% on average. That’s the sticky protein behind Alzheimer’s plaques."

‌



The study's lead researcher, Vesa Kiviniemi, believes the glymphatic system, the brain’s built-in waste network, was flushing it out into the blood. Brain scans showed fluid moving harder through those channels, The Scientific Report shared.

In separate analysis, New Scientist reports that "additional experiments by Kiviniemi and his colleagues tested either only the mattress vibrations or only the nitric oxide pills on the same participants, at least a week before or after they underwent the combined approach. Based on brain scans, these solo interventions seemed to have less than half the effect on the glymphatic system than when they were combined."

‌



View 2 Images Researchers hope to conduct similar trials soon (Image: Getty)

Now, researchers hope to trial the combined approach in 60 people with mild cognitive impairment or Alzheimer’s disease next year. This could produce results in the following two years.

Article continues below

New Scientist adds that if this is a success, researchers "hope to conduct a trial where a similar group of people has the treatment regularly for several months, rather than as a one-off intervention. This should be long enough to detect any improvements in cognitive abilities, like memory and problem-solving, says Kiviniemi."

Tuunanen, J., Hautamäki, K., Väyrynen, T. et al. Vasomechanic treatment is associated with increased efflux of human brain proteins. Nat Commun 17, 11164 (2026). https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78894-y https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78894-y

News.title: King Charles' aides reflect on 'challenging and exhausting' Caribbean tour
News.content:
King Charles' aides reflect on 'challenging and exhausting' Caribbean tour

The monarch has wrapped up a nine-day trip to the island nations, in which he showcased his soft diplomatic powers

The King's lasting legacy in the Caribbean

Senior aides to King Charles have reflected on his nine-day Caribbean tour, which saw the monarch undertake numerous engagements across the Bahamas, Guyana, and Antigua and Barbuda, where he concluded his trip with an address at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting.

‌



‌



Charles was solo for most of the trip, although was joined by Queen Camilla in Antigua. As the trip drew to a close, Buckingham Palace was quick to label the visit a success, although the jam-packed schedule was no doubt a tall order for the King.

‌



One palace aide said when talking about the challenges of the tour: "This has been a complex visit. It's been challenging. It's been exhausting.

‌



Prince William reveals his pint of choice in pub as he shares personal insights READ MORE :

Disgraced Andrew pocketed up to £2k a month subletting Royal Lodge cottages READ MORE :

View 2 Images King Charles spent nine days in the Caribbean (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

“It's been a hot tour across nine days, across three countries… But the takeaway is that it's been very successful, and I think the King has demonstrated his statecraft both by word and deed.”

‌



The aide praised the King’s resilience throughout the trip, where temperatures were regularly in the high 30s, as they said: said: “I think probably the best response to that is a picture of a man about to turn 78 wangling the cowbells as he jives down the street in nearly 40-degree heat.

“When the engagement finished, I’d get in the car next to him and say ‘Crikey, I'm hot’. He says, ‘Oh, never mind’. So no, he copes. I mean, frankly, he copes better with it than I do, and I'm younger than him.”

‌



View 2 Images Palace aides said it was a 'complex' tour (Image: Ben Stansall/Press Association)

Buckingham Palace also said the King, despite turning 78 in just over a week, and operating in sweltering 40 degree heat last week in Guyana, "enjoys the reaction he gets from people in the doing" of the job, and was committed to carrying on despite his continued treatment for cancer since 2024.

‌



The palace aides added that Charles is being deployed as a "secret weapon" by the government to head into "politically charged situations" around the world.

Buckingham Palace said the King's reign, now into its fifth year, was being shaped by a "very clear pattern emerging of the government asking the king to head into quite politically charged situations, quite challenging situations."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

They said: "The King is not just King for the easy parts of the job, but the tough parts of the job, too. In fact, that's probably the part of the job that he relishes most....where there have been some complex political issues at play, that is what he lives and breathes for.”

‌



As the trip came to a close, the King said in a statement: “As my wife and I depart the Caribbean, we would like to extend our heartfelt thanks to all the people of The Bahamas, Guyana, and Antigua and Barbuda for the warmth of their welcome and the many kindnesses they have shown us throughout this tour.

After three nations, four speeches, nine days, over 40 different engagements and countless hands shaken in firm friendship, I return home with so many treasured memories…and one slightly damp suit! Charles R.”

News.title: Kate Middleton reveals 'healing' connection with nature during emotional secret visit
News.content:
Kate Middleton reveals 'healing' connection with nature during emotional secret visit

It has emerged that the Princess of Wales visited those involved with the Dose of Nature charity, which helps improve wellbeing through clinical psychology as well as connecting with the natural world

View 5 Images The Princess of Wales on a visit to Dose of Nature in Kew (Image: Laura Lewis / Kensington Palace)

The Princess of Wales shared how she found a ‘healing’ connection with nature during an under-the-radar visit.

‌



‌



Kate spoke about her experiences as she chatted to those from Dose of Nature - a charity that helps improve wellbeing through a combination of clinical psychology and connection with the natural world. The princess has long been interested in how nature can support healthier, happier lives and previously said she used the natural world as a sanctuary during her recovery from cancer.

‌



In a new video and pictures released by Kensington Palace, Kate met those involved with the charity last month, including its founder Dr Alison Green and clinical lead Dr Georgina Gould, to learn more about the Kew-based organisation's approach to mental health support.

‌



View 5 Images The princess has long advocated the benefits of nature (Image: Laura Lewis / Kensington Palace)

Prince William lines up Take That for historic performance at Earthshot Prize Awards READ MORE :

During her visit, the princess dressed casually in jeans and a Barbour jacket, chatted to Tom, a former participant in the programme who now works for the charity and volunteers as a Nature Guide himself.

He told Kate about the role Dose of Nature had played in his own recovery, helping him build confidence, resilience and a stronger sense of connection to the natural world.

‌



In turn, she told him: “Our journey has been very very different, but it’s so wonderful to hear how your nature connection and how it’s been so healing for you, and I felt the same.

View 5 Images Kate with Dose of Nature founder Dr Alison Green and clinical lead Dr Georgina Gould (Image: Laura Lewis / Kensington Palace)

‌



“The fact that you’re able to provide that to so many other people in this community; that sense of purpose and meaning, and belonging, through that experience, I think is something that has got the longevity and the sustainability of feeling like, almost without knowing what’s to come, without having the control in your life of knowing what the future might hold, the fact that you feel that you can cope with things, because you feel that interconnection, I think that makes it holistic in a very true essence.”

She also dropped in on the charity’s weekly ‘Art in Nature’ session, where participants use the natural environment for inspiration.

‌



View 5 Images Dose of Nature works with NHS and GP referrals to support those experiencing a range of mental health challenges (Image: Laura Lewis / Kensington Palace)

Founded in 2018, Dose of Nature works with NHS and GP referrals to support those experiencing a range of mental health challenges through its clinically led ‘Nature Prescription’ programme.

‌



The charity uses nature as a tool for wellbeing, combining a psychology-led approach, one-to-one guidance from volunteer Nature Guides and nature immersion to help people reconnect with nature, improve their wellbeing and build lasting resilience.

View 5 Images The princess has long championed the benefits of experiencing nature, especially during her cancer journey (Image: Laura Lewis / Kensington Palace)

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

Last year alone, the charity delivered 547 Nature Prescriptions through its hubs in the Boroughs of Richmond and Guildford, supporting people experiencing a wide range of mental health challenges.

Article continues below

The princess has long championed the benefits of experiencing nature, especially during her cancer journey, and wrote in a recent essay: “By spending time in nature or being creative, we can nurture the very skills and emotions that cannot be digitised: awareness, empathy, humility, and above all, love.”

News.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel collision 'considering walking away from football'
News.content:
Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel collision 'considering walking away from football'

As the football world continues to mourn the death of Jesus de Miguel, the goalkeeper who he collided with is reportedly considering leaving football

View 3 Images Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono collided with FC Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel (Image: AP)

The goalkeeper who collided with Jesus de Miguel before the striker's death is now considering quitting football, according to reports. Jesus Owono was in goal for Andorra FC when he ran into De Miguel as he tried to clear the ball on Monday November 2nd.

‌



‌



The Tenerife forward was left on the floor after the challenge and passed away from "accidental chest trauma" the following morning while in hospital. Owono, who was sent off for the challenge, has been left devastated after the tragic collision and is now receiving psychological help from his team.

‌



He recently issued his own statement in reaction to the horrific tragedy. Now it's emerged he is considering quitting football for good.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

According to Mundo Deportivo, he may walk away from the game in the wake of the incident. Ana Maye, a close friend to Owono and a general coordinator of the Equatorial Guinea men's national team, said to the Spanish outlet: "No matter how much we tell him, he's deeply saddened.

"He's very affected, especially for Jesús Miguel's one-and-a-half-year-old son and for his widow. He doesn't know how to handle all of this."

‌



On the day after De Miguel passed away, Owono took to social media and wrote: "These are the most difficult days of my life. I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to process what has happened.

View 3 Images Jesus de Miguel with (right to left) his sister, girlfriend, daughter, mother and father (Image: Instagram/@martitamig)

‌



"I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

"But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

‌



De Miguel's funeral took place in his hometown of Navahermosa, where hundreds of mourners, including his family and several high-ranking Spanish football officials paid their respects.

View 3 Images Jesus de Miguel's funeral took place in his hometown (Image: AFP or licensors)

‌



While De Miguel's friends and family are still grieving, Owono is also struggling to come to terms with what happened. Maye has also claimed the goalkeeper's family have also been receiving abuse on social media and in person.

She added: "They're calling Jesús's brother a murderer. He's being heckled by his teammates, and even some parents are insulting him.

Article continues below

"It's very hard. His sister, who studies at the University of Valencia, is also suffering because of what's happening. They don't deserve this."

News.title: Major warning for anyone thinking of starting weight loss injections in UK
News.content:
Major warning for anyone thinking of starting weight loss injections in UK

People who may be keen to try the injections, if lifestyle and diet changes have not helped with weight loss, are being issued a warning

View 2 Images Important factors to consider if you are weighing up your options (stock image) (Image: Getty)

Anyone considering starting weight-loss injections has been issued an important warning. The alert comes as many people may be swayed to avoid high costs and long NHS waiting times by opting for cheaper weight-loss jabs found online.

‌



‌



However, a massive underground market for fake weight-loss injections is putting people across the UK at severe risk. High private prescription costs, long NHS waitlists, and strict eligibility rules have led many buyers toward unverified, cheap alternatives sold on social media and dodgy websites.

‌



Recent raids highlight the scale of the threat. In Birmingham, the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) and West Midlands Police seized over 12,000 counterfeit weight-loss pens from an industrial unit. Officials warn that these illegal products have never been tested for safety or quality. Some packages even contained retatrutide, which is a drug not licensed anywhere in the UK.

‌



Dr Amar Ahmed, GP partner at Wilmslow Health Centre, recently issued a fresh warning to anyone considering taking weight loss injections - especially if they are thinking of buying medication not from a pharmacy. In a video on Facebook, he said: "If your weight loss jab came from anywhere other than a pharmacy, can I have 30 seconds of your time?

"On October 14, the Medicines Regulator, that's the MHRA, went into an industrial unit in Birmingham with the West Midlands Police and it came out with over 12,000 counterfeit weight loss pens. And that's from the MHRA's own statement, which they put out the next day. Now, counterfeit doesn't just mean it's a bit weak.

‌



"It actually means nobody knows what's in it. The MHRA say these haven't been checked for safety, for quality, or for whether they do anything at all. So if you take it, you'd be injecting a complete unknown. And one of the two drugs that they named, Ritatritide, isn't licensed in the UK at all.

"So if you've bought something with that name on it, it can't have come through a proper route because there isn't one. So here's who this is for and who it isn't. If your medicine came from a pharmacy on a prescription, this isn't about you.

‌



"Carry on as you are. If it came off a website or a messaging app or someone at the gym, then please don't take the next dose until you've spoken to a pharmacist. Not next week, as soon as possible. And certainly before you take any more of it."

Legitimate weight-loss injections, such as Wegovy and Mounjaro, are prescription-only medicines. They are strictly intended for adults living with obesity or weight-related health conditions, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and regular exercise. However, high demand and supply shortages have opened the door for illegal sellers.

‌



View 2 Images Check you are buying from a legitimate source that works with licensed UK medical professionals (stock image) (Image: Getty)

Surveys reveal that an alarming number of adults are turning to unregulated channels. An Ipsos poll showed nearly one in 10 UK adults (9%) would buy weight-loss jabs via social media if they couldn't get a prescription. Even worse, a survey of 2,000 GLP-1 users by MedExpress found that over 20% had already bought unverified jabs, with adults aged 25 to 34 being the most vulnerable.

‌



Financial losses are also mounting. Santander UK reported that fraud losses from fake weight-loss jab scams doubled year-over-year, with victims losing an average of £120 as they sought cheaper deals.

Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings

‌



Why are some people taking the risk?

Several key factors drive people away from legitimate healthcare providers:

High private prescription costs

NHS delays and strict rules

Social media hype

‌



Private treatments can cost up to £2,500 a year. In one report, 51% of users cited cost as the primary reason for stopping treatment, creating a huge market for cheap fakes.

Limited NHS capacity leaves millions unable to access treatment through the public healthcare system, pushing frustrated patients online. Unregulated sellers use platforms like TikTok, Instagram, and WhatsApp, using misleading photos and code words like "for research purposes only" to bypass moderation.

‌



What are the dangers of fake injections?

Injecting an unapproved or fake drug poses life-threatening health risks. Authorities have uncovered fake injectables containing harmful bacteria, undeclared chemicals, and even dangerous substances like cement and arsenic.

‌



Many fake pens contain mislabelled insulin instead of weight-loss medication. Injecting high doses of insulin causes rapid blood sugar drops, resulting in severe hypoglycemic shock, coma, or death.

Nearly 90% of reported adverse reactions to fake semaglutide are classified as serious, including severe vomiting, acute pancreatitis, and dehydration.

‌



How to spot fake products and stay safe

Before buying any weight-loss medication, experts urge people to keep these vital safety rules in mind:

Check the source

Require a prescription

Inspect the packaging

‌



Legitimate prescription drugs are never sold directly on social media or general shopping marketplaces. Always check that an online provider is registered on the General Pharmaceutical Council (GPhC) register.

If a site offers jabs without a clinical consultation or BMI verification, it is illegal and likely fake. Real medications use proper branded pens. Be suspicious of loose syringes, unlabelled powders, poor printing, or cloudy liquid.

Article continues below

If your medication was dispensed by a licensed pharmacy with a prescription, you can safely continue your treatment. However, if you bought a jab online or through social media, stop taking it immediately and consult a GP or pharmacist.

News.title: WW2 veteran reaches the age of 107 by staying happy - and eating chocolate biscuits
News.content:
WW2 veteran reaches the age of 107 by staying happy - and eating chocolate biscuits

Harold Hodgson, a WWII veteran who served with the RAF ground staff, turns 107 tomorrow at Grange Care Home in Darlington, Co Durham

View 4 Images Harold Hodgson will turn 107 on Saturday (Image: Grange Care Home Darlington)

One of Britain's oldest men is about to turn 107 thanks to staying happy, fit - and McVitie chocolate biscuits. Harold Hodgson is a WWII veteran who served with the RAF. He joined up aged 22 and spent five years as ground staff, serving in Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Norfolk.

‌



He turns 107 on Saturday at the Grange Care Home in Darlington, Co Durham, where staff have organised a party with 107 cards from local well-wishers. His family paid tribute to his 'zest for life'. Daughter Christine Gibbon, 73, told how he loved the great outdoors. Harold said he owed so much to the "women in his life".

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 4 Images Harold Hodgson is about to turn 107

His mum Mary, was a farmer's daughter and 'amazing cook.' His late wife Sylvia, who died 10 years ago aged 95, travelled around the UK with him, alongside Christine, 73, and her sister Margaret, 77.

"I loved Sylvia with all my heart," said Harold, who has three grandchildren, and four great-grandchildren. "We used to get in my car and travel through the whole of England. We loved walking, swimming, and exploring. Keeping fit is key." He joked: "I am happy-go-lucky; being happy in life."

View 4 Images Harold in his RAF days when he served in WWII.

Christine said her dad loved a morning coffee 'and 'a McVitie's chocolate biscuit' as a treat. "He has been a really good hiker all his life," she said.

"He kept fit, looked after himself and took us away on holiday as kids. He served as a bricklayer for the RAF so he did not see active service in WWII. "He has a good sense of humour and we have always had a good laugh with him. He is one of the oldest people in the UK now. I am pretty sure he is now the oldest man in the North East."

View 4 Images Proud dad: Harold with his two daughters Christine and Margaret (Image: Family photo)

Family holidays were in Scarborough, Skegness and Great Yarmouth and Harold was a regular churchgoer. He played badminton and swam to keep fit.

Born in Darlington on November 7, 1919, he stayed there throughout his long life, apart from his time serving in the RAF in Belgium, France, Germany, the Netherlands and Norfolk. To celebrate his birthday, The Grange is hosting a special party with Harold's family, friends and fellow residents Representatives of the Royal British Legion are expected to attend.

They will be there alongside the Mayoress of Darlington Coun Helen Brumbie. The home has encouraged the local community to send Harold 107 birthday cards to mark his milestone.

A spokesman said that he remains a "sociable character". He has a wonderful sense of humour," he added. He affectionately describes The Grange as "a wonderful hotel".

The oldest known living man in the United Kingdom is Hugh Munro Kerr, born on October 9, 1915, who is currently 111 years old and lives in Paisley, Renfrewshire, Scotland.

News.title: Met chief says he wouldn't be surprised if more allegations made about Brand after rape conviction
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has also spoken about the case, defending the Labour Party's previous association with Brand, saying "it's not always the case that people know everything about people in public life".

Some within the party attempted to court Brand's support more than a decade ago, before police began investigating him, but Burnham told the BBC: "All I can say is I had no idea of the full extent of what he was doing or what he went on to do."

Speaking to the BBC on Friday, Sir Mark said that he "wouldn't be surprised if more people came forward" about Brand and said there were "two ongoing rape investigations" into him.

Brand has already been interviewed under caution in relation to those allegations.

In his interview Sir Mark praised the "bravery" of the women who came forward to tell "their story" to the police and during the trial.

"That's a real challenge for anyone having gone through something so ghastly and you have to admire them."

The head of the Met also said that whilst Brand's case "may look different because it's about celebrity, the majority of sex offending is about people abusing power", adding that victims will be believed.

"We will do everything we can to bring to justice the powerful person who are responsible for probably the most ghastly moment in your life.", he said.

It was put to Sir Mark during an interview with BBC Radio 4's Today programme that Brand's defence barrister "told jurors none of the complainants had in his words 'resisted, screamed or even tried to leave'".

Sir Mark said that what he heard reported from the trial was "very close to victim blaming".

Asked whether he would support the Victim's Commissioner's call for a legal duty in the Courts and Tribunals Bill that would require judges to direct juries on rape myths and misconceptions in every rape trial.

He said he would "strongly support" that call, adding: "It shouldn't be possible for inaccurate statements to be made to a jury to suggest that because a rape victim didn't behave in one way that somehow undermines their case."

Brand was refused bail following his conviction on Thursday and will now spend the weekend in custody before he is due to return to the same court on Monday for sentencing.

He is expected to face a substantial prison sentence.

Once the trial was over, it was reported that Brand is also facing further rape allegations made by two women and has already been questioned by officers in relation to the complaints. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation "remains ongoing".

Details in legal documents from a hearing at London's Southwark Crown Court before Brand's criminal trial began suggest that one of the women was 16 years old at the time and featured in a Channel 4 documentary.

During the trial, Brand faced allegations from six women spanning the decade between 1999 and 2009, when he rose to fame as one of Britain's most high-profile entertainers.

The women came to court to reveal how Brand used his immense fame to force them into sexual activity.

The judge, Mr Justice Bennathan, told Brand to expect "a significant custodial term" after the verdicts were delivered.

News.title: Katherine Ryan says she feels 'grief and relief' after Russell Brand conviction
News.content:

Details in legal documents from a hearing at London's Southwark Crown Court before Brand's criminal trial began suggest that one of the women was 16 years old at the time and featured in a Channel 4 documentary.

None of the women who featured in the media investigation were the complainants from Brand's criminal trial.

During a pre-trial hearing in October Brand tried unsuccessfully to have his criminal case thrown out.

His lawyers argued that the actor and entertainer couldn't receive a fair trial because of the publicity following the Dispatches programme.

Prosecutors opposed Brand's application to have his case stopped.

It was during that hearing that the prosecution said one of the complaints made in the documentary was being investigated.

Riel Karmy-Jones KC said: "Of the four women in the Ch4 documentary, two concern events outside the jurisdiction.

"One did not disclose any offence. The other is being investigated.

"There had been some interaction in 2018, she did not report the matter until 2024, after the documentary was aired."

In documents submitted to the court for the hearing prosecutors also said it was "plainly incorrect" to say there had been a decision not to investigate.

"The outstanding charges against RB in respect of 'Alice' from Dispatches demonstrate that there has been no such decision â rather that the police will and have responded appropriately once a formal allegation is made."

The head of the Metropolitan Police has said he "wouldn't be surprised" if more people came forward to make allegations about Russell Brand.

Sir Mark Rowley also told BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Friday that what he heard reported from Brand's trial at Southwark Crown Court came very close to "victim blaming".
