And although they suffered a 2-1 loss to City at the weekend, the independent side proved they are capable of competing with the elite.

With Putellas leading as captain, the ceiling continues to get higher.

Sports.title: Newcastle considering transfer raid on fierce rivals Middlesbrough for goal machine Will Lankshear
Sports.content:
Next

NEWCASTLE United are monitoring the progress of Middlesbrough goal machine Will Lankshear who has taken the Championship by storm.

His remarkable start to the campaign is the best by a Boro player at this stage of a season since club legend George Camsell in 1926, underlining why his performances are attracting Premier League attention.



But plans to update their dossier on the 21-year-old striker signed from Spurs in the summer for a bargain £10 million were foiled on Wednesday night.

Lankshear was a prolific goalscorer in Tottenham’s academy and was named Premier League 2 Player of the Season in 2023-24.



He went on to make six senior appearances for Spurs, scoring his only first-team goal against Galatasaray in the Europa League.

The Toon were due to watch Lankshear who has struck 13 goals in 13 Championship games at Wrexham.



But the England Under 21 star who has also impressed Three Lions head coach Thomas Tuchel was pulled out of the game at the 11th hour through injury.

Lankshear has made a stunning leap forward since spending last season on loan at Oxford United, where he scored 11 Championship goals in 43 appearances.

He has already eclipsed that tally in just 13 league games for Boro.

Without him Boro lost 2-0, failing to score in the Championship for the first time this season, and seeing their lead at the top of the table cut to one point.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The defeat also ended Middlesbrough’s 11-match unbeaten league run, with Wrexham’s George Thomason and Oli Rathbone striking in the final 20 minutes to stun the promotion favourites.

Newcastle’s recruitment since selling Alexander Isak to Liverpool for a British record £125 million has come under scrutiny with Nick Woltemade (£75 million), Yoane Wissa (£55 million) and Matias Fernandez-Pardo (£51 million) all failing to make an impact.

Now the answer to their goals dilemma could be just down the road on Teesside where Lankshear has blossomed.

And any potential deal would carry extra spice given the fierce North-East rivalry between Newcastle and Middlesbrough, with Boro desperate to return to the Premier League for the first time since their relegation in 2017.

It’s hard to see who is more desperate to see him return from Injury with Boro head coach Kim Hellberg admitting: “Any team would miss a player who has scored 13 goals in 13 games. It’s the same for every team in the world.”

Sports.title: Captaincy Options for Gameweek 10: In-form Evanilson rivalling default Erling Haaland
Sports.content:
Next

DREAM TEAM bosses must remember to select a captain for Gameweek 10 before today’s 6:30pm deadline.

For many, Erling Haaland (£9.1m) remains the default option as long as he’s available and with good reason.

Manchester City’s No9 is the game’s top performer by a wide a margin having amassed 137 points via 14 goals.



This weekend, he will be unleashed upon 19th-placed Nottingham Forest, certainly not a match-up to fear.



However, some gaffers will be tempted to take on the Norwegian poacher as there are some strong alternatives.

Oliver Glasner’s side are struggling but their problem is an inefficient attack whereas their underlying defensive numbers are actually rather good — Forest have conceded the fewest shots in the top flight this season.

Obviously, Haaland is perfectly capable of a goal (or two, three) in any fixture but it will be interesting to see how many of the top Dream Team managers stick the armband on somebody else.



Take Evanilson (£4.4m) for example.

Bournemouth’s No9 has banked 73 points across the last four Gameweeks via six goals and three assists.

This Haaland-esque spree has put him firmly in the spotlight and who would bet against him extending his fine form when the Cherries travel to Ipswich on Sunday?

Only Crystal Palace have conceded more league goals than the Tractor Boys this season.



Speaking of the Eagles, they really are in a pickle.

Daichi Kamada’s (£3.4m) stoppage-time equaliser against Hoffenheim gave the Selhurst Park faithful something to cheer on Thursday night but fans will be fearing another battering at the hands of Liverpool this weekend.

Alexander Isak (£6.5m) will fancy his chances of adding to his tally of seven goals when he’s let loose against the league’s worst defence.

The Swedish striker is a viable captaincy selection for sure.



Elsewhere, backers of Cole Palmer (£5.3m) and Morgan Rogers (£5.5m) will be expecting big things when Chelsea rock up at the Stadium of Light to face a Sunderland side sat at the bottom of the table.

The former averages 8.7 points-per-game in 2026/27, only Haaland boasts a better average among assets to have played at least three games.

Finally, Arsenal at home to Hull is another fixture that leaps out of the schedule.

Although it’s not all that easy to identify a standout captain among the Gunners’ ranks.

Gabriel (£5.7m) is his side’s top performer with 88 points to his name and has a high chance of adding another clean sheet to his collection but if he doesn’t have all that much defending to do then some gaffers may be tad underwhelmed by a seven-point haul doubled to 14 with the armband.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Brazilian does offer a threat from a set pieces but relying on a goal from a centre-back, even as one as potent in the air as Gabriel, is a low-percentage play.

In conclusion, stick with Haaland to play it safe or take a punt on Evanilson, Isak, Palmer or Rogers if you want to go against the grain this weekend.

Sports.title: Jude and Jobe Bellingham join elite list of brothers to play together for England
Sports.content:
Next

JUDE and Jobe Bellingham could become the first brothers to play together for England in almost 20 YEARS after Thomas Tuchel handed the younger sibling his maiden call-up.

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder, 21, has been named alongside Real Madrid superstar Jude, 23, for the Three Lions’ Nations League clashes against Croatia and Spain.



Jobe has earned his opportunity following an impressive turnaround in Germany after initially struggling to establish himself following his £28million move from Sunderland in 2025.

He has started six of Dortmund’s eight Bundesliga matches this season, providing two assists, and was unfortunate to have a goal ruled out against Bayern Munich last weekend.



His older brother, meanwhile, is already one of England‘s most important players, having won 60 senior caps and scored 14 goals since making his debut aged just 17 in 2020.

And the pair could now follow in the footsteps of some of English football’s most famous siblings.

The last brothers to actually share the pitch for England were Gary and Phil Neville, who both featured in a 1-0 friendly defeat against Spain at Old Trafford in February 2007 – more than 19 years ago.

Gary made his senior international debut in 1995 under Terry Venables, with younger brother Phil following him into the Three Lions set-up the following year.

Both had emerged through Manchester United’s famous Class of ’92 academy generation.

The elder Neville went on to make 85 appearances for his country, becoming England’s established right-back and representing the Three Lions at three European Championships and two World Cups.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Phil earned 59 caps and was capable of operating in defence or midfield.

But the Nevilles were not the most recent brothers to have both represented England, with Nathaniel and Trevoh Chalobah joining that exclusive club just last year.

They became the 21st paor of brothers winning senior England caps when Tuchel handed Trevoh his debut against Senegal in June 2025.

His older brother Nathaniel had made his solitary England appearance almost seven years earlier, coming on during a famous 3-2 Nations League victory over Spain in Seville in October 2018.

And perhaps the most famous brothers ever to represent the Three Lions were Sir Bobby and Jack Charlton, who achieved something no other English siblings have managed – winning the World Cup together.



Bobby made his England debut in 1958 and developed into one of the greatest players in the country’s history, winning 106 caps and scoring 49 goals.

The Manchester United legend was also crowned European Footballer of the Year after helping England lift the World Cup in 1966.

Older brother Jack had to wait until 1965 to make his international bow, aged 29, but quickly established himself as an important member of Sir Alf Ramsey’s side.

The Leeds United defender earned 35 caps and lined up alongside Bobby as England defeated West Germany 4-2 in the Wembley final.

The Bellinghams are now hoping to write their own chapter of England’s family history, although they are not the only famous footballing siblings to represent the country.



Chelsea stars Reece and Lauren James have both played for England’s senior teams, with Lauren making her Lionesses debut in September 2022 – becoming the first brother-and-sister combination to achieve the feat in the modern era.

Sports.title: ‘Thomas Tuchel is not serious’ – Fans baffled by second Chelsea star’s snub from England squad after Cole Palmer omitted
Sports.content:
Next

COLE PALMER has been snubbed by England despite his promising start to the season.

But it is a second Chelsea omission that has got some Blues fans even more riled up.



Thomas Tuchel selected Trent Alexander-Arnold and Djed Spence at right-back, as well as a trio of central defenders – Ezri Konsa, Jarell Quansah and Ben White – who can also play in the position.

That left no room for the in-form Josh Acheampong, who has played more minutes than Alexander-Arnold and White so far this campaign, and looked mightily impressive in the process.



Acheampong, 20, has played primarily as the right-sided centre-back in Xabi Alonso‘s back-three.

The youngster has started six of Chelsea’s nine Premier League games, coming on as a sub in two more.



And his performances have been so convincing that many Chelsea fans flocked to social media to rant about Tuchel overlooking him.

One wrote on X: “I’m surprised Tuchel didn’t invite Acheampong despite his form.”

Another put: “Bench-warmer Trent over Acheampong is diabolical from Tuchel.”

A third added: “Quansah, Spence, Trent and White in but no Josh Acheampong lol Tuchel is sabotaging England.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And a fourth chimed in with: “Trent over Acheampong? Tuchel is not serious.”

The England boss gave Jobe Bellingham and Josh King their first senior call-ups ahead of Nations League meetings with Croatia and Spain.

Palmer was one of the bigger names left out, along with Kobbie Mainoo and Phil Foden.



Tuchel admitted Palmer “missed too many chances to impress” after he pulled out of September’s squad due to a minor injury.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reveals why Cole Palmer was left out of England squad despite Chelsea confirming he’s 100 per cent fit
Sports.content:
Next

COLE PALMER was snubbed by Thomas Tuchel despite England being told he was ready to play.

Three Lions medics made checks on Palmer’s fitness with his club Chelsea after the playmaker withdrew from the last England camp due to injury.



Palmer, 24, was left out of the World Cup squad last summer having struggled with a groin injury all season.

Tuchel said he had been told the former Manchester City man was playing with discomfort and pain after he withdrew from the October camp, and added his frustration that Palmer missed too many opportunities with the national team.



However, ahead of Tuchel selecting his squad for games against Spain and Croatia this month, Chelsea informed England that he was 100 per cent fit and ready to play if called upon.

Despite that Palmer was omitted, with Fulham‘s Josh King and Borussia Dortmund‘s Jobe Bellingham called up for the first time instead.



Asked about Palmer’s omission, Tuchel said: “It’s enough number 10s and we stick to the guys from the last camp and the impact of all of them was immense.

“That is why we stick with the offensive players. We have Josh King but I want to see him on both wings. He can cover all eventualities as Josh King can play all four positions.”

Tuchel added: “Everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception. It counts when you are in camp and he missed too many chances to impress.

“It is not personal and we will never assume Cole is not in the mindset to be desperate to play for his country but the competition is on.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Having spent the summer on holiday and recovering from his injury problems from last season, many expected Palmer to be fired up to prove Tuchel wrong.

However, speaking on Chelsea’s pre-season tour in Australia, the midfielder said he was more focused on Chelsea and was “not too bothered” about his England prospects.

Palmer has scored twice for England, including his goal from the bench in the Euro 2024 final defeat to Spain.

Only three of his caps have come under ex-Blues boss Tuchel, with his last appearance for his country coming in a 1-0 defeat to Japan in March.

Sports.title: 'It's not personal' - Tuchel explains Palmer exclusion
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has insisted Cole Palmer's absence from the England squad isn't "personal" - but sent out an emphatic statement with the Chelsea star's exclusion.

Palmer is in form and a check from the England medical staff with Chelsea confirmed he is fit and ready to play this weekend. But Tuchel has prioritised players who were available and delivered in the previous international break.

Tuchel made headlines in September when he said Palmer misses too many opportunities to impress him, following the attacker's withdrawal due to injury.

During Tuchel's tenure Palmer has been unavailable for selection because of injury three times and has withdrawn from a further two squads. For the November Nations League games with Croatia and Spain, the England boss is putting his trust in the players who have shown him up close what they can do.

"It's always the ones who are in camp, the ones who don't withdraw," Tuchel said. "The ones who walk the talk, and come to camp and show it matters and put the quality in. That's what we will always reward.

"It matters what you do in camp. The last camp was an excellent one, so the trust and belief is on the players who were there."

Image: Cole Palmer ranks highly across attacking stats for his performances for Chelsea in the Premier League so far this season

Among No 10 options, Jude Bellingham, Morgan Gibbs-White, Eberechi Eze and Morgan Rogers retain their places from the previous round of internationals, when England beat Croatia and Czech Republic twice and narrowly lost to world champions Spain. Nineteen-year-old Josh King, who was part of the pre-World Cup training group, is included too.

"It's enough No 10s and we stick with the guys who were in camp," said Tuchel in a press conference. "The [last] camp was excellent and we were happy with the last two-and-a-half weeks we had together.

"The impact of all the players was immense throughout the whole camp, that's why we stick mainly with the group and all the offensive players.

"We have Josh King as a new player in there, but I want to see him on both wings. He's kind of an extra player. We can cover all four eventualities because Josh can play all four positions."

Image: Cole Palmer is substituted during England's international friendly against Japan in March

Palmer commitment to England not in question for Tuchel

Pressed on why Palmer, who has six goal involvements in nine Premier League games for Chelsea this season, couldn't break in, Tuchel reiterated the importance of what the previous squad "built" last time out.

"I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception," said Tuchel.

"I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. The players who were in camp built something extraordinary throughout these two-and-a-half weeks and that's why the credit goes to them, the trust is for them.

"It's not personal. We'll never assume Cole isn't in the mindset to come and play for his country but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place."

Asked if Palmer could find a way back in, Tuchel added: "The door is always open. Nothing has changed. We decided to do this camp without him."

Tuchel believes his approach with Palmer, as well as Man Utd midfielder Kobbie Mainoo, who also withdrew from the last camp and has been left out of this squad, sends a clear message about the impact withdrawing from an England camp can have.

"I think it's naturally coming through, without needing to talk about it. That was always the message since early when we took charge: it matters when you're in camp."

Sports.title: Club cricketer dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' banned for two years
Sports.content:
The local league player dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' has been banned for two years from all cricket, while his team has been relegated and handed a 60-point deduction for the upcoming season.

Brian Devine found himself making headlines across the world this summer when he was caught apparently clicking his fingers at first slip during a match for Saltburn Cricket Club's second XI to trick the umpire into thinking the batsman had edged the ball.

Devine was given the nickname 'Clicky Ponting' in reference to the former Australia captain, Ricky Ponting, with the North Yorkshire and South Durham league launching an investigation.

Image: Saltburn Cricket Club was at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' scandal

There were further complaints regarding previous matches and the investigation, which included player interviews, written statements and a detailed review of video footage, took a number of weeks.

Devine and Saltburn admitted the subsequent charges but appealed against the sanction, with a separate panel heard on October 26 and now concluded.

Devine has been suspended from playing, coaching, umpiring, scoring and managing junior teams at all levels until September 29, 2028 while Saltburn have been fined £300.

Their second XI have been relegated to division three of the league and will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction. Middlesbrough Cricket Club 2nd XI will retain their place in Division Two.

Outcomes of Saltburn CC investigation Brian Devine has been suspended from all cricket under the ECB's jurisdiction for two years, from September 30, 2026 to September 29, 2028. He is banned from allowed to coaching, umpiring, scoring or managing junior teams.

Saltburn have been fined £300. The club's second XI has been relegated to Division Three. They will start the 2027 season with a 60-point deduction.

Saltburn said in a statement reported on gazettelive.co.uk: "The club fully participated in the disciplinary proceedings and accept the decision of the appeal following the original decision from the league. We are now focusing on preparations for the 2027 season."

In a statement to Sky Sports, the North Yorkshire and South Durham league said: "The league recognises the strain this has placed on many people, especially those who were abused online and in person.

"We ask everyone to respect that the formal process is now complete. The league will make no further comment."

Sports.title: Hollie Doyle: 'It feels like I've never been away'
Sports.content:
Hollie Doyle won on her first ride back from a five-month injury lay-off last weekend and heads to Doncaster on Saturday - live on Sky Sports Racing - with two rides.

It feels like I've never been away

Almost a week after returning to the racecourse following a fall at Bath that left me with a badly broken left leg, I can honestly say that it feels like I've never been away.

I couldn't have wished for a better start, winning on my first ride back on the James Owen-trained Oxford Circus​ at Southwell. I kept myself fit during my layoff, thanks to daily sessions at Oaksey House in Lambourn, so haven't been lacking for sharpness.

Now I'm concentrating on riding as many winners as I can before I fly out to Hong Kong for the winter, hopefully at the end of November. In the meantime, I'm looking forward to my two rides on the final day of the British Flat Season at Doncaster​ on Saturday.

Baker chasing valuable black type

I'm hoping James Owen's filly Cherry Baker can outrun her big odds in the Listed Virgin Bet Every Saturday Money Back Wentworth Stakes (2.10)​ at Doncaster.

She ran well in the Listed Boadicea Stakes at Newmarket last month when she was fourth to Ruby's Angel and the reopposing Zen Diva​. The latter finished behind her at Chester in May, so the form looks strong.

The cheekpieces Cherry Baker wore for the first time on the Rowley Mile are retained but she will need to step up again if she's to gain some valuable black type.

Indian out to reproduce strong Irish form

Tina's Indian also needs to improve on recent efforts but will enjoy the soft conditions in the closing Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap (3.55)​ at Doncaster.

Brian Toomey's gelding drops back in trip after running over seven-furlongs and a mile in testing ground and wears a hood for the first time. He could be nicely drawn near the stands rail in stall 21 and will hopefully reproduce the good form he showed in Ireland last year.

Castle Can strike again in November Handicap

A plum ride for Cieren Fallon, the William Haggas-trained Castle Cove can come back from a year off to repeat last season's success in the Virgin Bet November Handicap (3.25)​ at Doncaster.

The five-year-old, who remains open to progress, has a good record fresh and will revel in the testing conditions on his first start since taking this valuable prize off an eight-pound lower mark.

A new rating of 100 could yet prove lenient and I prefer him to Richard Hughes's lightly raced market leader Nobody Knows​ who looks ready for this step up in trip with Ryan Moore an eye-catching booking.

In an open race, Ryan's son Toby can give the Moore family plenty to shout about with Too Soon​, whose handicap wins over 12f at Goodwood and Epsom entitle him to the greatest respect.

Beckett filly can make Stakes breakthrough

Ralph Beckett's Revoir is a major player in the Listed Virgin Bet Daily Price Boosts Irish EBF Gillies Fillies Stakes (2.45) at Doncaster.

Despite failing to win since her debut, the reliable four-year-old has posted some fine efforts in defeat, notably in an Italian Group Three last time.

John and Thady Gosden have found a good opportunity for I'm The One who probably needed her run when turned over at short odds at Southwell last time but is better judged on her close second to Amelia Earhart in the Yorkshire Oaks in May.

Toomey colt can make winning Handicap debut

My Boo Boo ​was impressive enough at Brighton to make a winning handicap debut in the Virgin Bet Supports Safer Gambling Nursery (1.35)​ at Doncaster.

Another Brian Toomey runner, he makes the transition from maiden company on an opening mark of 79 which may be enough to give him the edge over Michael Bell's Resemblance​ - a Ffos Las nursery winner two starts ago.

Shane Mosley Jr missed weight on the first attempt for his middleweight clash with Denzel Bentley.

Mosley fights Bentley in the chief support to Chris Billam-Smith vs Cheavon Clarke at the Copper Box Arena on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

The son of boxing legend Shane Mosley, the American contender took to the scales on Friday morning for the official weigh in.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Shane Mosley Jr produced the performance of his career as he floored Serhii Bohachuk in the sixth round before forcing an impressive stoppage win.

London's Bentley looked in fine condition as he hit the 160lb limit exactly. He stayed to watch Mosley return to the scales. The American took the full hour to shed the final pound but did so, having to strip again. The fight is on.

"That's what makes it a good fight, both of us are confident. We haven't got to be at each other's throats to make a fight. We're both respectful but we're letting each other know I think I'm coming out the victor."

Sports.title: Lacey and Man Utd's next generation can rescue Carrick
Sports.content:
Being at Old Trafford on Tuesday night was quite incredible.

Whether the feeling proves short-lived or sparks something bigger for Michael Carrick and Manchester United remains to be seen, but it was important to see a stadium that has been starved of moments to celebrate this season roaring again.

There was plenty to dissect from the comeback win over Roma, but one of the biggest positives for Carrick was the impressive 15-minute cameo from 19-year-old Shea Lacey.

Lacey came on with the drive, confidence and quality to take responsibility and push United forward. His inch-perfect pass to Matheus Cunha was pivotal in setting up the winner.

Manchester United

Aston Villa Sunday 8th November 4:25pm Kick off 4:30pm

It was a moment he had been working towards since the age of eight, when he first chose to join United's academy.

His family, who are originally from Liverpool, allowed him to make his own decision about where he wanted to play his football. He chose the red side of Manchester.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Paul Merson hails the performance of Shea Lacey against Roma and gives his opinion over a possible move for JJ Gabriel to Real Madrid

Having worked his way through the age groups at Carrington, despite a few injury setbacks along the way, it was already evident last season that Lacey was ready for the step up to senior football.

Having watched him extensively at U21 level, I have always been struck by the confidence he carries on the pitch. It is not just his trademark move of cutting inside from the right flank onto his left foot that stands out. His vision, spatial awareness and finishing are all qualities that could make him an excellent fit for a United side lacking creativity.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Dawson reflects on Manchester United's 3-2 comeback win over Roma in the Champions League

He has the work-rate to match, too. Since beginning to train with the first team permanently last season, Lacey has put plenty of work in behind the scenes to ease his transition into senior football.

He has shown real dedication in the gym and in the kitchen to prepare himself for the physical demands of the men's game. He has also regularly stayed behind after training to do extra work with senior players and coaching staff, including Travis Binnion, who knows the youngster well from his time coaching him at U21 level.

That dedication, combined with an infectious and bubbly personality, has made a big impression at Carrington. It has also caught the attention of Carrick, who wanted Lacey around the first team this season because he believed it could be a breakthrough year for the youngster.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lacey scored an incredible goal for Manchester United against Brighton in the Carabao Cup

After his impressive performance off the bench against Roma, I do not think it is getting carried away to suggest Lacey should start against Aston Villa on Sunday.

United are short of attacking options, with Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford both sidelined through injury, while Amad Diallo has looked short of confidence in front of goal.

Lacey is not the only young player who will take confidence from Tuesday night. Despite particularly strong performances from Harry Maguire and Youri Tielemans, Carrick will also be encouraged by the way his younger players rose to the challenge.

Leny Yoro continues to build on an encouraging season, while Kobbie Mainoo played a huge part in driving United forward against Roma in his first start since the beginning of October, having recovered from injury.

Throughout his time as United head coach, Carrick has largely relied on the tried and tested. He has favoured Lisandro Martinez and Maguire as his first-choice centre-back pairing over Yoro and Ayden Heaven. Matthijs de Ligt's return from a back injury could also influence those decisions.

Sports.title: Palmer left out of England squad as Jobe and King called up
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel has left Cole Palmer out of the England squad, along with Phil Foden and Kobbie Mainoo, but Jude Bellingham’s brother Jobe and Fulham midfielder Josh King have earned their first senior call-ups.

Chelsea's Palmer was hugely disappointed when he was overlooked for the World Cup in the summer after a stop-start season due to injury, and he withdrew from the last England camp in September and October because of a minor fitness issue, but he has been back to his best this season with five goals and three assists in 11 appearances.

England made medical checks with Chelsea on Thursday over Palmer and Sky Sports News understands those checks confirmed he was fully fit and ready to take a full part in England's upcoming Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

Speaking about Palmer's omission on Friday, Tuchel said the "door is always open" for him and added: "I guess everyone is desperate to play for England, Cole is no exception. It counts when you're in camp. I said last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. The players who were in camp built something extraordinary.

"It's not personal. We'll never assume Cole isn't in the mindset to come and play for his country but the competition is on and the players in the [last] camp did an amazing job."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel says Jobe Bellingham deserves his call up for England after his standout performances in U21's.

Manchester United midfielder Mainoo also withdrew from the previous squad with an unspecified injury having failed to feature at the World Cup despite being selected.

Tuchel stressed the importance of attending England squads when called up and believes the message is landing.

He said: "It's always the ones who are in camp, the ones who don't withdraw, the ones who walk the talk, and come to camp and show it matters and put the quality in. That's what we will always reward.

"I think it's naturally coming through, without needing to talk about it. That was always the message since very early since we took charge: it matters when you're in camp.

"It matters what you do in camp. The last camp was an excellent one, so the trust and belief is on the players who were there."

Manchester City forward Foden remains out of favour despite contributing six goal involvements in as many games, having been overlooked for last summer's tournament and the autumn squad.

However, the notable absences have created opportunities for first-time call-ups for King and Borussia Dortmund's Jobe Bellingham, both of whom have previously represented England at youth level.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jay Bothroyd has questioned some of Thomas Tuchel's England squad selections

Defenders Trevoh Chalobah and Tino Livramento have both withdrawn through injury, while left-back Nico O'Reilly misses out after being deemed "not 100 per cent" by Manchester City head coach Enzo Maresca, but Real Madrid right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold retains his place in the squad.

Inter Milan full-back Djed Spence returns for the first time since the World Cup after an injury, while Arsenal defender Ben White is recalled after being overlooked since March, when some England supporters booed him.

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is ruled out with a thigh injury, so Everton's James Garner, who was called up as a replacement in the autumn, comes in.

Nottingham Forest forward Morgan Gibbs-White and Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha will look to fill the void left by injured England stalwarts Marcus Rashford and Bukayo Saka, with Arsenal winger Noni Madueke overlooked.

Tuchel makes statement with King over Palmer, Foden

Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

"Josh King's England call-up follows a strong start to the season with Fulham. The 19-year-old, who made his senior breakthrough under Marco Silva, has started every Premier League game under Alvaro Arbeloa and impressed in tough circumstances.

"King, a regular in England's youth teams, has usurped club-record signing Emile Smith Rowe in the No 10 role for Fulham. It is a testament to Thomas Tuchel's belief in his ability that he sees him as an option in a position in which England are stacked with talent. King has been picked ahead of Cole Palmer and Phil Foden. It is a statement by the manager.

Image: Josh King ranks top for touches in the box and six for shots on target

"King joined England's pre-World Cup training camp and only narrowly missed out on selection for September's squad, according to Tuchel. Since then, he has continued to grow in stature for Fulham, taking on more responsibility even at his young age.

"He has two goals and an assist in the Premier League so far this season and his attacking threat is evidenced by an unmatched total of 57 touches in the opposition box, which puts him ahead of Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku. Now to test himself with England."

Can White win over England fans?

Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

"Ben White's England career appeared to be over during his self-imposed exile following a fall-out with Gareth Southgate and Steve Holland at the 2022 World Cup but the Arsenal defender's call-up underlines his value to Thomas Tuchel.

"White's return to the fold in March was divisive. He was booed by some fans at Wembley against Uruguay, even when scoring the opening goal, and ended up conceding a late penalty before attracting more boos in the subsequent meeting with Japan.

"But Tuchel may well have included him in his World Cup squad if not for the knee injury he suffered in May and clearly the manager has not been put off by the hamstring issue that caused him to miss England's last camp in September.

"White has impressed for Arsenal this season, starting regularly at right-back with Jurrien Timber sidelined for the opening months of the campaign. He has shown the attacking threat he offers in the role with three assists in seven Premier League appearances.

"His versatility, as a natural centre-back, likely adds to his appeal to Tuchel but his reception in March shows he still has work to do to repair relations with the Three Lions fanbase."

Sports.title: Amar Dedic set to escape Newcastle sanction over carrying bow and arrow
Sports.content:
Newcastle’s Amar Dedic is unlikely to face a club sanction after being spotted holding a bow and arrow in the Northumberland countryside and sparking a major police pursuit involving an armed response unit.

Dedic is expected to start Newcastle’s match at Fulham on Saturday following an incident that at one point saw six patrol cars pursue the Bosnia right-back back to his home on the upmarket Darras Hall estate, just outside Ponteland.

Northumbria Police were alerted on Wednesday afternoon when a member of the public spotted Dedic and a friend walking through the Northumberland countryside equipped with bows and arrows. This equipment was eventually seized from the boot of the 24-year-old’s car when he arrived back home at Darras Hall.

In a statement the force said they were satisfied the bows and arrows were “for recreational use and there was no threat to the public”, but inquiries were “on-going”. Pursuing animals using bow and arrows or crossbows is illegal in the UK but there are no suggestions that Dedic or his friend were on a hunting expedition.

“Shortly after 1.55pm on Wednesday we received a report of two men carrying a bow and arrow while walking along a track by the reservoir on the Military Road in the Harlow Hill area,” said Northumbria police. “Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized bows and arrows.”

Dedic, a £29.5m summer signing from Benfica, is believed to have been grateful for the coincidental intervention of Newcastle’s fourth-choice goalkeeer Mark Gillespie and former full-back Paul Dummett. The pair were passing Dedic’s home and, spotting the police presence on his drive way, stopped to offer assistance and are understood to have helped calm the situation down. Newcastle are understood to believe Dedic acted “naively.”

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27. The former are one of only five teams in the history of the English top flight to have failed to score in their first four home league matches. Three of the preceding four also drew a blank in game five, which will be deflating news for Oliver Glasner with Manchester City heading to the City Ground on Saturday looking for a win after consecutive league defeats. Forest’s expected goals total implies they should have scored but a flaw in their data shows a reason why.

They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. This is a longstanding issue.

The dishonour of scoring the fewest home goals in Europe’s big five leagues in modern times belongs to Dijon, who bagged eight in 19 Ligue 1 games in 2020-21. Fulham went one goal better in the same season to claim the Premier League’s wooden spoon for home scoring. Both scored three across their first four games, showing the unlikely depths to which Forest’s attack has sunk at the City Ground.

With expected goals a frequent element of post-match analysis, it can be easy to overlook that shots are independent of each other. One is not more likely to be converted when those that preceded it were missed, even though the team’s xG total ticks upward. A side that produced one expected goal through 100 shots valued at 0.01 xG would be far from guaranteed to score.

This reality lies at the heart of Forest’s home woes. Their 62 league shots have been worth 3.58 expected goals. It may feel reasonable to assume they deserve three goals. But only two of the efforts were deemed by Opta to be big chances, only five more had a better than one-in-10 probability of being converted and more than two-thirds were valued at 0.06 xG or less. Only against Coventry did they muster at least one expected goal in total, needing 24 attempts to register 1.09 xG.

Forest’s chance quality is so poor because many of their efforts are struck from long range. They have taken 50.3% of their City Ground shots from outside the box, at least 6% more than any Premier League team did on their respective patch in any of the past five seasons.

Glasner’s side are having to do this because they are struggling to get the ball into the penalty area. Again, this is a problem that predates the Austrian’s appointment. Forest were below the league average of 36.6% for their home pass accuracy into the box in 2025-26 (33.3%) and have sunk lower this season (29.6%). Cross accuracy is not the most instructive metric because the most dangerous deliveries can evade teammates if they are not anticipating them. Nonetheless, Forest’s home data paints the same picture as with their passing; below league average (26.6%) for completion rate last season (21.7%) and worse again in 2026-27 (19.0%).

Having to shoot from distance has helped make them chronically unable to put shots on target. Forest have done this only nine times in the league at the City Ground, giving them a shot accuracy rate of 14.5%. It is unsurprising to see Schalke on 18.8% given they are equally goal-shy. The least accurate home side across the past 10 seasons of football in Europe’s big five leagues are the Parma class of 2025-26. Even they managed to put 23.7% of their shots on target when taking last place in a sample of 974 team season examples.

If Forest don’t score against City, their next opportunity will come against a Chelsea side that have recently tightened up. No English top flight side have failed to score in their first six home games but Forest setting this unwanted record looks distinctly possible.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Lampard will get warm welcome at Everton

Nothing better encapsulates the dysfunction that was Everton under Farhad Moshiri than the idea that an unknown vandal with a can of spray paint could influence the club’s managerial direction. “Pereira out, Lampard in” they daubed on a wall at Goodison Park when it appeared Vítor Pereira was in line to replace Rafael Benítez in 2022. Alarmed by fan protests, the Everton board opted instead for Frank Lampard and, while his tenure ended 12 months later with the club immersed in another relegation battle, there will be appreciation for the Coventry manager when he makes a first visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. The connection between Lampard and Evertonians was genuine and a factor in keeping the club up in 2022. Both parties will be glad to see the other emerging stronger from those troubled times. Jack Grealish, meanwhile, will again be absent for Everton after his recent disciplinary breach, although the manager, David Moyes, said: “We will be working again with Jack soon.” Andy Hunter

Everton v Coventry City, Friday 8pm (all times GMT)

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard enjoys Coventry’s victory against Sunderland last month. Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/Shutterstock

2 Farke keeps it real as Leeds aim to stop slide

Back in September, when Leeds thrashed Newcastle 4-1 at Elland Road, talk of European qualification filled the West Yorkshire airwaves. Since then Daniel Farke’s side have drawn three and lost two of their ensuing Premier League games, scoring just two goals along the way. Given that their final pass has persistently let them down, optimism is turning to pessimism. Farke would call it realism. The German – who could probably do without facing Roberto De Zerbi’s improving Tottenham on Saturday – is confident his side are making progress but knows they cannot expect to run before properly mastering the art of walking. “We don’t have the individual quality [of the Premier League’s leading teams],” said Farke on Thursday. “We have to compensate by being tactically spot on and good at winning second balls. It’s not a criticism of my players, it’s reality. The dream of Europe is allowed but we know our main aim is to reach 40 points as quickly as possible.” Louise Taylor

Leeds v Tottenham, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Zubimendi fights for his Arsenal future

Martín Zubimendi has yet to start a Premier League game this season after falling down the pecking order at Arsenal and the Spain midfielder is likely to be the subject of speculation that he could seek to depart in January. The emergence of Myles Lewis-Skelly as an alternative in the No 6 position at the end of last season has had an impact on Zubimendi after he had been a regular starter for most of his debut campaign in the Premier League. The 27-year-old signed from Real Sociedad for around £55m 15 months ago and Mikel Arteta has insisted he remains an integral part of his plans. But with the Arsenal manager trying to find the right balance in his midfield after the arrival of Bruno Guimarães, Zubimendi will be hoping he gets another chance to stake his claim against Hull on Saturday after starting in the narrow win over Slavia Prague in midweek. Ed Aarons

Arsenal v Hull City, Saturday 3pm

4 Fulham reap rewards of sticking with Arbeloa

Álvaro Arbeloa is proof that a struggling young manager working in England for the first time can bounce back after a difficult start. Arbeloa was sliding towards the sack a month ago but he has responded at Fulham, who have taken seven points from their last three games, and will hope to extend the unbeaten run when Matthias Jaissle’s inconsistent Newcastle visit Craven Cottage. It is an inviting fixture for Fulham and a big one for Newcastle, who were poor when they lost to Everton on Monday. Jaissle, hired as Eddie Howe’s replacement in the summer, is already under pressure. But the 38-year-old could take inspiration from how Arbeloa has given himself breathing space at Fulham. Jacob Steinberg

Fulham v Newcastle, Saturday 3pm

5 Will Glasner’s risky words inspire Forest?

Oliver Glasner has previous. He led Wolfsburg from mid-table to the Champions League but fell out with the club hierarchy and left in 2021. Glasner next guided Eintracht Frankfurt to Europa League glory but was openly critical of the squad’s imbalance and quality in four separate outbursts and departed in 2023. His time at Crystal Palace was a great success but after accusing the Eagles’ board in January of “abandoning” his team with the sale of Marc Guéhi to Manchester City, the Austrian left this summer for Nottingham Forest, where he became the fifth head coach in less than a year. You can probably guess where this is going. After Saturday’s defeat by Brentford left Forest 19th, Glasner was typically abrasive: “If the players buy in [to my methods], I think we can have a turnaround. And if not, the sixth manager will come in.” We’ll soon find out if Glasner has won the players around with City visiting Nottingham this weekend. If Forest’s woeful form continues, Glasner may either walk or get his marching orders from trigger-happy owner Evangelos Marinakis. Michael Butler

Nottingham Forest v Manchester City, 5.30pm

View image in fullscreen Oliver Glasner is under pressure at the City Ground. Photograph: Andrew Kearns/CameraSport/Getty Images

6 Nketiah ready to step back into limelight

Pierre Sage pulled no punches in his assessment of Eddie Nketiah’s career after his excellent winning goal against Fulham last week in the EFL Cup. “I think his potential is higher than his performance for the moment,” said the Crystal Palace manager. “And we have to reduce this gap – because he needs it, the team needs it.” Nketiah is now 27 and won his solitary senior cap for England in 2023 after becoming the record scorer for the under-21s while he was still at Arsenal. His chances of adding to that look unlikely these days having been relegated to third-choice striker at Selhurst Park behind Jean-Philippe Mateta and Jørgen Strand Larsen. But with Mateta suspended for three matches after Palace’s appeal over his red card against Tottenham was rejected, Sunday’s meeting with Liverpool could be another chance for Nketiah to show his ability after scoring a late winner against them in Palace’s thrilling win over Arne Slot’s side last year. EA

Crystal Palace v Liverpool, Sunday 2pm

7 Brighton dreaming of Champions League nights

It has been three weeks since Brighton’s fans were savouring a famous 5-0 thrashing of arch-rivals Crystal Palace at the Amex. But the quirks of the fixture list meant that Fabian Hürzeler’s side played five successive games on the road since then, including two trips to face Manchester City. While they lost some of the momentum from the Palace victory in the defeat by Liverpool at Anfield, last week’s Premier League win over City showed they are serious contenders for the top four and perhaps even more. But Brentford’s visit to the south coast should provide a real test of those credentials as the owner, Tony Bloom, renews his rivalry with his west London counterpart Matthew Benham, who traditionally eschews his seat in the directors’ box for one in the away section. EA

Brighton v Brentford, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen The Seagulls celebrate their victory at Manchester City last weekend.

Photograph: Robbie Jay Barratt/AMA/Getty Images

8 In-form Kroupi pushing for start at Ipswich

Eli Junior Kroupi did not take the headlines in Bournemouth’s win over Leeds but his cheeky nutmeg and sumptuous no-look pass to set up Amine Adli for the Cherries’ second goal was a reminder of why the youngster continues to be linked with a move to Arsenal, Bayern and PSG, despite being sidelined recently. Kroupi scored 13 Premier League goals last season – only Ryan Giggs, Wayne Rooney, Michael Owen and Romelu Lukaku have reached that total as teenagers – and only Erling Haaland and Will Osula enjoyed a better goal-per-game ratio in 2025-26. Kroupi’s foot injury, sustained in pre-season, has been carefully managed but after three substitute appearances in the wins over Manchester United, Aston Villa and Leeds, will Marco Rose be tempted to start Kroupi at Ipswich? Evanilson is in red hot form as the central striker but Kroupi is just as comfortable as a No 10 and surely has to play if he is fit as Bournemouth chase a seventh consecutive win in all competitions. MB

Ipswich v Bournemouth, Sunday 2pm

9 Chelsea return to a very different Sunderland

It is not quite six months since Sunderland beat Chelsea 2-1 at the Stadium of Light and qualified for Europe for the first time in 53 years. A day when Régis Le Bris’s side eclipsed the Club World Cup holders and Enzo Le Fée upstaged Enzo Fernández concluded with Sunderland finishing seventh. During the prolonged post-match celebrations, the captain, Granit Xhaka, grabbed a microphone and declared: “This is just the beginning – we want more.” Fast forward to gloomy November and it is not quite working out like that with even the excitement of next month’s trip to Milan overshadowed by anxiety. Sunderland are bottom of the Premier League, Le Bris concedes his side are in a relegation fight and Xhaka has looked a shadow of his former self ever since Chelsea tried and failed to sign him in the summer. Is Xhaka capable of turning back time? Sunderland securing just a second league win of the season depends on it. Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Chelsea, Sunday 2pm

10 United brace for another chaotic weekend

Can Manchester United win two games of football on the bounce for the first time this season? Being able to pose this question sums up the state Michael Carrick and his side are in as they seek to build on Tuesday’s chaotic comeback victory over Roma. Aston Villa arrive five points better off than their hosts and are everything United are not: stable, upwardly mobile and boasting a manager in Unai Emery who consistently improves players and yields results. As the international break beckons after this last Premier League fixture of the weekend, will Carrick survive what could be an eighth loss in 15 matches? Possibly, if it is not another humiliation, but the truth may be that even United’s erratic executives do not currently know the answer. Jamie Jackson

Sports.title: Win at Everton would put Coventry on right side of history in survival fight
Sports.content:
If Coventry win at Everton on Friday night they will take an enormous stride towards maintaining their Premier League status. That might seem a huge statement with 28 games remaining, but victory would put Frank Lampard’s side on the right side of recent history. For now, they stand on a precipice.

Coventry have taken nine points from nine league matches. Eight teams in the previous 10 seasons were in the same position – seven stayed up. The exception, Leicester in 2024-25, were newly promoted and have tumbled downwards ever since.

There were 21 clubs in the last decade with 12 points after 10 matches. None of them went down and eight finished in the top half. Lampard’s first return to a former club this season suddenly looks remarkably important. Even if a win cannot guarantee Coventry’s top-flight survival, they would occupy what has been a strong position historically.

Lampard has a similar managerial record to former teammate (and new West Ham manager) Scott Parker, a midfielder alongside whom he made 27 appearances for Chelsea. Excellent in the second tier - Lampard reached the playoffs at worst in each of his three Championship campaigns - he has never fully convinced in the Premier League. Given he took Chelsea to fourth place and the FA Cup final in 2019-20, perhaps that is unfair. Equally, they had finished third the year before and were champions in two of the four campaigns prior to that.

Though he kept Everton up in 2022, Lampard won only nine of his 38 league matches with the club. No Everton manager with at least as many games has a lower win percentage in all competitions, with that post followed by a caretaker spell back at Chelsea in which he won only once in 11 matches.

Regardless of Lampard’s ability, what can we reasonably expect from Coventry? Capology estimate the club have the lowest wage bill in the division, while Transfermarkt rate their squad as having the third-lowest market value. This challenging reality was reflected in pre-season predictions. Opta gave Coventry a better chance of staying up than their fellow promoted sides, Hull and Ipswich. The former have delivered the weakest performance of the three and are now deemed the most likely of the trio to go back down. They have faced all the current top three, in fairness, while Hull haven’t played any of them and Ipswich have only tackled one.

Coventry remain third-favourites for the drop, as they were in pre-season. It is just the teams below them that have changed, with Sunderland and Crystal Palace now propping up the forecast. With the possibility of Manchester City facing a points deduction, third bottom might be enough to remain in the Premier League.

That issue notwithstanding, Coventry’s underlying performance needs to improve. Not that anyone would have cared when they scored three times to beat Sunderland last weekend when only recording 0.69 in expected goals. Newcastle had the better of the chances when losing 4-1 at the Coventry Building Society Arena, too. Their match against Hull is the only one this season in which they were on the right side of the xG.

Coventry led the Championship for expected goal difference last season. Lampard’s Chelsea improved on this metric in 2019-20 from the season before and were only 0.6 behind champions Liverpool. The 48-year-old has shown he can lead teams to strong statistical performance, though Coventry are clearly far more of an underdog this season than Lampard’s sides were in his strongest campaigns.

Everton did not beat any of the top seven at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season and lost 2-0 to Chelsea in their previous home league match. They have generally performed well against struggling sides, though. Their only home defeats to bottom-half sides last season were against Newcastle and Tottenham, two clubs who were in the Champions League.

Victory on Friday is a tall order for Coventry, but if Lampard can win at Everton for the first time in his managerial career, his side will be well set for the task of staying up.

Sports.title: Cape Verde captain Ryan Mendes cleared of rape allegation as woman charged with false statement
Sports.content:
New Zealand police have dismissed a rape allegation against Cape Verde football captain Ryan Mendes and have charged the accuser with making a false statement.

Detective inspector Scott Beard said Friday the claim that a sexual assault occurred at a central Auckland hotel in March had not been substantiated.

A 40-year-old woman has been charged under New Zealand’s Crimes Act with making a false statement. She is expected to appear in court next week.

“A decision to prosecute in these circumstances is not taken lightly and follows months of investigative work by our Adult Sexual Assault Team,” Beard said.

The incident was alleged to have occurred hours after Cape Verde played Chile in a friendly match in Auckland, won 4-2 by Chile.

Mendes’ lawyer, Karl Trotter, said the allegation resulted in his client facing intense international media speculation.

Cape Verde qualified for the 2026 World Cup and the subject of the alleged assault arose at almost every media conference Mendes attended.

“Mr Mendes was thrilled to finally be able to get this behind him and he regards it as a complete vindication,” Karl Trotter told the New Zealand Herald newspaper.

“It is to be hoped that this recent turn of events, clearing Mr Mendes of the allegation of rape, attracts the same level of media attention as the original reporting.”

The 36-year-old Mendes is Cape Verde’s most capped player, having made 103 appearances since his debut in 2010. He currently plays for RS Berkane in Morocco.

Sports.title: Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words
Sports.content:
Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon.

“It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.”

Parker is back in the thick of it. Out of work after leaving Burnley in the wake of relegation from the Premier League last April, he cut short his break from management when West Ham parted company with Nuno Espírito Santo. Nuno was sacked early on Tuesday and replaced by Parker, who is intent on leading West Ham out of the Championship at the first time of asking.

It will not be easy. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after three games without a win and displayed their inconsistencies against Cardiff. They made another slow start, conceding three during the first half, but roared back after a triple half-time change from Parker. Jarrod Bowen was inspired. But Parker needs complete performances if West Ham are to win automatic promotion.

“The Championship’s a tough league,” he said. “It doesn’t matter what name you have on a bit of paper. You have to have a level of humility of what this league needs. That’s a challenge when you come out of the Premier League.”

Parker argued that talent was not enough. Burnley were stingy when they won promotion. Parker has to sort out West Ham’s defence. “Of course we want to play a certain brand,” the 46-year-old said. “But I think it’s just a non-negotiable in terms of a committed team.”

Connections need to be rebuilt with disillusioned supporters. Parker was an all-action midfielder who loved his four years at West Ham as a player. He has added Mark Noble to his backroom staff. Noble has held the role of West Ham’s sporting director since retiring in 2022 but Parker confirmed the former club captain would have a role as an assistant coach. “He’s going to be coaching with me and be that sounding board,” Parker said.

View image in fullscreen Jarrod Bowen was inspired during West Ham’s comeback to earn a 3-3 draw at Cardiff. Photograph: David Davies/PA

Noble will be able to get Parker up to speed on his squad. West Ham need improvement at the back, better balance in midfield and more bite up front. Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, could be busy in January. Parker wants to give everyone a clean slate, though. Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez will have opportunities. Even Maxwel Cornet travelled with the squad to Cardiff.

Parker did not focus during negotiations with Karim Virani, West Ham’s interim CEO, and Daniel Kretinsky, the club’s largest shareholder, on whether funds would be available for signings. One step at a time.

West Ham are in transition. David Sullivan still owns a 40% stake but is no longer on the board. Kretinsky’s power has grown, although the Czech billionaire is yet to say much in public. Parker has heard more from Kretinsky than most people.

“I found a man that was hugely passionate,” Parker said. “I instantly felt that, along with Karim, along with Nils. These were three people who know where they want the club to go.”

The target is a return to the top flight. Parker has won promotion with Bournemouth, Burnley and Fulham but his record at keeping teams up is less impressive. He has been dismissed a little unfairly as nothing more than a promotion specialist.

“In a short space of a coaching career I’ve had some huge success,” Parker said. “I’ve had some blips in terms of two full seasons in the Premier League. All I know is that I’m fully committed.”

That mindset convinced Kretinsky, Virani and Koppen to pick Parker. They wanted his knowledge of the club and record at this level.

West Ham are eighth before visiting Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. They are taking 7,000 fans to Ewood Park and Parker knows there can be no more complacency.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye?

The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back.

At the 2022 World Cup, Fernando Santos belatedly took the decision to leave Ronaldo out for the last-16 tie against Switzerland. Portugal suddenly had a fluency and fluidity they had lacked for years and the player who had replaced Ronaldo, Gonçalo Ramos, scored a hat-trick. That seemed incontrovertible evidence the end was upon Ronaldo, or at least his role might become that of an impact substitute.

But even in the final minutes of that game, half the crowd were chanting for Ronaldo. Some, perhaps, were Portuguese fans but many were tourists. They didn’t care much about the result or who went through, they just wanted to see the famous man do the famous thing. Near the end, he scored a goal that was obviously offside. He knew it was offside, but he also knew what his public wanted. So he did the “Siuuuu …” celebration and was rewarded with the biggest cheer of the night. This was like seeing late-period Elvis in Las Vegas: it didn’t matter he was no longer the singer he had been, he was still Elvis. It’s just that Elvis wasn’t also carrying Portugal’s World Cup hopes on his rhinestoned shoulders.

When a player has such celebrity status, when he is still somehow the show no matter how sluggish his movements, making that decision on when to quit must become even harder. And Ronaldo, with his status as Portugal’s greatest soft-power export, also became a political issue. A cabinet minister publicly said he couldn’t be dropped because of how much revenue he generated and what he meant for Portugal’s brand. Portugal is not a country replete with global superstars.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo shows his frustration in the Nations League game against and Wales in September – which has turned out to be his last for Portugal. Photograph: Patrícia de Melo Moreira/AFP/Getty Images

Quick Guide 'Thank you, idol': reaction to Ronaldo's international retirement Show Portuguese Football Federation "Every drop of sweat, every decisive goal, and every captain’s arm-band he wore with honour on the field reflected his unconditional love ⁠for our jersey. His dedication ⁠and his legacy ​transcend the four lines of the field. Ronaldo has raised Portugal’s profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for ⁠many of us, he is the greatest player of all time! …" Al-Nassr (Ronaldo's current club) "It’s not just a chapter – it’s history you’ve shaped. You’re an icon to the entire world, not ⁠just Portugal. Portugal is in your heart, and you are in the hearts of the world. A page ​has turned, but there is still history left ‌for us to write together at ‌your home, Al-Nassr." Manchester United (one of Ronaldo's former clubs) "Congratulations on an incredible international career." Bruno Fernandes (Portugal and Manchester United) "Thank ‌you for the inspiration. It was a privilege to be able to share great moments with our national team alongside my childhood idol." Diogo Dalot (Portugal and Manchester United) "They don’t know that dreams are a constant in life … Portugal’s history tells us that we are a people who have never accepted limits, unafraid of uncharted seas or weathering storms. We were and are shaped by achievements, sacrifices, tears, and sweat … ‌By dreams that seem impossible – until someone has the courage to make them a reality. You did it. You made us believe, dream, and achieve! A legacy that will be remembered ​not only for the trophies or the goals, but also for the path you paved for all those who came after you. Your passion and determination to represent our country is something I’ll never forget and that will stay with me forever. I’m immensely proud of everything you’ve done for our national team! Thank you, idol." Pepe (Former Portugal and Real Madrid defender) "It was more than just soccer. Thanks for everything, Cris." Gianni Infantino, Fifa president "Few players have ever ​touched the heart of football fans ​around the world quite like Cristiano. A career defined by extraordinary talent, relentless determination and ​an unwavering desire to ‌push the boundaries ​of what is possible … Cristiano has ​achieved milestones that may never be matched but his greatest legacy goes far beyond records, trophies and goals … Thank you, Cristiano, for the passion, the unforgettable moments and the immense contribution you have made to our beautiful game proudly wearing the 'Selecao' shirt. Your international career will forever be part of football’s history." Reuters Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Ronaldo hung around at Euro 2024, weeping after missing a penalty against Slovenia, the magnitude of his fame and ego warping perception so everything became about him, no matter how many other hugely gifted players were in that squad. And implausibly he was still doing it at the World Cup this summer: gumming the mechanisms, constantly demanding the ball, occasionally drifting out to the left to get in Rafael Leão’s way. At one point against Spain in what turns out to have been his final World Cup game, Ronaldo was released on the break but, lacking pace, ended up having to turn back and play the ball to his full-back, the opportunity gone. There was something almost painful about seeing a player once so explosive reduced to this.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There needed to be some sort of intervention. This generation of Portuguese players, who really should be challenging for major honours and not just the Nations League, could not continue to struggle on with such an albatross around their necks. It came from Jorge Jesus, the admirably forthright 72-year-old national coach, who was appointed after the World Cup. He didn’t bring Ronaldo off the bench in the second half of a tight game Portugal ended up winning against Norway. Ronaldo insisted he had been promised minutes – but even if there had been an agreement, it would be absurd to refuse a coach the capacity to adapt to circumstance – and stormed out of the camp, an indication perhaps of how his self-regard had come to distort his judgment.

And, assuming this retirement isn’t some sort of power play to force Jesus out, that is where it ended, with a €255 (£212) fine and 30-day ban over a period in which Portugal had no games. Ronaldo will go back to the Saudi Pro League to continue his pursuit of a 1,000th goal. He has been an extraordinary player. He will be remembered as an all-time great, vying with Eusébio as the greatest Portugal player of all time, but his legacy is undoubtedly tainted by this protracted farewell, by the sense that a player who at his best could win games single-handed, came by the end to be a burden to his national team. His has been a great career, but it would have been greater had it been a little shorter.

Sports.title: Bayern Munich tipped to re-sign Harry Kane teammate months after selling him
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich have not given up on Maurice Krattenmacher despite allowing the young midfielder to leave the club this summer.

The 21-year-old spent last season on loan at Hertha Berlin before Bayern sold him to SV Elversberg with the goal of getting him solid Bundesliga experience.

3 Krattenmacher started his career at Bayern back in 2013 when he was 8 years old Credit: Getty

The German giants wisely secured a buy-back clause in his contract knowing the upside of him doing well away from the club - which he has so far.

Krattenmacher’s buy-back clause with Bayern is reportedly worth €7.5million (£6.2million), with his contract with Elversberg running through to June 2030.

He almost came back to haunt the Bavarian behemoths in September, scoring a stunning goal in their 2-1 loss to Bayern Munich.

While he was on the losing side, the 21-year-old's progression has been noted by chiefs in Munich who would want him to combine with Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane.

Krattenmacher himself has also left the door open to a Bayern return, and previously said: "Of course, it's every young player's dream to play for FC Bayern."

However, he stressed that his priority was continuing his development and said: "I think sometimes you have to take what may seem like a step backwards in order to then take two steps forward."

Additionally, Bayern Munich are currently dealing with several injury problems in attack, with Jamal Musiala, Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari all unavailable.

And European football expert Andy Brassell told talkSPORT.com he believes Krattenmacher could help them solve a big problem.

He said: "I think the first weeks of this season have suggested that Bayern are in a win-win situation.

"They will be able to activate the buyout clause because the way that Krattenmacher has started this season, there is absolutely no way on God's green earth that he's going to be at Elversberg next season.

3 Kompany has also spoken about how impressed he is with the youngster Credit: Getty

"Absolutely none, because his level is so high. He is a player who you'd be excited by as a fan, but I think you'd be excited by as a scout because he offers so many potential solutions.

"He's someone who is great at creating space in tight areas, who can drift in as a midfielder running into the box to make a late run, who can get into those pockets of space, who can pop up on the left, on the right, two good feet, good at beating defenders, good finisher with either foot in the box or from a distance as well.

"I'm just wondering what the numbers are going to be at the end of the season because if he carries on like he's playing, Elversberg aren't going to be anywhere near getting relegated. And bear in mind they are the heavy favourites to get relegated like they were at the start of the season.

"They are a club that doesn't have a train station in a town, doesn't have a town hall; they've had to build a press box to get more people in."

Elversberg currently sit seventh in the Bundesliga on 13 points, and are equal to Bayer Leverkusen who currently are in the European positions.

Krattenmacher has made eight appearances, scoring four goals and making one assist so far this season, the kind of output Bayern could do with during their injury crisis.

3 Elversburg are competing in their first season of the Bundesliga Credit: Getty

Bayern's injury solution

Brassell added: "It's sort of scaffolding at the moment. It's a remarkable situation. You've got this guy who turns up, and of course he's from the other side of the tracks. He's from Sabener Strabe, he's from all the facilities at Bayern and there must be a bit of a culture shock for him as well.

"But he has been so good and he's embraced the challenge really well, he's got good players around him to link up with, you think of Cole Campbell who came from Borussia Dortmund who Elversberg have spent proper money on to get him in.

"And I just think, either Bayern are going to bring Krattenmacher back for their own purposes, and don't rule that out by the way because they've got so many forward injuries at the moment. I do wonder if they have a little dip for him in January.

"Now obviously Elversberg would be within their rights to refuse that. I'm not sure they would because if they could get a substantial amount of cash in, and it would be a substantial amount of cash for them with their record signing costing just over £5million.

"And that for them is really pushing the boat out. For them to get some proper money would be a good thing, especially for a player who doesn't really feel as if he's going to be there sustainably.

"If Bayern don't take him to cover for all those attacking injuries that they've got at the moment, remember Saibari is out until probably January, February at least, then another mid-table Bundesliga club will pick him up next season.

"Because he is a player who I think if you drop him into any team outside the top six or eight, he gets into the eleven quite easily. And he adds a little bit of X-factor to any of those teams."

Sports.title: 39-cap England star told he may never play for Three Lions again
Sports.content:
39-cap England star told he may never play for Three Lions again

Jack Grealish’s international career is fading quickly.

That is the view of talkSPORT’s Ray Parlour as the Everton loanee's long England absence continues.

4 Jack Grealish has been warned that his international days are fast approaching the end Credit: Getty

Grealish has clocked up a total of 39 caps but has not featured for the Three Lions since a Nations League clash against Finland in October 2024.

In that time, the 31-year-old fell out of favour at Manchester City, paving the way for a loan spell at Everton last season.

Grealish secured a return to the Hill Dickinson Stadium again this summer but has since failed to convince Thomas Tuchel.

The former Aston Villa captain has been further hampered by the country’s boom in attacking talent.

Josh King, Rio Ngumoha and Morgan Rogers are just two of the players who have leapfrogged Grealish in the international set-up.

And with the hierarchy unlikely to budge any time soon, Parlour believes the light is almost out on Grealish’s international career.

Time is running out

“I think his age is against him now and I think there’s too many players in front of him,” the former Arsenal midfielder told the Breakfast Show.

“All Jack has got to worry about is playing well for his club.

“If there’s a really bad list of injuries or something happens (who knows?), but I think his time has probably gone now.”

Grealish arguably has more pressing concerns at present.

4 Grealish has not pulled on an England shirt for over two years Credit: Getty

4 The Everton winger has featured eight times this season but is yet to register a goal or an assist Credit: Getty

The winger is set to miss his fourth consecutive game when the Toffees host Coventry City on Friday night – live on talkSPORT.

Grealish was initially dropped from the Everton squad for the visit of Newcastle United on October 29, for a 'breach of club discipline'.

talkSPORT understands that Grealish had an unauthorised absence from training although Everton are yet to reveal reasons for the sanction.

Toffees’ boss David Moyes has remained tight-lipped on the conflict but told reporters that he supports the club’s decision on Grealish while highlighting Everton’s values.

Moyes confirmed on Thursday that Grealish would not be considered for Friday’s fixture but left the door open on a return to the side.

Asked if the upcoming international break could help conclude the issue, Moyes told reporters: "We just need to wait and see how things go.

4 Everton boss David Moyes says Grealish still has a future at the club Credit: Getty

"I wouldn't give you the plan (on a reintegration timeline) but we will be working with Jack again soon."

Casting an eye over the standoff, Parlour likened Moyes’ values to those of the Premier League managerial old guard.

“I think he’s old school, David,” Parlour said. “There’s rules that you set. Sir Alex Ferguson and George Graham back in the day, they would stand for certain things.

“David is very similar.

“There’s a lot of young players at Everton and they’ll be looking at the senior pros and Jack is a player they will be looking at. Jack’s got to try and help the young players.”
