Sports.title: Man United wonderkid Shea Lacey eyed up by rival nation amid uncertain England future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson is considering poaching Manchester United starlet Shea Lacey.

The 19-year-old is an England youth international, but qualifies to play for Ireland through his dad.

3 Academy graduate Lacey has played an increasingly bigger role for United this term Credit: Getty

Lacey has impressed in cameos for the Red Devils this season, making six appearances in all competitions.

His biggest contribution yet came in United's 3-2 comeback win over Roma on Wednesday, as he assisted Matheus Cunha's winner in the Champions League thriller.

International tug-of-war?

While Lacey will need more experience under his belt before he can think about an England senior call-up, there could already be international recognition elsewhere.

His displays have caught the eye of Ireland boss Hallgrimsson, who admitted the national set-up have been exploring his eligibility.

Asked if he has been in contact with the teen ahead of next week’s Nations League clash with Austria, Hallgrimsson said: "That would be for other guys in the association.

"But it was interesting looking at his Irish connection."

Lacey has represented England from Under-15 to Under-20 level, earning 19 caps and scoring nine goals across all age groups

He is expected to be included in the Under-20 squad for the upcoming games against Czechia and Portugal in the U20 Elite League.

But there is a United connection in the Ireland set-up, with Hallgrimsson’s assistant manager former cult hero John O’Shea.

Ireland's interest in Lacey comes after a promising start to the season from the youngster, who has made just 8 first-team appearances.

3 Heimir Hallgrimsson admitted Lacey's Irish heritage has been discussed Credit: Getty

Previously dubbed by United fans as 'the Scouse Lionel Messi', Lacey made his senior debut under Ruben Amorim in December 2025.

He featured off the bench in a 2-1 loss to Aston Villa, while his full debut came in the Carabao Cup 3-2 defeat to Brighton in September, where he scored the opener after just seven minutes.

Lacey in line for Prem debut

After his game-changing cameo against Roma in midweek, Lacey now looks set to be given a huge opportunity this weekend.

talkSPORT host Andy Goldstein has revealed that sources have told him that Michael Carrick will hand the teenager his first-ever Premier League start against Aston Villa this weekend.

With Lacey's contribution against Roma helping to keep Carrick in a job, he is now primed to be repaid with a huge show of faith.

Speaking on Thursday's Drive, Goldstein said: "I've heard, by the way, it's the same person that told me that Bruno Fernandes was going to be dropped, that Shea Lacey starts against Villa.

3 Lacey's impactful cameo off the bench against Roma has shown he's ready to play a bigger part for Man United Credit: AFP

"How about that? He was so good for Man United [against Roma], and when the crowd watch him, they're on the edge of their seat.

"Genuinely, you can hear that 'gasp'."

"I like Amad, but there's obviously something that we're missing with his game. Maybe his finishing's not that great," Goldstein added.

"Shea Lacey looks like a really, really good player."

Lacey has just made two cameo outings in the Premier League so far this term, the first of which came in the opening-day defeat to Hull City.

Sports.title: Conor Coady announces shock retirement from football aged 33
Sports.content:
Ex-England international Conor Coady has announced his retirement from football at the age of 33.

Coady posted a heartfelt video on Instagram on Friday morning disclosing the decision to call time on his career.

4 Conor Coady was best known for his time at Wolves where he clocked up 273 appearances for the club Credit: Getty

The defender started his career with Liverpool before going on to represent seven other clubs throughout his 15-year career.

He is best remembered for his eight-year spell at Wolves where he rose to prominence.

That saw him break into Gareth Southgate’s England squad in 2020 and made his debut in a Nations League clash against Denmark.

He went on to earn ten caps for the Three Lions, scoring once.

Coady was part of the England squad that finished runners up at Euro 2020, losing in the final to Italy on penalties.

His last act as a player came with Wrexham last season following his £2million exit from Leicester City.

Coady initially signed a two-year deal with the Red Dragons but left the club in August following the mutual termination of his contract.

Hi path outside of football was always well mapped out having carried out regular punditry appearances.

And just days after leaving the Racecourse Ground, Coady started a new role as England Under-21s assistant boss.

Coady's video statement.

In an outpouring of emotion on Instagram, Coady said: “So where do I start? From being a young boy at Rainford Rangers, to living every young lad’s dream and playing at the highest level.

4 Coady was part of the England squads for Euro 2020 and the 2022 World Cup Credit: Getty

“Eight clubs, 503 appearances, two promotions, a World Cup and a Euros. Ten England caps.

“Football is my life. It always has been. But everything at some point always comes to an end.

“I never, ever thought playing for Wolves in Europe or going with England to a World Cup this day would come.

“But honestly, the last couple of years have been tough. Not playing as much as I would have liked I have struggled with, as I live for playing footie.

“Coming through at my boyhood club and putting the red shirt on was one of the proudest days as no one could ever take that away from me."

He then gave a classy nod to his other former employers.

4 Coady spent a season on loan at Everton Credit: Getty

“Sheffield United and Huddersfield were perfect clubs for me and made me grow. Then came Wolves, the place I needed and the place that made me a man.

“Eight of the best years, with the best people in a city that made me their own.

“My kids were born in old gold and you made Amie truly enjoy football. For that it will always be home.

“Then came Everton, when Frank gave me the opportunity to play for your great football club. The Bournemouth game, when you dragged us over the line, when we were on the floor. I’m very proud to say I played at Goodison.

“On to Leicester, then Wrexham, which were tough at times but filled with amazing people and supporters who care deeply about their club.

“Then Charlton, who put a smile back on my face. The truth is I’m ready now. I’ve given football everything and I will continue to do so in my next chapter.

4 Coady's time at Leicester was shrouded in difficulty sparked by the club's relegation from the Premier League Credit: Getty

“But it’s time for my incredible wife Amie, and four boys, to enjoy seeing daddy a little bit more.

“And my four boys; Henry, Freddie, Louis and Jesse. To say you’ve seen me play football and be there during my career, the memories we can talk about forever.

“Mum, dad and my brother Harrison. I can’t thank you enough for all the sacrifices you made, and helping me live out my dream.

“And onto James. You’re not just an agent, but you’re a friend. You’ve helped me throughout my career and I can’t wait to see what the next few years in store for us.

“Thank you to all the fans from every club I played for. With every shirt I put on, I gave it my all. It’s been an honour to say I played this unbelievable game. Thank you for everything. Coads.”

Sports.title: Jobe Bellingham handed surprise England call-up along with uncapped Premier League star as Cole Palmer left out
Sports.content:
Jobe Bellingham handed surprise England call-up along with uncapped Premier League star as Cole Palmer left out

Jobe Bellingham has been handed a surprise England call-up for the upcoming international break.

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder, brother of Jude Bellingham, gets his first senior nod along with uncapped Fulham star Josh King.



3 Jobe Bellingham has helped Dortmund to joint-top of the Bundesliga summit with Bayern Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, there is no place in the squad for Cole Palmer despite the Chelsea midfielder being available.

The 24-year-old's commitment was questioned by manager Thomas Tuchel after he withdrew from the most recent international break.

Manchester City star Phil Foden is another big name who misses out once again.



Who is in the England squad?

3

What has Tuchel said?

Tuchel insisted he is focussed on being loyalty to players who are committed to international football after a host of withdrawals before and during the September camp.



"Overall I think the message in the nomination is clear: we trust the team that was with us the [last] two-and-a-half weeks and had such an excellent camp," Tuchel said.

"This is how it is. If you are in camp and you are good and the team is flying, then you have every right to stay with us because you contributed in the right manner and in an excellent way.



"So this is maybe the overall headline."

On the inclusion of 21-year-old Jobe Bellingham, Tuchel pointed towards his form with Lee Carsley's Under-21s after 12 appearances for the Young Lions in the last two years.

He added: "Carsley has been talking highly about Jobe for weeks and months that he deserves - if there is a spot and if there is a possibility - to make an impression in the first team.

"He had good matches and is in good run of form with Dortmund. So he deserves to be with us."

3 King is the latest promising Premier League youngster to get an England call-up Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



Who are England playing?

England host Croatia at Wembley on November 12 before a massive trip to world champions Spain on November 15.

Tuchel's side are all-but certain to qualify for the knockout stages of the Nations League, sitting six points above third-place Croatia with an unassailably-superior goal difference.

The Three Lions have won three of their four matches so far, leaving them three points adrift of Spain - who have a perfect record.

Group winners and runners-up will progress to the quarter-finals - set to be played in March next year - before the Nations League finals in June.

Sports.title: Leicester release statement as porn star becomes ambassador for shirt sponsor
Sports.content:
Leicester release statement as porn star becomes ambassador for shirt sponsor

Leicester have acknowledged 'concerns' after their main shirt sponsor appointed a porn star as a club ambassador.

BC Game has been the Foxes' front-of-shirt sponsor since 2024, and announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador on Tuesday.



4 have had BC Game as their primary shirt sponsor for the last three season Credit: Getty

With BC Game an unlicensed online cryptocurrency gaming platform, their partnership with the League One side has already proved controversial among some supporters.

However, the sponsor drew yet more controversy when it revealed it would be teaming up with pornstar Elfie earlier this week.

Controversial promo video

Announcing the partnership, the online gambling company posted a suggestive video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media.



The innuendo-laden promotional clip shows the adult actress accepting her BC Game contract, and has already been viewed over 6 million times on X.

The post was accompanied by the caption: “Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin.”



This quickly sparked backlash among BC Game's eSports fanbase, as well as Leicester supporters, particularly fan group The Foxes Trust.

In a lengthy statement, the supporters' group said: "Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City."



Leicester issue statement

Following continued backlash over BC Game's partnership, Leicester have since responded and confirmed they were in discussions with the company over a 'mutually acceptable resolution'.

Their statement read: "Leicester City Football Club recognises the concerns raised about recent developments involving our Principal Partner, BC GAME.

"We have raised these concerns directly with BC GAME and are continuing discussions with the company to explore a mutually acceptable resolution."

4 In a promotional clip announcing the partnership, Elfie grabs a delivery driver by the shirt and pulls him inside the room Credit: @bcgame



4 Elfie then poses with her BC Game contract

'Ditching its values'

Leicester's vow to explore the partnership comes amid renewed pressure from the Foxes Trust for their association with BC Game.

The group has previously accused the club of 'ditching its values' over their sponsorship deal with the company, which is based out of Curacao and unlicensed in the United Kingdom.

Earlier this week, the Foxes Trust said: “Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the trust’s dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor.



“BC Game have now announced a new partnership with ‘international content creator and esports personality’ Eva Elfie… who just happens to be an international porn star.

“From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company we felt Leicester City were ditching its values.

“Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content.

4 BC Game was Leicester's main shirt sponsor in their last Premier League campaign Credit: Getty



“Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people’s lives, in particular young people.

“Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?”

Leicester's partnership with BC Game has coincided with a challenging spell for the club on the pitch.

Their first season together - the 2024/25 campaign - saw the Foxes relegated from the Premier League, before they dropped another division to League One last term.



Now managed by Russell Martin, the 2016 English champions have had a mixed start to life in the third tier - initially struggling with just one win in five to pile pressure on their coach, but have since steadied the ship.

Had they stayed in the Premier League two seasons ago, then the partnership with BC Game - which lost its licence to operate in the UK in December 2024 - would no longer be allowed.

Sports.title: What time is the England squad announcement? Thomas Tuchel to reveal team to face Croatia and Spain
Sports.content:
What time is the England squad announcement? Thomas Tuchel to reveal team to face Croatia and Spain

Thomas Tuchel will make his latest England squad announcement this morning, as his team aim for a top-two finish in the Nations League.

After finishing third at this summer’s World Cup, England won three of their opening four League A Group C fixtures across an 11-day period during the extended September/October international break.



4 Kane started in all four of England's games over the extended international break in September and October, scoring six goals Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

The Three Lions had to quickly respond after a defeat to world champions Spain in their opening game with a 7-0 victory against Croatia.

Additionally, captain Harry Kane is set to return to international action for the first time since winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

He is already the nation's all-time top scorer with 91 goals, and will hope to surpass Peter Shilton's 125 appearance record to become England's most-capped player.



But before supporters can catch the Three Lions out on the pitch again, Tuchel must name his next squad.

When will the England squad be announced?

Tuchel will reveal his squad for the upcoming international break today - Friday, November 6.



The squad announcement will be made at 10am.

The Three Lions boss will then hold a press conference to explain the decisions he has made.

talkSPORT will provide you with all the latest updates from the squad confirmation as it unfolds.



England captain Kane will then be joining talkSPORT Drive from 4pm next Wednesday with Andy Goldstein and Darren Bent.

He'll be discussing everything from his record breaking numbers at Bayern Munich, England's upcoming games and, of course, his Ballon d'Or win.

4 Henderson may return to the England setup after impressing for Chelsea after recovering from his arm injury that he picked up at the World Cup Credit: Getty

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.



Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

talkSPORT.com will also reveal the full squad when it is announced.

Additionally, the Under-21s all the way to the Under-18s will also be announced throughout the day.



4 England will hope to beat Luis de la Fuente's side after being beaten in the previous two occasions including one being the Euros final in 2024 Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Who are England playing?

England will welcome Croatia to Wembley Stadium on Thursday, November 12 at 7:45pm.

Tuchel's side will conclude their Nations League group with a trip to Atletico Madrid's Metropolitano Stadium to play Spain on Sunday, November 15.

talkSPORT will have live commentary of both matches.

Following the November international break, there will be a four-month break from England action and they will not return for international duty until March 2027.



The last international break of the 2026/27 campaign falls in June next year, running from Monday, June 7 to Tuesday, 15 June.

Who will Tuchel pick?

England currently sit second in Nations League group with nine points from their opening four matches, three behind leaders Spain who boast a perfect record.

The Three Lions sit six points clear ahead of Croatia in third and know that either a draw or victory against Slaven Bilic's side would guarantee a top-two finish in the group.

Tuchel could use this international break as an opportunity to experiment, despite him likely to select veterans such as Kane, Jordan Pickford, Declan Rice, and Jude Bellingham.



4 De Zerbi's Spurs have now won three games in a row and have risen up the Premier League table after a miserable start Credit: AFP

And, after the England boss gave call ups to Rio Ngumoha and Alex Scott in September's international break, he will likely reward others for their form at club level.

One player who might have a chance is Tottenham's Archie Gray who recently scored the opening goal against Crystal Palace as a makeshift right-back.

Additionally, Everton's Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall may also be given the opportunity to prove himself after sticking with England despite having the option to deflect to Ireland.



So far this season, he has netted two goals and secured one assist in eight appearances in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Leeds have the longest unbeaten home run in the Premier League - from new transfer strategy and napping to choosing 'rough and ready' over 'comfy and nice', this is how they turned Elland Road into a fortress again
Sports.content:
We will know a great deal more about the strength of Tottenham’s revival by mid-afternoon on Saturday. If Roberto De Zerbi’s men can escape one of the toughest venues in English football without taking damage, perhaps he really is on to something. The Elland Road factor is no myth – Leeds United are currently on the longest unbeaten home run of any Premier League side, dating back eight games to a 1-0 reverse against Sunderland on March 3. Since Daniel Farke took over in 2023, only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have more points per game at home. Farke's Leeds have won 44 of 69 games at Elland Road, losing only eight and scoring a whopping 141 goals. After collecting a single point from matches at Sunderland and Bournemouth and failing to score in either, Leeds are desperate to be back in front of their own supporters. Here, Daily Mail Sport looks at how one of England’s most evocative stadiums is baring its teeth again. Reawakening the giant The last time Leeds were in the top flight, their home form was a huge part in their downfall. From 2021-23, Leeds lost nearly half of their home games (16 of 38) and won only nine. The Elland Road factor is no myth. Since Daniel Farke became Leeds United boss in 2023, only Arsenal, Manchester City and Liverpool have more points per game at home Farke's Leeds have won 44 of 69 games at Elland Road, losing only eight and scoring a whopping 141 goals. They are unbeaten there this season, and recently thrashed Newcastle 4-1

Your browser does not support iframes.

Farke and the players were able to set it right in the Championship, where Leeds won 35 of 47 in the following two campaigns including the play-off semi-final against Norwich. In the Premier League, it was always going to be a different story but Farke, his players and the supporters have responded to the challenge. ‘Since we’ve come back up, people realise how important the home record is and how we need to drive the team on,’ says Dan Moylan, co-owner of the Square Ball fan channel who has been going to Elland Road since 1982. ‘We know what we need to do to help the team. A lot of players will come to Elland Road and not fancy it. So many stadiums are too comfy and nice. We need it a bit rough and ready to get behind our team. ’Daniel Farke has galvanised the fanbase in a steady way. It’s not been spectacular, more of a steady building of momentum. There has been a lot of jeopardy with Leeds in recent seasons as they’ve gone through the divisions. There was a lot of anxiety in the Championship years but when the nerves were shredded, fans seemed to get behind the team more.’ Elland Road has always provoked strong reactions. Leeds supporters will always be hostile towards Gary Neville but the former Manchester United defender and Sky Sports pundit knows the value of these old-school sporting cathedrals. ‘Elland Road was unbelievable,’ Neville has said. 'There was a real nastiness and hostility to it, but it’s a proper football club with an incredible crowd. You always knew you were in for a brutal afternoon.’ Pep Guardiola saw the other side of the same coin. The 2021-22 campaign had few joys for Leeds, as they stayed up on the final day of the season. ‘Since I arrived, I heard many times about what Elland Road means,’ he said after Manchester City won 4-0 there in April 2022. 'At the end, 4-0 down, fighting to stay in the Premier League and singing, chanting, showing support. I can imagine how the people feel.’

Your browser does not support iframes.

Leeds prioritised top-flight experience after coming up in 2025, signing players such as Dominic Calvert-Lewin (centre) who can handle a rough atmosphere Calvert-Lewin has scored 12 times at Elland Road since joining in summer 2025 The players To thrive at Elland Road you need players who can handle it when Leeds are struggling – and this was a significant part of their recruitment plan for the Premier League. Mindful of the failures at Elland Road between 2021 and 2023, Leeds took a different approach to recruitment after returning to the Premier League in 2025. To make the most of their home, Leeds decided that top-flight experience was needed. In came players like Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Sean Longstaff and James Justin – battle-hardened Premier League footballers who know what it is to play in spicy atmospheres. These were men who would not wilt when Elland Road was at its most exacting. The groundwork was laid in the Championship. For any home match outside the top flight, Leeds will always be heavy favourites – but this is double-edged. If a match against a low-profile club is still goalless after half an hour, fans start to groan. A couple of misplaced passes later and those groans turn to jeers. It takes a certain kind of character to override those difficulties and in the second tier Leeds found it, racking up 190 points across the two seasons. Before home games, Leeds have followed the same routine under Farke. They will meet at a hotel in the city on the morning of the match and travel by coach to Elland Road. The pre-match meal and final tactical briefings will take place at the hotel and for later kick-offs, players are encouraged to have an afternoon nap. Sleep-deprived players with very young children may opt to stay in the hotel the night before the game. They will arrive at the ground 90 minutes before kick-off. Elland Road is in the initial phase of a major redevelopment project that is designed to take the capacity from around 37,000 to 53,000. That means players now enter the stadium via a different route and can no longer be greeted by fans on their way in. The mystique remains, though. Harry Wilson and Jayden Bogle were in the Derby side who won a spectacular play-off semi-final at Elland Road in May 2019. Both regard it as the best atmosphere they had ever played in and it played a part in their decision to join Leeds. Harry Wilson and Jayden Bogle won a play-off semi-final at Elland Road with Derby in May 2019. Both regard it the best atmosphere they've played in While stadium improvement is crucial, it is just as important that the essence of Elland Road does not slip away The risk and reward Leeds lean heavily on their fanbase when recruiting. About 150,000 turned out in Leeds city centre to celebrate promotion 18 months ago and the club show videos of those scenes to transfer targets. It is all part of the Leeds brand and while stadium improvement is crucial, it is just as important that the essence of Elland Road does not slip away. ‘It depends who can afford to get in,’ adds Moylan. ‘The club need to be careful not to price out supporters and they have to make sure young working-class fans can afford it. ‘I’ve seen the ground pretty raucous and animalistic, going back to the 1990s. Football has changed a lot over the years and the moving of kick-off times doesn’t help but on its day Elland Road now is as good as it’s ever been.’ Tottenham have been warned.

Sports.title: Inside Mohamed Salah's new life after his Liverpool fall-out: LEWIS STEELE visits Turkey's 30th biggest city, where the Egyptian King hikes, drinks salted yoghurt - and still gets hero worship
Sports.content:
Inside Mohamed Salah's new life after his Liverpool fall-out: LEWIS STEELE visits Turkey's 30th biggest city, where the Egyptian King hikes, drinks salted yoghurt - and still gets hero worship

It started just minutes after touchdown in Turkey.

In a taxi journey across Istanbul's intercontinental bridge to Fenerbahce's stadium, the driver took a break from lighting up a cigarette or shouting profanities at other road users. He turned, looked me in the eye, and asked: 'You know Mohamed Salah?'

Two and a half hours after fighting through mind-blowing traffic (think your gridlocked motorway at 5pm multiplied by 100), on arrival at Liverpool's press conference, one gentleman did not even exchange pleasantries. He shoved a selfie stick in my face and asked about Salah.

And these two encounters were 650 miles away from where the Egyptian player now plies his trade. This fandom was only a starter when compared to the main course of Salahmania that greeted us upon arrival in the port city of Trabzon, to the east of Turkey on the coast of the Black Sea.

Here, his face and name were everywhere you looked. 'You come for Salah?' enquired the hotel receptionist. Upon hearing that was indeed the purpose of the visit, he upgraded the room to a superior suite overlooking the ocean. Result.

The streets of this city, which feels a world apart from the bustling metropolis of Istanbul, never mind Liverpool, are packed with antique dealers, and markets selling two-foot-long fish for less than £1 and the local delicacy of hamsi (anchovy to you and me).

Mohamed Salah can relax in Trabzon and has taken multiple hiking trips in the highlands (Source: Instagram/Mohamed Salah)

Fans have now taken to posing at the same spots Salah appeared at - such is their hero worship

Everywhere you turned, there was a nod to Salah. His name was heard in conversations as the melodic call to prayer rang out from the nearby Hagia Sophia mosque, his picture seemed to be hung from every building and his name was on the back of every shirt being sported in town.

Shops were selling mugs, scarves, plates, masks and even cigarette lighters shaped like Salah.

At the futuristic waterfront stadium known as Papara Park, Salahmania continued - with punters putting on impromptu barbecues and DJ sets from beside their cars similar to tailgates in American sports. Everyone in this city was dancing to the beat of the Egyptian King.

Fans, many in Trabzonspor-coloured jester hats with bells on, glowed about Salah. Most do not speak a word of English in this city not far from the Armenian and Georgian border. But those who could summed up the mood.

'We love him, he is going to make us champions,' said one.

Another told us: 'People across the country now support Trabzonspor and people come from other countries, people want us to win just because of Mohamed Salah.'

Trabzonspor supporters told Daily Mail Sport: 'We love him, he is going to make us champions'

Everywhere you turned there was a nod to Salah in his new club's kit

There were plenty of children in the crowd, and more women than expected. Some had come from afar to see him, others could not believe that Salah had chosen their team and hometown.

So, why Trabzon? Why did Salah choose this project in Turkey's 30th biggest city? Why not one of the three Istanbul giants – Fenerbahce, Galatasaray or Besiktas – who have won 28, 27 and 21 Turkish titles respectively, compared to Trabzonspor's seven, including only one since 1984.

The answers are obvious, according to sources. Salah, now 34, wanted a place where he could enjoy his football without the intense scrutiny. Every word and facial expression would generate days of news coverage in Liverpool or Istanbul or another one of Europe's giant cities.

On the outskirts of Trabzon, Salah can relax, hiking up to a group of boulders in Yayla. Even there, he's worshipped, though. Trabzonspor fans flock there to pose for photographs on the same rock where he sat for a photo posted on his Instagram.

Salah's family are settled, he is becoming obsessed with chess and he has started drinking the Turkish salted-yoghurt drink ayran each day.

On the pitch, there is a belief Trabzonspor can beat the big three and end Galatasaray's four-year grip on the title.

The team also stars former Liverpool midfielder Fabinho, ex-Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana and Jerome Boateng, once a stalwart at Bayern Munich. The manager Thomas Reis was poached from Ludogorets and has lost just once since his arrival.

Salah is settled with his family and faces less scrutiny than in Istanbul or Liverpool (Source: Instagram/Mohamed Salah)

Salah has scored 10 goals and assisted five more in his 15 games in Turkey so far

The highlight so far came on September 19, when Salah scored a hat-trick in a 4-0 thumping of Galatasaray. Trabzonspor have won seven league games in a row and will aim to go deep in the Conference League despite Thursday's undeserved 1-0 defeat to Freiburg.

Salah has scored 10 goals and assisted in five more in his 15 games in Turkey.

'Everyone wants to work with a star the size of Mohamed Salah,' striker Paul Onuachu, once of Southampton, told us after that game. 'He is a top guy and a world star.

'He adds so much to us and helps all of us, thanks to his experience and quality, and he contributes positively to the development of our team.

'I am grateful for him. It is a blessing to play with him.'

Salah did not have the rub of the green in the clash with the German side, who were Europa League finalists last year. But a trip to Papara Park underlined an answer to those wondering just why he picked Trabzon and not any of his other mega-money offers.

A man wearing Trabzonspor's claret and light blue colours shows off his support for Salah

A trip to Papara Park underlined an answer to those wondering just why he picked Trabzon

He had approaches from America, and the Saudi Arabian federation tried to sign him right until the day he jetted into Trabzon - where he was greeted by 35,000 fans with fireworks and flares. Besiktas held advanced talks with Salah's agent Ramy Abbas.

But Trabzonspor won the race and Salah is playing with a smile again, even though that face pulled a bit of a grimace when he spotted a familiar face or two from the English press pack waiting for him after the game.

His laugh faded into an expression that said: 'I thought I got rid of you lot pestering me!'

That face confirmed his reason for joining Trabzonspor: Salah is out of the spotlight – certainly while still in with a chance to win trophies and maintain a good level of football until next summer's Africa Cup of Nations.

After a public fall-out with Liverpool that saw the final year of his contract ripped up and him accuse the Anfield club of 'throwing him under the bus', it feels like Salah is feeling at home and happy again.

It's not difficult to turn down the multiple opportunities to buy Salah-branded magnets or shirts or teddies or socks or lighters as we bid farewell to Trabzon, but it is hard to escape the conclusion that the feeling of love is mutual in this football-mad city.

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca backs Gianluigi Donnarumma after Man City No 1's spate of high-profile errors: Latest from Premier League press conferences
Sports.content:
It's the final Premier League gameweek before the international break, and managers up and down the country will be speaking to the press. Daily Mail Sport will bring you all the key news here... Enzo Maresca has not felt the need to dissect Gianluigi Donnarumma's troubling form with Manchester City's No 1 amid a number of high-profile errors. Donnarumma was flat-footed in being beaten at his near post during Wednesday's Champions League win at RB Leipzig, following mistakes against Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa. City's manager does not see the value in raking over the issues with his goalkeeper and believes the Italian's confidence is still high. 'He's good, overall he's good,' Maresca said of Donnarumma's mood. 'He's quite relaxed, in terms of recognising that he has done some mistakes but has made some good saves. Enzo Maresca has not felt the need to dissect Gianluigi Donnarumma's troubling form 'There are players that when they make mistakes you need conversation with them, and there are players that when they make some mistake you just need eye contact to understand that he recognises. 'With Gigio it's quite easy because every time he has made some mistake or something that was not correct, he recognises immediately. Sometimes you don't need to be so deep with some players.' Meanwhile, Maresca insisted that Elliot Anderson has another level to reach after an encouraging start to his City career. The £116million summer signing goes back to Nottingham Forest on Saturday, with Maresca claiming that Oliver Glasner's side are in a false position. 'Elliot can do many [more] things, but he knows that,' Maresca added. 'We had a conversation before the last Champions League game, a nice conversation on understanding the game and slowly he is getting better and better. 'Elliot in this moment is playing more as the holding midfielder, but in future he can also play a little bit more up front.' By Jack Gaughan Arbeloa: Special moment for King Fulham head coach Alvaro Arbeloa has backed Josh King to make the most of his 'special moment' after being called up to the England squad for the first time. The 19-year-old has been selected by Thomas Tuchel for the upcoming Nations League games, having continued to impress this season after being part of England's pre-World Cup camp. 'It is a special moment for him and also for us as a club and our supporters. I think Josh is the pride of our club and supporters,' Arbeloa said at a press conference ahead of Saturday's Premier League game against Newcastle. 'He came to this club when he was eight and now you look at how he is playing and performing, so we are really proud of him. It is a big step for him and I am so happy for him because he is a very humble kid. You can see every day he wants to improve, to work and become a better player.' King will again be central to Fulham's gameplan when Arbeloa's side take on Newcastle looking to build some momentum following last weekend's battling 1-1 draw at Aston Villa. 'For me, he is a very talented player. He can receive between the lines where there is no space,' Arbeloa said. 'He can drive, he can run, he can dribble with the ball, so he has everything, and we are working with him about his finishing. 'Obviously he needs to improve there and it is the most difficult thing in football, scoring goals, but his mentality, his character, he is a very mature player. You can't forget that he is just 19 years old, so it is unbelievable how he is performing. I think he has everything to become one of the best players in the world.' After losing their last home game 1-0 to strugglers Crystal Palace, Arbeloa is expecting a response back at Craven Cottage. 'We know how difficult it will be to beat Newcastle tomorrow, they are a very good team, but we are playing well,' said the Fulham boss, who will be without defender Timothy Castagne because of a knee issue.

Sports.title: Why Enzo Maresca is sticking with 'awe-inspiring' Gianluigi Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show, growing catalogue of errors and a worrying downward trend
Sports.content:
Why Enzo Maresca is sticking with 'awe-inspiring' Gianluigi Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show, growing catalogue of errors and a worrying downward trend

There was a Manchester City fan on Thursday’s Ryanair flight back home from Leipzig wearing a Gianluigi Donnarumma sticker on his coat, portraying the Italian as Don Vito Corleone. The sticker, a bit worn and a bit crumpled, was peeling off. A metaphor exists within that somewhere.

Tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League – beaten at his near post by Ridle Baku's cross for one goal, fumbling another routine effort at the feet of a striker and allowing a straightforward shot to squirm through his fingers – just adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Question marks around Donnarumma’s suitability between the sticks are becoming more pronounced after a catalogue of mistakes this season. One against Paris Saint-Germain when Maghnes Akliouche’s shot was too hot (some would argue two after neglecting his near post for Desire Doue’s opener) and then Nicolas Jackson shooting through him at Aston Villa last month.

Each time, Enzo Maresca has publicly recognised the errors and intimated that nobody needs to rake over them in detail with his No1, who is experienced enough to know he must do better.

Now Leipzig. ‘It’s not a concern,’ Maresca said of the latest gaffe. The manager’s defences of Donnarumma are racking up and what City are witnessing is fundamental problems from somebody described as the best the world has to offer.

Maresca has rejected the idea that summer signing Geronimo Rulli, a 34-year-old Argentina international, could take over the gloves, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’. Rulli understood his lot when joining from Marseille, to feature in domestic cup competitions, and was happy with that.

Gianluigi Donnarumma had a night to forget in Leipzig this week, making at least three individual errors

But Man City boss Enzo Maresca will stand by his goalkeeper, claiming that City line-ups are always ‘Gigio plus 10’

Happy in a way that James Trafford was not, after making it clear that one season as Donnarumma’s understudy was not palatable.

He has flourished at Leeds United so far this season, leading to some observers criticising Hugo Viana for letting him go, only to blunder for a goal at Bournemouth last weekend. Worth remembering that it does happen to all of them at some point.

Trafford did not appear ready for the big time last year when starting the season ahead of the wantaway Ederson and City had their eyes on Donnarumma months before landing him – a £26million deal struck just as Ederson left for Fenerbahce.

Trafford will be ready soon and is pushing Jordan Pickford hard to be England's No1, but definitely wasn’t back then.

With Trafford gone and Maresca seemingly ruling out his No2 taking over – while also making a vague reference to taking stock over the international break – it appears that City would have no option but to stick with Donnarumma if they did actually want to bring about a change. January signings seem remote in the current climate of guilty verdicts and appeals.

But there is something outstanding that Donnarumma does offer, one that does set him apart. Maresca categorised the stunning one-handed save from Leipzig’s Christoph Baumgartner as one nobody else could make.

And while some hyperbole might be at play there, very few could lay claim to producing that kind of moment on a semi-regular basis.

Repelling Baumgartner is up there with Donnarumma’s instinctive save from Bryan Mbeumo at a crucial juncture on debut last year and thwarting Alexis Mac Allister in a victory at Anfield. The sort of awe-inspiring saves thousands pay money to witness.

Very few goalkeepers can claim to make wonder-saves as regularly as Donnarumma does

Donnarumma's impressive shot-stopping in the Premier League is evidenced by this graphic of every shot he has faced since joining City (red circles = goals, blank circles = saves)

Nobody across the Premier League has a higher save percentage than Donnarumma’s 71.5 since his arrival from PSG. More scientifically, only Bart Verbruggen and Senne Lammens have prevented more goals in that time – a metric measured by the xG of shots compared to how many goals were conceded.

Donnarumma has prevented seven goals (1.4 this season), with Brighton’s Verbruggen at 9.7 and Manchester United's Lammens at 8.1 across the same period. These are broadly encouraging numbers for City, despite Donnarumma's save percentage dipping to 69.7 this season – eighth among his peers, with Trafford way out in front on 79.5.

City will need to keep a careful eye on that downward trend from a 27-year-old who they brought to the club to act as the anchor, to bail them out in a way that Ederson struggled. That was the trade-off for his limited footwork, being incapable of playing through the opposition lines in a way the Brazilian could.

The wonder saves cancel all of that out. Donnarumma has been the goalkeeper’s goalkeeper for those alone. But were the certainty around that aspect of his game to waver on a longer-term basis, City should have decisions to make.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel tells Cole Palmer he 'misses too many opportunities' to play for England after leaving Chelsea star out of his latest squad
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel tells Cole Palmer he 'misses too many opportunities' to play for England after leaving Chelsea star out of his latest squad

Thomas Tuchel has warned Cole Palmer he 'misses too many opportunities' to play for England, after leaving him out of his latest squad.

The Chelsea star is a high-profile omission ahead of upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, having withdrawn from duty during the last international break with a minor muscular injury.

England were assured Palmer is 100 per cent fit and ready when they contacted Chelsea this week – with his omission purely down to a selection decision from Tuchel and not to do with any fitness issues.

The German said on Friday: 'I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

'We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress.

'It was a long camp, it was two and a half weeks and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary.

Thomas Tuchel has warned Cole Palmer he misses too many opportunities to play for England

Palmer is a high-profile omission from Tuchel's squad for England's upcoming Nations League games

He withdrew from the last squad, leaving boss Thomas Tuchel questioning his commitment

'That's why the credit goes to them, the trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress.

'So it's not personal and of course we will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.'

Last month Tuchel appeared to question Palmer's desire to represent his country, warning he 'misses way too many camps' as the 24-year-old skipped all four England fixtures in September and October.

Palmer had played a full 90 for Chelsea away at Bournemouth before that break, which he then used to fly abroad to the Caribbean with his girlfriend, Olivia Holder, after withdrawing from England duty.

He was accompanied by a personal rehab coach on that trip, and was provided with an injury-specific training and recovery plan by his club.

Palmer started in Chelsea's first fixture when the Premier League returned at home to Brentford with Blues boss Xabi Alonso insisting they were right to take care of their star player themselves.

It has been described as standard procedure for England to make medical checks on players with clubs. While it does not guarantee a call-up, it indicates how Tuchel has been weighing up offering Palmer another chance as he names his next squad on Friday morning.

Sports.title: Mum rushes to goalkeeper in Spanish football's killer collision: Jesus Owono suffering 'hardest days of his life' and being comforted after striker he clashed with died from 'chest trauma'
Sports.content:
Mum rushes to goalkeeper in Spanish football's killer collision: Jesus Owono suffering 'hardest days of his life' and being comforted after striker he clashed with died from 'chest trauma'

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono's doting mum has rushed to Andorra to comfort him as he endures the 'hardest days of his life' following his death clash with a rival striker whose funeral took place yesterday.

Maria del Carmen Owono Mangue made the five-and-a-half-hour drive from her home in the Basque city of San Sebastian to Andorra where her 25-year-old son currently plays his football after learning Jesus de Miguel had lost his fight for life in a Tenerife hospital.

She and the Andorra FC keeper have been deeply close since he moved to San Sebastian from their native Equatorial Guinea as an eight-year-old boy to rejoin her after she had emigrated earlier in search of work to provide for her family and an aunt had taken the youngster into her home.

Owono, the eldest of six siblings, has admitted of his arrival in a new country: 'I came in pursuit of a dream, not the dream of playing football, but the dream of being with my mother.'

His mum has confessed: 'Waking up in the morning and seeing your child doing what they love most is a mother's greatest joy.'

She said in the same interview when the goalkeeper was just 20 in comments which could now come back to haunt the family: 'He needs to keep working. We still don't know what will happen. If God allows things to turn out well for him and if not, well, you know that he has worked hard and done what he could.'

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono is suffering and being comforted after his killer collision

Owono, who has closed his social media accounts, has had his mother rush to his side in the days following Jesus de Miguel's death (Source: Instagram)

Overnight one of Jesus' younger brothers confirmed their mum was by his side in Andorra.

Speaking from the second-floor four-bed apartment she owns in a tree-lined street in a middle-class residential neighbourhood east of San Sebastian's city centre, he said: 'We're all very distraught. My mum has gone to be with Jesus because he is suffering.'

A source close to the goalkeeper added: 'Maria del Carmen is one of the most important, if not the most important, people in Jesus' life.

'He had a difficult start being separated from his mum at such an early age and it was very difficult for her too.

'They have been inseparable since Jesus moved to Spain as an eight-year-old.

'Maria del Carmen has helped him integrate into completely new surroundings and supported him every step of the way on his road to becoming a professional footballer.

De Miguel and Owono collided - and hours later the former died of 'accidental chest trauma'

De Miguel's team-mates are pictured arriving at his funeral in Navahermosa on Thursday

'It's only natural that she'd want to be by his side now when by his own admission he's in pieces and finding it impossible to come to terms with the fact a fellow footballer has died because of something he did.'

LETTER OF SUPPORT Dear Jesus Owono: From the FC Andorra supporters' section, we want to send you all our support and love during these tough and difficult times. We are aware of the suffering you are going through after what happened. We know these aren't easy days, but we want you to remember one thing: you are not alone. You have your family, your friends, your team-mates, the staff, and the entire club by your side. But you also have us, a fanbase that appreciates you, respects you, and today, more than ever, wants to send you all our love and support. We also want you to know that we categorically reject all the insults, threats, and judgments you've been receiving lately. An accident doesn't define a person, much less their character. We don't want the pain, anger, or helplessness to turn into hatred towards you. Behind the footballer is a person, with feelings and a family who are also suffering. We want you to know that this is your home. When you return to the pitch, to defend our goal and wear this jersey again, you'll have a stand that will still be by your side, cheering you on as always. Now you don't have to prove anything to anyone. It won't be easy and it will take time, but even though it's difficult and painful, we have to move forward, we have to work to recover that fighting spirit and smile that are so characteristic of you. The most important thing now is your recovery, but along the way, know that you can count on us, that you're not alone. Stay strong, Jesus. We're with you. Our Spider Man today, tomorrow, and always.

Some of Owono's Andorra FC team-mates and members of the club's supporters' group have also paid him a visit to deliver a letter of encouragement.

The letter refers to the goalkeeper as 'their Spiderman,' 'his joy,' and 'a person with feelings and a strong family connection.'

Owono was red-carded after kneeing the 30-year-old CD Tenerife striker in the chest in a reckless tackle late into stoppage time during a second-division match on Monday.

The match was suspended when the two sides were drawing 2-2.

Tragic Jesus, whose partner Marta Fernandez and one-year-old daughter Carla were watching from the stands, was reportedly revived by paramedics on the pitch after going into cardiac arrest before being rushed to hospital.

His club confirmed around 9.30am local time on Tuesday he had died about 8am the same day, saying they were 'heartbroken' and had a 'lump in their throats' after revealing earlier the footballer's neurological condition had worsened.

A post-mortem concluded in a preliminary report his death was consistent with 'accidental chest trauma' although the results of further tests conducted during the autopsy are still pending.

Owono used 'excessive force' while contesting the ball near the half-way line according to the match referee's report.

He is facing a lengthy ban and possible criminal charges after police in Tenerife confirmed homicide squad officers were looking into whether had committed an involuntary manslaughter.

Legal experts have cast doubt on the possibility of prosecution because the clash that resulted in Jesus de Miguel's death occurred during open play.

The first photos of the dead footballer's partner emerged overnight as his team-mates prepared to travel to the small town of Navahermosa, 80 miles south-west of Madrid, where his devastated parents come from.

Jesus' mum and dad made the return trip after jetting to Tenerife to try to reach their son before he died in hospital on Tuesday morning hours after his clash with Owono.

The father was watching the match in a bar in his home town when he saw him slump to the ground.

Equatorial Guinea international Owono, who turned round as he headed back to the dressing rooms following his sending off and walked back to the player he had hurt after realising how seriously injured the Tenerife frontman was, broke his silence on Wednesday.

The father of De Miguel, is hugged at his son's wake, three days on from his death

The football world has rallied behind De Miguel and his family with tributes to the striker

A neighbour said De Miguel's father (pictured right, with his mother, girlfriend and sister R-L) burst into tears after seeing the impact of the collision on television. (Source: Instagram/martitamig)

He released a statement via his club that said: 'These are the most difficult days of my life.

'I am struggling to find the words, and it is very hard for me to process anything that has happened.

'I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesus. I am thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

'I know there will be many matters to address, and I will face whatever comes with complete respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything other than Jesus and the grief we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'

FC Andorra, reacting to news of the Tenerife striker's death in hospital, said on Tuesday morning: 'Heartbroken and devastated, we wish to extend our deepest condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his colleagues and friends, and to CD Tenerife.

'May he rest in peace.'

Sports.title: 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!': Kevin De Bruyne at centre of Napoli dressing room meltdown as 'divided' squad lurches towards 'disaster'... with an 'every man for himself' culture setting in at Italian giants
Sports.content:
'Why are you speaking? F*** off!': Kevin De Bruyne at centre of Napoli dressing room meltdown as 'divided' squad lurches towards 'disaster'... with an 'every man for himself' culture setting in at Italian giants

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' repeatedly during Napoli's 4-1 thrashing against Porto on Wednesday, with a dressing room crisis heating up at the club.

The Napoli squad has become increasingly fractured in recent weeks, according to the Italian media, with an 'every man for himself' culture developing into a 'disaster'.

Napoli sit eighth in Serie A under new manager Massimiliano Allegri – just two seasons after winning the title under Antonio Conte – and are near the bottom of the Champions League table after three defeats in four games.

Their cracks are showing on the pitch, with striker Lorenzo Lucca yelling at De Bruyne: 'Why are you speaking? F*** off!' during their Porto drubbing.

The pair squared up to each other and Lucca shouted his expletive command three times before they went their separate ways.

After the match, Matteo Politano told Sky Sport Italia: 'It would be nice if a few other teammates came here to give an explanation and not just us Italians, but never mind, I never hide my face.'

Kevin De Bruyne was told to 'f*** off' three times by team-mate Lorenzo Lucca during Napoli's 4-1 defeat by Porto on Wednesday

There is said to be a rift developing between Napoli's native stars and foreign players

La Gazzetta dello Sport reported that Politano was calling out Cameroonian star Frank Anguissa and Kosovan Amir Rrahmani, both two-time title winners with the club.

Politano added: 'The attitude is one that a team like ours cannot have at this level. I was not attacking anyone, we have a squad that is struggling, but we need to come together and think about this next game before the break for international duty.

'Hopefully we can recover a few players during that spell and then our season can really begin.'

There is a 'divide' between the Italian group of players and foreigners, La Gazzetta dello Sport reports, though it is mostly down to frustration with results.

Individuals such as De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund, and Stanislav Lobotka are more 'reserved personalities' who have reportedly not bonded as well with their team-mates away from the field.

Scott McTominay, who has an ally in fellow Scottish player Billy Gilmour, said after the Porto loss: 'Of course I’m angry.

'We lost 4-1 in the Champions League; there’s nothing to smile about. For us, it’s go on and try to figure out how to fix it.

'We’ve had a lot of injuries, a lot of important players you can’t change; attacking players as well. Let’s not beat around the bush; we’ve got a lot of injuries, and that makes a big difference whenever you come into play every three days.

Napoli have had a rough start to the season under new manager Massimiliano Allegri - despite him being a legendary coach in Italy

'So, things like these can make a huge difference for the team when the same players are playing over and over again. People need to understand that, but we also need to do better. First and foremost, we need to do better, injuries in football are part of it, but we have too many.'

Napoli have nine players out injured.

Their dressing room troubles have dragged on for a while. Last season, Conte complained of a lack of unity after they signed nine players on the back of their Scudetto. They still managed to finish second, but it was a turbulent ride.

'Nine new players were too many. We weren't balanced,' he said at the time.

'I experience the dressing room every day, so I say certain things; we mustn't despair. We'll try to recreate last year's chemistry.'

In one match against AC Milan, De Bruyne threw a tantrum after being subbed off by Conte.

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson: The day the NHS saved my life
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson: The day the NHS saved my life

Fergie, 84, took over as manager of Manchester United 40 years ago, on November 6, 1986. He went on to transform not only the fortunes of a footballing giant, but the game itself

Sir Alex Ferguson reacts to the stupidest question in the world

Sir Alex Ferguson has paid an emotional tribute to the NHS staff who saved his life in a moving new memoir.

‌



‌



As the legendary Manchester United manager celebrates 40 years since he took the helm at Old Trafford, he admits that he is only here to tell the story of his remarkable life thanks to the miracle of the NHS and the dedication of its staff.

‌



Fergie, 84, took over as manager of Manchester United on November 6, 1986. He went on to transform not only the fortunes of a footballing giant, but the game itself.

‌



He managed the club for 26 years until his retirement at the end of the 2012–13 season.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

During his time at Old Trafford, he won 38 major trophies, including 13 Premier League titles and two UEFA Champions League titles.

‌



View 6 Images Sir Alex Ferguson with his late wife Cathy: his latest memoir is dedicated to her (Image: Macmillan)

Arsenal star on Real Madrid radar as injuries and squad depth could force his hand READ MORE :

He is rightly lauded as the greatest manager of all time. But in his new book, 'Games of My Life,' he tells how he almost died after suffering a brain haemorrhage following Manchester United's match against Arsenal in May 2018.

‌



The first 'Game of his Life' was his return to Old Trafford four months later, accompanied by a medical team including neurosurgeon Dr Alexandru Cotici.

A grateful Fergie describes how Cotici was careful not to touch a drink throughout the match and went straight to Salford Royal to start a shift after the final whistle.

‌



He tells his readers: "It is that sort of commitment from doctors, nurses and hospital staff all over the United Kingdom that helps millions of people a year.

"Without them, I wouldn't be writing these words."

‌



View 6 Images Govan High team Sir Alex is front row second from the right) (Image: Macmillan)

He also recounts how his late wife Cathy, who died in 2023, saved him.

‌



His latest memoir is dedicated to her, with the words, "For 59 years she was my everything."

On the day of his collapse due to the brain haemorrhage, he got out of bed "with a savage headache".

‌



"It prevented me from sleeping most of the night, and promptly collapsed against a shoe rack," he adds. Cathy heard him collapse, and he was rushed to Macclesfield Hospital about 20 minutes later, then to Salford Royal.

He did not come around until the next day. He was asked a series of questions, including whether he had met the Queen and how many wives Henry VIII had.

‌



View 6 Images Sir Alex 1960s while at St Johnson FC (Image: Macmillan)

He joked: "I had indeed met the Queen, but I didn't remember meeting Henry VIII - or any of his wives." He goes on: "On the day they operated on me at Salford Royal, four other patients had surgery for the same complaint.

‌



"Only two of us lived to tell the tale."

Sir Alex's autobiography, published in 2013, sold more than a million in the UK alone and was one of the fastest-selling non-fiction books of all time, with 115,000 copies flying off the shelves in the first week.

‌



For his latest work, he selected 21 games that were 'particularly meaningful,' taking him back to different points in his life.

View 6 Images Sir Alex Ferguson and his wife Cathy arrive at The Orange British Academy Film Awards (BAFTAs) at the Odeon Leicester Square on February 19, 2006 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Rather than writing of the "big games" with United, he has gone back to those matches which 'mean so much' on his personal journey.

The first is his return to Old Trafford after his operation: Manchester United against Wolves.

‌



He recalls: "It was one of the most memorable days of my life. As well as being able to thank all the people who saved my life, the reception I received from those in the crowd at Old Trafford that day meant more to me than anything.

"It meant more than being in Aberdeen after we won the European Cup Winners Cup, more than during the various ticker-tape parades while I managed United, and more than at the end of the last game of my career.

‌



"Without a great deal of luck, I would never have seen that match."

It was not just luck, but "an astonishing number of people" who came to save his life that day.

‌



He goes on: "Between 75 and 85 percent of people over 60 who have an incident like mine die. I survived because my wife Cathy was downstairs when she heard all the shoes come clattering down from the shoe rack on the wooden floor above.

"If she hadn't been there, the referee in the sky might have blown the final whistle for me. Cathy had been due to travel to London a couple of hours later, so I was lucky she was still home.

‌



"She immediately called my son Jason who lives nearby. He rushed over and phoned Steve McNally, United's doctor, who on hearing that I had been having headaches thought that I might be suffering from a brain bleed."

View 6 Images Sir Alex Ferguson and wife Cathy after he was knighted by the Queen in 1999 (Image: PA)

‌



Fergie did indeed have a subdural hematoma, or bleeding on the brain, as shown by scans taken on May 5, 2018.

By September 22 of that year, doctors finally gave him the go ahead to return to Old Trafford for the Wolves game.

‌



In the 27th minute, the entire crowd stood to mark his 27 years as United boss, and sang his name. One banner read: 'Every single one of us loves Alex Ferguson.'

"I was greeted as if I had returned from the dead which, in a way, was true," he writes.

‌



"Many of the stories that were printed after the news spread of my brain injury read like premature obituaries.

View 6 Images Sir Alex with wife Cathy and twins Jason and Darren in 1977 (Image: SSPL via Getty Images)

‌



"It was an extraordinary feeling one that I had never previously experienced in all the years that had taken me from the tenements of Govan to Buckingham Palace.

"When you are lying in a hospital bed, it is all too easy to think the rest of the world never knew you existed. It was so touching, I could hardly breathe. It got right inside me."

‌



Sir Alex was accompanied by a team of medics to the Old Trafford game and admitted that he was so overcome with emotion at the end, he had to go home and go straight to bed.

In his final chapter, Sir Alex reflects: "I am not one to dwell on what maker has in store for me, nor am I afraid of dying.

Article continues below

"I'm much more interested in squeezing the most out of life. "

Games of My Life, By Alex Ferguson with Michael Moritz, is available in hardback, ebook and audio

Sports.title: Bayern Munich 'line up Rio Ngumoha transfer' after being rejected by Man Utd star
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich 'line up Rio Ngumoha transfer' after being rejected by Man Utd star

Bayern Munich are on the lookout for attacking reinforcements in January and seem to have set their sights on Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha

View 3 Images Liverpool star Rio Ngumoha is reportedly of interest to Bayern Munich (Image: Getty)

Bayern Munich will reportedly renew their interest in Liverpool star Rio Ngumoha ahead of the January transfer window. The 18-year-old has established himself as a mainstay in the Reds' first-team squad.

‌



Ngumoha is one of the Premier League's brightest young talents and has made 13 appearances in all competitions so far this season. He's also started all four of Liverpool's Champions League games and provided two assists whilst dazzling in last month's 4-3 win over Villarreal.

The teenager has mostly been used as a substitute in the Premier League, but has featured in all but two games so far this campaign. His performances have earned him a place in Thomas Tuchel's latest England squad for the upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain.

Bayern reportedly showed interest in Ngumoha in the summer, but the Reds swiftly rebuffed any approach. Ismael Saibari was signed instead. However, German outlet BILD now reports that Bayern are keen to sign a back-up to Luis Diaz and are targeting a young attacker to do just that. Ngumoha is said to be on the list of targets.

Liverpool need to accept Alisson and Virgil van Dijk reality before it's too late READ MORE :

According to the report, Ngumoha is admired. Other targets for Bayern include FC Porto's Oskar Pietuszewski, Bournemouth's Eli Junior Kroupi and Borussia Monchengladbach's Wael Mohya. Pietuszewski is the name at the top of the list, as per the report.

View 3 Images Ngumoha has started all of Liverpool's Champions League matches this season (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Renewed interest in Ngumoha comes after Bayern appear to have missed out on signing Manchester United star JJ Gabriel. The 16-year-old is closing in on a move to Real Madrid after deciding to leave United.

Gabriel requested to exit Old Trafford back in September after growing frustrated at waiting for his first-team opportunity. Bayern were one of the teams linked with Gabriel, but it seems he has opted for a move to Spain.

He is one of the most highly-rated youngsters in European football. In his three appearances for United's youth sides this season, he has scored five times and provided two assists, including a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League clash vs Sabah.

View 3 Images Gabriel looks bound for Real Madrid (Image: Getty)

But Ngumoha is equally as exciting, especially if Reds boss Andoni Iraola's words are considered. Speaking after the win over Villarreal, Iraola was full of praise for Ngumoha: "I'm happy with his attitude because he's eager to improve the things that we think he needs to improve. He's eager to add more things to his game.

"He has changed the sides a lot and has played a lot on the right lately. He's feeling so comfortable now and he's adding even some shots with the left [foot] that he hasn't scored but he's getting there and if he can add these small things to his game it will put him in an even better position.
