How Nigeria reached the final

Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match.

They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1.

The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final.

Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final.

Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition.

How Japan reached the final

Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal.

Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory.

They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea.

Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final.

Players to watch

For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats.

Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition.

Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions.

What the coaches and captains said

Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy.

“We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.”

Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter.

“We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. Now we have just one more match to win, and we’re determined to make history.”

Nigeria coach Akeem Busari said his team would approach the final with the same mentality they displayed against DPR Korea.

“It’s just about showing the same character and playing the same way we played with North Korea, because they play with the same philosophy. They want to build the ball, they look at the high line of passes, they want their full-backs to support, so we really want to look at all that. I’m excited and I’m happy, but we just really want to pick up the trophy. That would be the icing on the cake.”

Queen Joseph described reaching the final as a privilege and said the team were representing the entire continent.

“I feel very happy. Playing in the final is a big privilege, representing my country in the final is a big privilege for me. I’m super proud of myself and my team because we made history. We are not here just representing Nigeria; we are here representing Africa as a whole.”

Key facts ahead of the final

Japan will play their 50th match in the history of the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

Only DPR Korea, who will face Brazil in the third-place match, have played more matches in the competition.

Nigeria are the first African nation to reach the U-17 Women’s World Cup final.

Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai will become the competition’s record appearance-maker among coaches, with Saturday’s final marking his 16th match.

A victory for Nigeria would make the Flamingos the first team to lose their opening match and subsequently go on to win the tournament.

Vanguard News

World.title: NaijAidUK Marks 10 Years, Trains 8,000 Nigerians in Life-Saving Skills
World.content:
Funmi Ogundare

NaijAidUK, through its HealthAid charity initiative, has trained more than 8,000 healthcare professionals and members of the public in first aid and emergency response over the past decade, as part of efforts to strengthen Nigeria’s emergency preparedness and save lives.

The organisation disclosed this as it marked its 10th anniversary with a four-day specialised training programme in Lagos, designed to equip healthcare workers, students and members of the public with practical skills to respond to medical emergencies and mental health challenges.

The programme, held from October 27 to 30, 2026, featured Immediate Life Support (ILS) training for clinicians, mental health awareness training and two days of general first emergency response training.

Speaking on the anniversary and the initiative, the Chief Executive Officer and Founding Trustee of NaijAidUK, Dr. Lanre Nehan-Babalola, noted that the organisation was committed to building a network of trained individuals capable of responding to emergencies and transferring life-saving knowledge to others.

She said the train-the-trainer programme was designed to create a multiplier effect by empowering participants to extend their knowledge to families, schools and communities.

“The essence of our train-the-trainer programme is to empower people with the skills to save lives and, more importantly, equip them to pass that knowledge on to others. We believe in training one and saving many.

“Emergency response is not just an activity; it is a culture of knowing the right things to do at the right time,” she said.

Nehan-Babalola emphasised the need to integrate physical and mental health into emergency preparedness, noting that participants were trained to recognise when individuals required support, respond appropriately and seek professional assistance before situations deteriorated.

The programme received commendation from stakeholders in the health sector, including the Director of Nursing, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Omowunmi Folashade Ekong, who described the training as a timely intervention for improving awareness and community support.

She stated that the training had equipped participants with the knowledge to recognise stressors, identify early signs of emotional and mental health challenges, provide appropriate support and direct individuals requiring further attention to professional care.

She added: “The knowledge acquired would benefit homes, schools, workplaces and the wider society.”

Similarly, the Director of Ogun State Ambulance and Emergency Services, Dr. Festus Adetonwa, who represented the state Commissioner for Health, commended NaijAidUK for addressing mental health and first aid, describing them as critical areas requiring greater attention in the country’s healthcare system.

He noted that the first few minutes following an accident, collapse or medical emergency could significantly determine the outcome, stressing the need to equip ordinary citizens with life-saving skills to provide immediate assistance before the arrival of an ambulance.

Adetonwa also called for greater efforts to tackle mental health stigma and encourage people to seek appropriate support.

“These initiatives align with the government’s commitment to strengthening emergency medical services and promoting preventive, people-centred healthcare. The Ministry of Health fully identifies with this effort and encourages its sustainability,” he said.

Established in 2015, NaijAidUK interventions have also included donations of medical equipment, professional development for healthcare workers and community-focused health initiatives aimed at strengthening healthcare delivery in Nigeria.

The organisation’s clinical and emergency response courses include UK-certified programmes delivered by qualified clinical experts based and trained in the United Kingdom, in alignment with World Health Organisation (WHO) guidelines and recognised best practices.

It has also extended its interventions to underserved communities through initiatives such as Project ACT, which adapts first aid education to improve access for people with hearing and speech impairments.

The anniversary programme also featured the Executive Chairman of Ose Local Government Area, Ondo State, Clement Kolapo Ojo, as a guest, underscoring the importance of government and community participation in expanding access to life-saving knowledge.

As part of its next phase, the organisation called for stronger collaboration with government institutions, healthcare organisations, schools, businesses and community stakeholders to expand access to first aid and mental health education across the country.

The charity reaffirmed its commitment to promoting a society where emergency preparedness is a shared responsibility and more citizens possess the knowledge and practical skills to respond when lives are at risk.

World.title: Military Pension Board Honours 98-Year-Old Veteran, Ewemiwe, in Delta
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Military Pensions Board (MPB) has honoured a 98-year-old former Warrant Officer, Echenim Emmanuel Ewemiwe, at Ute-Erumu, near Agbor, in Ika North East Local Government Area of Delta State.

The Board’s delegation, led by its Chairman, Major General Julius Ehioze Osifo, also included Navy Commodore Galadima Ciroma, Director of Navy Pensions; Squadron Leader Aliyu Muhammed; and Captain Robertson Akpojovwo, Chairman of the Delta State Legion.

According to a statement by the Board’s Public Relations Officer, Squadron Leader Aliyu Mohammed, the visit was a special gesture to celebrate the veteran’s 98th birthday.

“It was a remarkable milestone and an opportunity for the Board’s leadership to identify with one of Nigeria’s oldest military veterans. The birthday celebration featured colourful cultural performances, traditional dances and the presence of family members, friends and well-wishers who gathered to celebrate the veteran’s life and legacy,” the statement said.

Speaking at the event, Major General Osifo acknowledged the sacrifices and contributions of military veterans across the country, reaffirming the Board’s commitment to their welfare and well-being.

He noted that the welfare of veterans remained a priority for the Board.

The Board’s spokesperson said other dignitaries at the event included the traditional ruler, the Aruwe of Ute-Erumu; members of the clergy; and other community leaders.

In a vote of thanks, the family’s representative and former Master Warrant Officer, Chuks Echenim, expressed appreciation to the chairman for travelling to Delta State to celebrate with their father and honour him on his special day.

The visit underscores the Military Pensions Board’s recognition of the sacrifices made by military veterans and its commitment to upholding their dignity, honouring their service and identifying with them beyond the administration of pensions.

World.title: 2027: Imansuagbon Decries Court Judgment Nullifying ADC Leadership
World.content:
* Don’t set Nigeria on fire, he says

A stalwart of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Edo State and former governorship aspirant, Ken Imansuagbon, Friday warned that the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the party’s leadership could plunge Nigeria into chaos and anarchy, describing it as a clear attempt to cripple the opposition and set the nation’s democracy on fire.

Imansuagbon, who condemned the judgment, said it was a desperate political move capable of triggering a national conflagration, warning that the consequences could threaten the unity and stability of the country.

“Don’t set Nigeria on fire. This judgment is an invitation to chaos and anarchy. It is a desperation taken too far, whether now or tomorrow,” he declared.

He described the ruling as a “bobby trap that won’t catch anything,” insisting that any attempt to prevent the ADC from participating in the 2027 elections was bound to fail.

“The government must not use power to intimidate its citizens. Nigerians have sacrificed so much to keep this country together, and any attempt to plunge the nation into chaos will be resisted,” he said.

The ADC chieftain called on the international community to intervene urgently to safeguard Nigeria’s democracy, alleging that the judiciary was being subjected to political pressure under President Bola Tinubu.

“Today, the courts are becoming repressive under his watch against the people and democracy. The military never did this. Nigerians must rise against those who want to destroy this country,” he stated.

Imansuagbon also warned against attempts to stop former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, whom he described as the only candidate capable of rescuing Nigeria from its current downward trajectory under the Tinubu administration.

“Atiku is the candidate who can rescue this country from the downward trend under the Tinubu presidency,” he said, urging the Court of Appeal to “do the needful” and protect the party’s participation in the electoral process.

He further cautioned that the ruling could threaten national unity, saying: “For me, I fear for the unity of this country because this judgment is setting up a conflagration capable of consuming the entire nation. Nigeria is bigger than the personal ambition of any individual, group or political class. The people must be resilient and defend democracy.”

Drawing parallels with authoritarian African leaders, Imansuagbon questioned the legacy President Tinubu intended to leave behind, referencing former Zairean leader, Mobutu Sese Seko, and Cameroonian President, Paul Biya.

He also criticised the administration’s economic policies, including the tax law, saying: “The poverty and suffering are too much. The government must remember that power is not permanent. Tinubu should prepare to vacate the presidency by next year.”

A Federal High Court in Abuja, presided over by Justice Peter Lifu, had Thursday nullified the leadership of the ADC led by former Senate President David Mark and the process through which former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar emerged as the party’s presidential candidate.

Imansuagbon expressed confidence that the ruling would not survive appellate scrutiny, declaring: “We still have a few credible judges at the Supreme Court. The attempt to keep ADC off the ballot will fail. The country belongs to all of us, and what matters most is the Nigerian people.”

World.title: Victoria Island Power: The 40 MW Plant Rewriting the Rules of Commercial Power in Lagos
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Elektron Energy’s 40mw Victoria Island Power project is advancing towards commercial operation in Q1 2027. Backed by institutional capital, international engineering expertise and growing commercial demand, the project demonstrates how strategic partnerships, disVictoria Island Power: The 40 MW Plant Rewriting the Rules of Commercial Power in Lagos

ciplined execution and purpose-built infrastructure can deliver more reliable electricity to one of Nigeria’s most important commercial centres.

At the aerial view of the Victoria Island Power Plant, where construction is progressing ahead of planned commercial operations at the Victoria Island Power Plant in Lagos, three Wärtsilä gas engines have been installed, marking a significant milestone in the development of a major new power generation facility.

Supporting infrastructure, from treatment facilities to electrical systems, continue to advance, while a dedicated 12.6-kilometre underground network has been developed to distribute electricity to businesses across one of Nigeria’s most important commercial centres. In September 2026, the project achieved another significant milestone when the Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC) granted Elektron Energy a generation licence, strengthening the project’s regulatory foundation as construction and preparations for commercial operation advance.

The project’s significance lies in the problem it is built to solve. For decades, unreliable electricity has been one of the defining costs of doing business in Nigeria. The scale of the challenge was laid bare in mid-October 2026, when national grid generation fell from 3,840mw to 476.7mw within six hours – an 87.6% drop that triggered outages across the country. Such disruptions expose a deeper commercial problem: businesses must not only contend with interruptions to supply but also absorb the capital, fuel, maintenance and operating costs of maintaining alternative power systems.

For many businesses, the cost of an unstable grid is not only the risk of disruption but also the ongoing expense of securing their own backup supply. Even in Victoria Island, home to many of the country’s largest banks, multinationals, hotels and commercial towers, businesses have been left to generate their own electricity. Diesel generators, fuel storage and maintenance contracts are now a standard cost of doing business on the Island, consuming capital, management time and contingency planning that could be spent elsewhere.

Elektron Energy believes there is a better way: Its approach is to address the challenge at scale: develop dedicated, professionally managed power infrastructure around concentrated commercial demand, enabling businesses to access reliable electricity without each having to maintain extensive and expensive independent generation systems. With more than a decade of experience developing, financing, owning and operating energy infrastructure, Elektron has established capabilities spanning project development, engineering, commercial structuring and long-term operations.

Its portfolio includes infrastructure supplying critical government facilities in Alausa and dedicated power solutions supporting Rack Centre, one of Nigeria’s important data centre facilities. Victoria Island Power builds on this experience, extending Elektron’s established model of purpose-built generation and reliable power delivery to a wider commercial customer base, with an initial capacity of 40mw and the potential to expand to 70mw. Where the project stands, building a power plant involves far more than installing engines. Developers must prove demand, secure land and permits, raise finance, procure technology, arrange fuel, lay distribution lines, sign customers and satisfy regulators – and each piece has to fit the others.

Developed by Elektron in partnership with Eko Power, Victoria Island Power has translated years of planning, technical development and commercial structuring into substantial physical infrastructure. With its generation engines installed and key supporting systems progressing, the project is moving through the final stages of development towards inauguration and commercial operation. The project is currently 56.39% complete, with significant progress recorded across civil, mechanical and electrical works.

Civil construction has reached 67.31% completion, while mechanical and electrical installations stand at 46% and 26.26% respectively. Work is also progressing on the upgrade of the existing Eko Power substation, strengthening the infrastructure required to support electricity distribution to connected customers. With the three Wärtsilä gas engines installed, the next phase of work will focus on mechanical testing and completion activities, alongside substantial completion of outstanding infrastructure works.

These activities form part of the project’s preparations for provisional acceptance, bringing Victoria Island Power closer to commercial operation in Q1 2027. Three Wärtsilä gas engines are installed at Elektron Energy’s 40mw Victoria Island Power Plant. Wärtsilä, the Finnish energy technology group, is the project’s engineering, procurement and construction contractor and its long-term operations and maintenance partner, an arrangement that ties the company’s expertise to the plant’s performance over many years, not just to its delivery.

Victoria Island Power’s strength lies in its integrated infrastructure model, bringing together dedicated generation capacity, an underground distribution network and long-term commercial arrangements with customers. Rather than treating electricity generation and delivery as separate challenges, the project has been developed as a coordinated system in which infrastructure investment is aligned with clearly identified commercial demand.

The partnerships behind the project infrastructure of this scale is rarely delivered by one organisation. It takes a coalition of technical and financial partners, each bringing capabilities the others do not have. Elektron’s partnership with Eko Power, a key partner in the project, combines complementary expertise in power generation and distribution-sector capability.

Wärtsilä brings internationally proven technology and operating support. The project’s financing and investment structure brings together institutional participation and financial support from ARM-Harith Infrastructure Fund, InfraCredit, Africa Finance Corporation, Stanbic IBTC, the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority and the Bank of Industry (BoI), reflecting the institutional relationships required to develop commercially viable power infrastructure at scale.

For such institutions, technical feasibility is only the starting point. Long-term capital depends on more than sound engineering. It requires predictable revenue, appropriately managed risk and a commercial structure that aligns financing, construction, fuel supply, customer commitments and operational performance over the life of the asset. As Nigeria seeks more private investment in electricity, projects that can demonstrate both sound engineering and bankability will do much to sustain investor confidence. For Elektron, the ability to originate projects and assemble this kind of coalition is the core of its business.

Commercial Demand: The Customers Behind the Investment.

The commercial strength of a power project is measured not only by how much electricity it can generate but by the demand it has secured. Victoria Island Power has attracted approximately 25 customer commitments across banking, hospitality, telecommunications, commercial property and professional services within its portfolio. Each with needs that differ. A hotel must keep guest services running around the clock; a bank must protect sensitive systems and business continuity; a landlord needs dependable services to attract and keep tenants; telecoms and digital businesses depend on constant power for critical systems.

What they share is a need for supply they can plan around, and a desire to spend less of their capital and attention generating their own. Securing long-term customer commitments is central to the project’s investment proposition. Contracted electricity demand provides greater visibility over future revenues, supporting the financial structures required to develop and operate capital-intensive power infrastructure.The project’s potential benefits extend beyond its immediate customer base.

By enabling connected businesses to reduce their reliance on diesel generation, it offers the prospect of lower local emissions and noise, while more dependable electricity can support productivity, operational resilience and the attractiveness of commercial properties.

According to Victoria Island Power’s projections, customers connected to the network could achieve savings of up to 40% compared with diesel-generated power, while the plant’s gas-fired embedded generation technology is expected to produce up to 50% less carbon dioxide than diesel alternatives. Beyond these financial and environmental benefits, reliable electricity supply also reduces the operational burden of managing generators, fuel procurement and maintenance, allowing customers to direct more resources towards their core operations.

By developing shared power infrastructure around concentrated commercial demand, Victoria Island Power introduces a more coordinated and scalable alternative to the conventional model of individual businesses investing heavily in their own generation capacity. Its significance lies not only in the customers it will serve, but in the wider possibilities it creates for commercial power delivery in Lagos. Advancing Lagos’s New Electricity Market Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC) during an official visit to Victoria Island Power Victoria Island Power is arriving at an important moment for Nigeria’s electricity sector.

The Electricity Act 2023 and subsequent state legislation have opened the door to new market structures and greater state-level participation in generation and distribution, and Lagos has moved to establish its own framework under LASERC. Following the September award of an electricity generation licence to Elektron Energy, authorising the company to generate electricity within Lagos State, the commission’s leadership visited the plant to review construction progress, technical requirements and operational readiness with Elektron’s engineers and project partners.

For Lagos, the challenge is not only to create a framework that attracts investment but to ensure that framework produces projects that actually deliver power to customers. Victoria Island Power demonstrates how regulatory reform can support tangible infrastructure development, connecting an enabling policy environment with private investment, technical expertise and commercial demand. As the project moves into operation, it is positioned to contribute to the growing body of experience supporting embedded generation and dedicated power infrastructure within Lagos’s electricity market.

Beyond Victoria Island Victoria Island Power forms part of Elektron Energy’s broader strategy to develop, finance and operate critical energy infrastructure across Nigeria and other African markets. The company’s approach combines deep knowledge of local energy demand with sophisticated commercial structuring, international technical partnerships and the capacity to execute projects through their full development and operating lifecycle. This ambition is evident in the company’s portfolio, spanning very different needs: gas-fired generation for Lagos State’s offices at Alausa, dedicated supply for the Rack Centre data centre, and to West Africa’s largest rooftop solar installation at Jabi Lake Mall in Abuja.

These projects demonstrate Elektron’s ability to deliver tailored energy solutions across different sectors and scales. Building on this experience, Elektron continues to expand its footprint in embedded generation, distributed power and renewable energy. This integrated capability is central to Elektron’s long-term growth strategy. Rather than approaching power projects as isolated developments, the company is building a scalable infrastructure platform capable of delivering solutions across commercial centres, industrial clusters and other high-demand markets. Victoria Island Power provides a tangible example of that approach, demonstrating how proven capabilities and established partnerships can be deployed to address increasingly complex energy needs.

“Victoria Island Power reflects how we approach infrastructure development at Elektron. We start with a clear understanding of demand, bring together the right technical and financial partners, and build solutions designed to perform over the long term, proving power can work in Nigeria” says Tola Talabi, Chief Executive Officer of Elektron Energy. “This is the capability we have spent years developing, and it is the foundation on which we are building our wider portfolio.”

The Next Phase: Towards Commercial Operations

With its engines in place, supporting works progressing and customers signed, Victoria Island Power is entering its final stretch. The remaining steps centre on completing, testing and integrating the systems needed to deliver electricity safely and reliably. Nigeria’s electricity conversation has long been dominated by the scale of unmet demand, the cost of unreliable supply and the investment needed to close the gap. Victoria Island Power offers a different perspective: what can be achieved when commercial demand, institutional capital, engineering expertise and disciplined execution are brought together around a clearly defined need.

For Elektron Energy, the project represents more than another addition to its portfolio. It demonstrates the value of an infrastructure development model built on experience, strong partnerships and long-term commercial thinking. As Victoria Island Power advances towards operation, it offers a compelling indication of how purpose-built energy infrastructure can support Nigeria’s most productive commercial centres, and how that model can be extended to other markets.

World.title: FWIFT Underscores Training, Collaboration for Women in Film, TV, Digital Media
World.content:
Forum for Women in Film, TV and All Digital Media (FWIFT) has expressed the need for women in film, TV and digital media to train and collaborate.

It stated this in a communique it issued yesterday following its national convention, which held on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at Glover Memorial Hall, Lagos, under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together.”

It noted that the convention brought together women from film, television, radio, advertising and digital media, with the aim to support one another, grow the industry and build real agency for women professionals.

Participants, according to the communique,

made pledges to mentor, collaborate and co-produce, while FWIFT promised to ensure that the pledges were turned into actions.

The keynote speaker, Sandra Mbanefo Obiago, underscored the need for collaboration.

She said: “Tearing another sister down is an opportunity wasted when you could have had an elevating conversation.

“Be humble. It makes it easier to collaborate.”

FWIFT Patron, Erelu Bisi Fayemi, also shared her thoughts at the convention.

She said: You don’t need to have more money, speak through your nose, be bigger, be smaller or be lighter to be successful. You are enough.”

Other speakers also share their thoughts on sundry issues. Participants, for instance, were called upon not allow the fear of failing to stop them from asking for help. They equally advised women to do their due diligence with people.

“Do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with, then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop. Get up and go again,” the participants were told.

Participants were also advised to be flexible with the times.

“If you don’t change with the times, you will die.”

The conference also settled the age-long fallacy that women could not work together.

“Women work well with women. It is a myth that they do not”, one of the speakersn told the participants, among other issues.

FWIFT announced three future plans. The first is FWIFT Law Clinic. It said there would be a Law Clinic that would provide practical advice to participants on setting up and registering a company, and on the rights and protection of women working in the media.

The second is FWIFT Finance Workshop, which would unveil grant and finance packages available to media professionals, and which would inform women how to access them, in addition to business plan writing, and getting finance-ready.

It said TWIFT would follow up on pledges made on partnerships. This is the third plan. “FWIFT will follow up every pledge made at the convention, linking those offering support with those who need it, and backing new collaborations and co-productions,” it said.

It promised the participants that dates and registration details for these initiatives would be announced shortly.

FWIFT thanked every speaker, partner and participant, who made its first convention possible.

It reiterated: “FWIFT is a Forum for Women in Film, TV and All Digital Media (FWIFT). It is a national body uniting women professionals across Nigeria’s film, television, radio, advertising and digital media sectors. The Forum could be reached via Fwiftnigeria@gmail.com.”

World.title: Adesina Takes Up Insurance Ambassador Role, Tasks Operators on Public Trust
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

Former President of the African Development Bank (AfDB), Dr Akinwumi Adesina, has been named Global Ambassador for Insurance in Nigeria and Face of Insurance in the country, with a pledge to champion reforms aimed at repositioning the industry as a major driver of economic growth.

Adesina made the commitment while delivering the keynote address at the Nigeria Insurance Directors Conference, organised by the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria (CIIN) in collaboration with the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM) in Lagos.

He said he would deploy his experience, international networks and leadership influence to promote the growth, visibility and transformation of Nigeria’s insurance sector.

Speaking on the theme, “Building the Nigerian Insurance Industry: Institutional Transformation, Public Accountability and National Economic Development,” the former AfDB president challenged insurance operators, regulators and industry leaders to prioritise public confidence, accountability and professional standards.

He said Nigeria’s insurance penetration, estimated at about 0.5 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), remained a major constraint to the country’s capacity to protect households, businesses and productive investments.

According to him, the industry must move beyond conventional business practices and assume a more strategic role in supporting the Federal Government’s ambition of building a one-trillion-dollar economy.

“Do not just build insurance companies. Insure the nation. Protect its wealth. Finance its growth,” he said.

Adesina maintained that sustainable economic growth depended on an insurance industry capable of protecting productive assets, managing risks, supporting investments and mobilising long-term capital.

He identified rebuilding public confidence as one of the most urgent priorities facing the sector, stressing that the credibility of insurance companies was ultimately determined by their willingness to honour legitimate claims.

He said the value of insurance was demonstrated not when premiums were collected, but when policyholders suffered losses and received the protection promised under their policies.

“When a policyholder pays an insurance premium, that policyholder deserves a premium service in return,” he said.

He urged insurance companies to ensure prompt and transparent claims settlement, while calling on their boards to take greater responsibility for claims performance, customer complaints and management accountability.

The former AfDB president also proposed that NAICOM introduce an annual public accountability and performance report detailing claims received and settled, outstanding claims, settlement timelines, customer complaints, regulatory compliance, financial soundness and corporate governance.

He argued that the industry could not demand public confidence while resisting public scrutiny.

On the ongoing recapitalisation exercise under the Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act 2025, Adesina cautioned that increased capital alone would not guarantee stronger institutions.

“Recapitalisation is not the same as institutional transformation,” he said.

He explained that stronger capitalisation must be supported by sound corporate governance, disciplined underwriting, adequate technical reserves, effective risk management and stronger reinsurance arrangements.

He called on insurance directors to strengthen board oversight, scrutinise related-party transactions and ensure that internal audit, actuarial, compliance and risk-management functions operated independently.

He also urged NAICOM to deepen risk-based supervision and ensure that insurance companies were held accountable for measurable performance under the industry’s reform framework.

Adesina further called for expanded insurance coverage across agriculture, infrastructure, manufacturing, energy, transportation, healthcare and housing, noting that effective risk management was essential to attracting investments into productive sectors.

Drawing on his experience at the AfDB, he said development finance and risk management must work together, as investors were unlikely to commit substantial resources to projects where risks were inadequately managed.

He urged insurance companies to channel part of their investible funds into commercially viable infrastructure and productive-sector investments, while maintaining their obligations to policyholders and complying with applicable regulations.

He, however, cautioned that national development priorities must not override the financial interests of policyholders.

Adesina also advocated stronger domestic reinsurance capacity to enable Nigerian institutions to retain and prudently manage a greater proportion of insurable risks within the country.

The former AfDB president welcomed NAICOM’s 2031 targets of increasing insurance penetration to 10 per cent of GDP, extending active insurance coverage to 25 million Nigerians and developing 6,000 certified insurance professionals.

He said achieving the targets would require coordinated action by the regulator, professional institutions and insurance companies.

He urged NAICOM to provide strategic direction and regulatory oversight, while the CIIN should strengthen professional development, certification, competence and ethical leadership.

Insurance companies and their boards, he added, should establish measurable targets for expanding coverage, improving claims settlement, strengthening corporate governance and deploying technology.

He proposed an annual industry performance scorecard supported by quarterly monitoring and periodic independent assessments.

“The measure of success must be outcomes, not announcements,” he said.

Adesina’s acceptance of the ambassadorial role, according to the statement, reflects his commitment to strengthening the insurance industry and positioning it as an institution capable of supporting Nigeria’s long-term economic development.

He also drew on his doctoral research at Purdue University on agricultural risks, his experience managing agricultural risks as Nigeria’s Minister of Agriculture and his work on climate resilience and development financing during his tenure at the AfDB.

He urged insurance professionals, regulators and industry leaders to take collective responsibility for building institutions worthy of public confidence.

He said the future of Nigerian insurance would depend not merely on the volume of capital raised or premiums collected, but on the protection delivered to policyholders and the confidence inspired among the public.

“And the time to begin is now,” he said.

World.title: A’ Ibom Recruits 4,000 New Workers into State Public Service
World.content:
Okon Bassey in Uyo



The Akwa Ibom State Government has recruited 4,000 new workers into the state public service to strengthen its workforce.

According to the state Governor, Umo Eno, who disclosed this yesterday, the recruitment exercise is aimed at filling vacant positions, improving government operations and making public institutions more effective.

The governor explained the reason behind the recruitment during the orientation programme for the newly employed workers at the Ibom Tropicana Entertainment Centre in Uyo.

He said the appointments were based on vacancies identified across the public service and were not intended to unnecessarily increase the workforce.

Eno said a staff verification exercise conducted at the beginning of his administration uncovered more than 2,000 ghost workers, alongside several retired employees, revealing gaps in the workforce and the need to recruit qualified personnel to fill vacant positions.

“The decision reflects the administration’s effort to strengthen the public service and ensure that government departments have the personnel needed to carry out their responsibilities effectively,” he stressed.

The governor tasked the new employees to regard their appointments as an opportunity to serve the people and contribute to the development of the state.

He further charged them to demonstrate discipline, commitment, transparency and professionalism in their daily duties.

Eno also emphasised the importance of digital skills, explaining that the state was working towards the full digitalisation of public services.

He told the new employees to embrace technology, introduce fresh ideas and help make government processes faster and more efficient.

Eno reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the prompt payment of salaries and gratuities.

He commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for making funds available to state governments to support project execution and the payment of workers’ entitlements.

Also, the Head of Service, Mrs. Elsie Peters, welcomed the recruitment and expressed confidence in the quality of the new workforce, describing the orientation programme as an important preparation for the responsibilities ahead.

She said the recruitment added another important development to the administration’s public service record, as its greatest value will be seen in the quality of work delivered, the efficiency of government offices, and the improvement of citizens’ experience when accessing public services.

“For the 4,000 new employees, the real task begins now. Their commitment, conduct and performance will determine how well this opportunity translates into better service for the people of Akwa Ibom State,” she added.

World.title: EFInA, LBS Facilitates Evidence-Based Financial Inclusion Policymaking
World.content:
Enhancing Financial Inclusion and Advancement (EFInA), in partnership with Sustainable and Inclusive Digital Financial Services (SIDFS), an initiative of Lagos Business School, Pan-Atlantic University, has equipped 147 professionals with practical skills to apply financial inclusion data in policymaking, towards addressing key challenges across Nigeria’s financial inclusion ecosystem.

Delivered through the Leveraging Financial Inclusion Data for Policymaking course, the initiative sought to strengthen participants’ ability to use evidence to inform policy decisions and support more inclusive financial systems. This focus is particularly relevant following the release of EFInA’s 2026 Access to Financial Services (A2F) Survey findings, as stakeholders work to translate the evidence into policies and interventions that respond to the needs of underserved populations.

Over seven weeks, participants completed seven modules combining e-learning with live virtual sessions. They explored how financial inclusion data, including insights from the Global Findex and A2F Surveys, can help identify gaps, understand the needs of underserved groups and inform policy priorities.

The programme’s impact was reflected in improvements in participants’ knowledge and confidence.

Knowledge accuracy increased from 72.5 per cent before the course to 88.5 per cent afterwards, while confidence in applying the skills rose by 21.5 percentage points. These gains point to stronger readiness among participants to use data in their professional work and policy decisions. That strengthened capacity was put into practice through the course’s capstone assignments. They propose recommendations on issues such as agent banking geo-tagging, inclusive eKYC, consumer protection, open finance, Takaful, pension literacy and rural youth credit. These proposals address key challenges across Nigeria’s financial inclusion ecosystem and have the potential to inform ongoing policy discussions and interventions.

According to EFInA’s Research Lead, Dr Oluwatomi Eromosele, “We are encouraged by the progress participants have made, from improved knowledge and confidence to developing policy briefs that address real financial inclusion challenges. These results show that when professionals are equipped to interpret and apply financial inclusion evidence, they are better positioned to identify gaps, assess policy needs and recommend responses that reflect the realities of underserved communities. We look forward to seeing this strengthened capacity contribute to more effective policymaking in Nigeria.”

Participants also described how the course had changed their approach to using financial inclusion data. One participant shared: “I now approach financial inclusion data more intentionally, not just as information to understand trends, but as evidence for identifying gaps, understanding underserved groups, and informing more targeted policy and interventions.” Another participant reflected: “I now approach policy decisions with a more evidence-based mindset, and I am better equipped to identify where interventions are needed most.”

Together, these reflections illustrate the programme’s central aim: to help professionals move beyond understanding financial inclusion data to applying it in ways that can support more targeted, evidence-informed policy and interventions.

The course was delivered through EFInA’s partnership with SIDFS, an initiative of Lagos Business School, Pan-Atlantic University, which supports inclusive digital financial services through research, capacity building and engagement.

World.title: 7 kilometres from South Africa’s platinum city, there are 12 acres with R90 rates
World.content:
4.8 hectares on sale for R980 000. Image: Pexels

According to a 5 November 2026 listing from Remax, buyers can purchase 11.86 acres for under R1 million in Primindia, a town just outside of Brits in the North West.

The listing describes the property as a prime location for agricultural activities.

The land is currently unserviced; a buyer will need to connect water and electricity.



But there’s plenty of potential, as buyer interest in the area is growing.

In-demand location with developer-friendly property

According to Private Property, there are 5 active listings in this town; 2 of these were listed in November.

Properties sell almost as soon as they list.

That’s because supply is limited, even as demand grows.



So far this year, the South African Deeds Office recorded 8 sales in Primindia with an average sale price of R600 000.

But Primindia could be the region’s next up-and-coming area.

Abutting the Crocodile River, the property offers proximity to Brits, the bushveld, and a host of Game Reserves.



It’s also at the cusp of a population boom.

Since 2011, Brits’ population has nearly doubled.

According to the 2011 census, the town was home to 53 511 people. Today, Brits has 100 030 residents.



The expansion has pushed buyers further from the city centre.

Platinum mining community

Primindia is attracting some well-heeled residents.

Currently, there’s a 3-bedroom home on the market listed for R6 million, 6 times the average sale price in Brits and 10 times the average sale price for Primindia.



The home is set on 4.8 hectares and has 500 square metres of living space.

In neighbouring Brits and Rustenburg, considered South Africa’s platinum belt, roughly 125 tonnes of platinum are extracted every year.

An increase in mining production and industry growth has also meant population growth.



Population expansion has also aided property prices.

In Brits, property prices have increased 20% since the start of the year.

Safety in Brits

But buyers may be hesitant because of rising crime in Brits.



In the last 7 years, crime in Brits rose 19.1%, according to South African Police Service (SAPS) data.

Crime peaked in 2025.

Violent crime and drug-related crime have accelerated the increase.



In the year ending March 2021, violent crime surpassed property crime for the first time since SAPS started reporting on its data.

Violent crime has been rising ever since.

World.title: Proteas vs Bangladesh: South Africa chasing top of WTC table
World.content:
Bangladesh's tour of South Africa will define the World Test Championship for the Proteas. Image: Wikimedia Commons, Proteas Men CSA (X).

South Africa return to Test action against Bangladesh later this month (November 2026).

The Proteas lead the ICC Test rankings, but are not leading the World Test Championship (WTC) standings.

Here’s why the first Test at the Wanderers from 15-19 November could be pivotal.



World Test #1 still second in WTC

South Africa’s loss in the first Test against Australia saw them dip to third in the WTC standings.

The Proteas bounced back masterfully to eventually win the series 2-1.

This also pushed them to the top of the ICC’s Men’s Test Team Rankings.



After the third Test at Newlands, Australia dropped to third in the WTC behind South Africa.

New Zealand have now jumped to the top of the table with a marginal lead.

The Black Caps start their Test series against India a few days after the Proteas and Bangladesh.



This means that a win by South Africa will knock New Zealand to second place.

However, the home team still has to navigate past a Bangladesh team that has caused some upsets.

The Tigers are fifth in the WTC standings behind fourth-placed India, and took a win off Australia during their past series.



PROTEAS announce squad for Bangladesh Tests

South Africa’s squad for the Bangladesh Test series was released on 2 November.

Tony de Zorzi returns after missing the Australia series with a hamstring injury.

Anrich Nortje is back in the mix after leaving the second Test against the Aussies.



Zubayr Hamza also returns, having last played a Test for the Proteas in February 2024.

David Bedingham, Kyle Verreynne, Senuran Muthusamy, and Gerald Coetzee have been dropped for the series.

Coetzee was drafted into the squad in place of Nortje for the third Australia Test.

World.title: ‘We struggle but we fought for this country’: Pensioners push for more from SASSA
World.content:
Pensioners say their South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) grants no longer stretch far enough. Many are calling on government to rethink how and when it increases payments.

Commenting on The South African’s Facebook page, grant recipients shared their frustrations about the rising cost of living. They responded to a story about a pensioner who called for the Older Persons and War Veterans grants to rise to R3 000.

FOOD COSTS LEAVE SASSA GRANT RECIPIENTS SHORT

Petunia Allan said even R3 000 would not be enough.



“Yes, that’s better, but we want R5000. The cost of living is high. What I think is to increase 2 times a year. Food goes up every day. We struggle, but we fought for this country. I don’t understand,” she wrote.

Freeman Ncube agreed that grants barely cover the basics.

“Yes the money of sassa is too small for important things it finish on food and still short,” he said.

Since April 2026, the Older Persons Grant, Disability Grant, and Care Dependency Grant have been paid at R2 400 per month, following an R80 increase. The War Veterans Grant rose by R80 to R2 420. The government currently announces grant increases once a year in the Budget Speech.

TAX AND PAYMENT IDEAS

Some commenters proposed other ways to ease the pressure on older people.

Rita Botha wrote simply: “No tax or vat for pensioners !!”



Social grants do not attract income tax, but pensioners still pay VAT on most goods they buy. A few basic foods, such as brown bread and maize meal, are zero-rated.

Abduragmaan Crombie suggested a change to how often pensioners receive their money.

“Pensioner should receive twice a month your Pension Payments,” he commented.

CONFUSION OVER CHANGING NUMBERS

Michelle Naidoo questioned the frequent changes.

“why does the numbers keep changings,” she asked.

She did not say which figures she meant. However, many grant recipients have had to adjust to new grant amounts this year, as well as once-off November payment dates that SASSA introduced because of the Local Government Elections.

SASSA has confirmed that the December dates will follow the original schedule. Older Persons Grants will be paid on 2 December, Disability Grants on 3 December and Children’s Grants on 4 December 2026.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs coach to replace 30-year-old leader
World.content:
Inacio Miguel plays for Kaizer Chiefs in the Betway Premiership. Image: Vino Snap

Kaizer Chiefs vice-captain Inácio Miguel is suspended for Sunday’s clash. Coach Fernando Da Cruz will reshuffle his central defensive partnership as Amakhosi hunt a Carling Knockout semi-final place.

The 30-year-old Angolan defender’s disciplinary record continues to draw scrutiny. He has already faced several bookings and a red card this season.

INÁCIO MIGUEL SUSPENDED FOR KAIZER CHIEFS’ MATCH AGAINST SIWELELE

Following his booking in the Soweto Derby, Miguel will sit out the Carling Knockout quarter-final at home to Siwelele FC on Sunday, which kicks off at 18:00 at the New Peter Mokaba Stadium.



A red card and a growing collection of cautions have made discipline a talking point surrounding Miguel.

Since joining Amakhosi in August 2024, Miguel has made 28 appearances and played 2,520 minutes during his standout 2024/25 debut season.

He also proved dangerous in the opposition’s penalty area, scoring three goals in his first three Nedbank Cup matches. His contribution helped Amakhosi secure a memorable 2-1 victory over Orlando Pirates in the final.



Miguel has already received three yellow cards and one red card across his first nine appearances of the current campaign.

His aggressive approach has previously attracted criticism, although his coach has defended his commitment and intensity.

RUSHWIN DORTLEY EXPECTED TO PARTNER THABO MOLOISANE

With Miguel unavailable, Rushwin Dortley, returning from a long injury layoff, is expected to get the opportunity to partner Thabo Moloisane in central defence.



On the opposite side, Siwelele’s Aphiwe Baliti is also out suspended for the encounter.

INACIO MIGUEL’S EXPERIENCE HE BRINGS TO KAIZER CHIEFS

Before joining Amakhosi, Miguel accumulated 157 career appearances and scored eight goals across 10 seasons.

His journey included spells at Braga B in Portugal (33 appearances), Universitatea Cluj in Romania (28), FK Liepāja in Latvia (15) and Petro de Luanda in Angola (25 league appearances and four goals).



He helped Petro secure a domestic double, including the Girabola title, and has also earned six senior caps for Angola.

FIXTURE DETAILS

Venue: New Peter Mokaba Stadium

Match: Kaizer Chiefs vs Siwelele FC

Competition: Carling Knockout Cup quarter-finals

Date: Sunday

Kick-off: 18:00.

World.title: ‘Relebohile Mofokeng is too good for Belgium’
World.content:
Relebohile Mofokeng is being tipped to make a move to one of Europe’s top five leagues after a stellar debut season in Belgium.

Relebohile Mofokeng has dazzled since leaving Orlando Pirates

Mofokeng has sparkled in his debut campaign with Royal SG. The ex-Pirates man has scored five times and laid on four assists in 15 outings. Most recently, he was a key creative force as Mofokeng and his teammates claimed an impressive win away to Celta Vigo in the Europa League. The 22-year-old scored on his European debut against Viktoria Plzen. Now, he’s been nominated for the Jupiter Pro League Player of the Month for October.

According to@ekremkonur on X, Bayer Leverkusen and SC Freiburg are targetting the gifted young South African. However, Royal USG have strong leverage and would demand at least €15M (R275 million) for their prized asset.



A breakdown of Rele Mofokeng’s month of October

Rele Mofokeng and Royal Union Saint-Gilloise are flying both domestically and in Europe. They went unbeaten in the month of October, winning four matches on the bounce across all competitions at the back end. Mofokeng scored and assisted in a 5-2 win over Cercle Brugge, assisted in a 4-0 win over Hapoel Beer Sheva in the Europa League, and was man of the match in an impressive 1-1 draw with Real Sociedad. Next up for them is a league match against Genk on Sunday, 8 November kicking off at 19:30 SA time.

Orlando Pirates get the better of Kaizer Chiefs

Meanwhile, Mofokeng’s old club beat Kaizer Chiefs 2-1 in last Saturday’s Soweto Derby, effectively ruling the Glamour Boys out of the title race after just nine matches. Orlando Pirates boss Abdeslam Ouaddou notched his 50th win for a PSL club in the process. The Sea Robbers have won four of the last six meetings between the sides.

World.title: Orlando Pirates coach Ouaddou on why Appollis is benched
World.content:
Orlando Pirates coach Abdeslam Ouaddou has explained the reason behind Oswin Appollis‘ recent lack of game time.

Appollis was an ever-present member of Ouaddou’s squad last that won a domestic treble last season.

However, he has had to settle for a place on the bench and he’s mostly used sparingly as an impact player so far this term.



Appollis was also benched in big matches such as the MTN8 final against Mamelodi Sundowns and the Soweto Derby against Kaizer Chiefs.

Pirates lost the MTN8 final to Sundowns but redeemed themselves by claiming the bragging rights with a win over Chiefs.

Now, according to Ouaddou, the aim is to protect Appollis from fatigue, adding that the attacker is still going to play a huge role this season.



APPOLLIS’ LACK OF GAME TIME AT ORLANDO PIRATES EXPLAINED

“Appollis is a master class, he is one of our best players. Appollis is one of the best players in South Africa but we don’t have to forget that he is human. He is not a robot,” Ouaddou told the media.

“Appollis had a fantastic season in his first season at Pirates after coming from Polokwane City.

“You know, a lot of things have changed for him, and he managed to handle all these things. He had a wonderful, fantastic season straight away.



“He went to the World Cup, and it’s not only him. Many players in Europe, at other clubs. He played the games, he gave everything for his country.

“So, he is a guy who is not cheating. We can understand one moment that sometimes a player can have this fatigue,” he explained.

“So, we are protecting our diamond. We are protecting our diamond because we have many games, and we know that if we protect him, we give him his time.



“We know that he will be important for us. We will benefit from this protection that we give him but soon you are going to see Appollis back,” concluded Ouaddou.

World.title: Five Orlando Pirates stars called up for November international duty
World.content:
Five Orlando Pirates players will represent Bafana Bafana during the upcoming November international break. Image: SAFA website

Five Orlando Pirates players will represent Bafana Bafana during the upcoming November international break.

Club football is set to pause once again as national teams turn their attention to international fixtures, including the latest round of Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying matches.

READ | Bafana Bafana overseas players: 9 players travelling to camp



Bafana Bafana head coach Pitso Mosimane has named a 27-man squad for the November window, retaining much of the group that featured in South Africa’s three international matches in September.

Five Orlando Pirates players have made the cut.

Five Buccaneers in Bafana Bafana squad

Goalkeeper Sipho Chaine has received another national team call-up following his consistent performances between the posts.



He is joined by defender Lebone Seema, who has continued to make progress at international level after making his debut as a substitute in the 5-0 victory over Eritrea.

Seema subsequently earned his first start in South Africa’s 1-0 friendly win over Egypt.

Midfielder Thalente Mbatha also returns to the national team setup after an injury-enforced absence.



Completing the Orlando Pirates contingent are attackers Oswin Appollis and Tshepang Moremi, both of whom retain their places in the squad.

Bafana BAFANA prepare for two matches against Kenya

South Africa will face co-hosts Kenya twice during the November international window.

The first encounter is scheduled for Friday, 13 November, at Orlando Amstel Arena.



Bafana will then travel to Nairobi for the return fixture at Nyayo Stadium on Tuesday, 17 November.

The matches form part of South Africa’s preparations and campaign for the 2027 AFCON tournament, which will be hosted in East Africa.

For Orlando Pirates, the five call-ups provide another opportunity for their players to gain valuable international experience during a busy period of the season.

World.title: DA open to coalition talks - Hill-Lewis
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Democratic Alliance leader Geordin Hill-Lewis says the party is open to coalitions with other political parties.

The DA is calling on political parties to help it rebuild municipalities nationwide.

Hill-Lewis says the party is determined to improve service delivery in failing municipalities.

"We will approach the next few weeks with respect for the mandates those parties have received from their voters," he says.

"We know that these cities desperately need a period of long and sustained progress under the honest and integrity-driven government," he adds.

The party has amassed a leading number of votes in many of the country's metros and municipalities.

However, as seat allocation gets underway, a different picture is emerging that could change the trajectory of many municipalities.

The party is open to talks with 'like-minded' people. It says even an alliance with the Economic Freedom Fighters is a possibility.

"We have already reached out to many parties over the last 24 hours and we will continue," says Hill-Lewis.

World.title: eNCA MarkData | Understanding overhangs in municipal councils
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - As the final votes come in, political parties are turning their attention to their seat allocations in municipal councils.

The final allocation of council seats should broadly reflect each party’s share of the vote. But what happens when a party wins more wards than the number of seats it would normally be entitled to under proportional representation?

This is known as an overhang.

World.title: Paraguay president steps down as banking crisis sows chaos
World.content:
ASUNCION - Paraguayan President Santiago Pena will face an impeachment trial after a financial crisis that led the US-allied leader to resign Thursday, after a banking takeover blocked almost half the population from accessing their money.

Congress put Pena's resignation on hold while the impeachment process move forwards, which means he will remain in office provisionally.

The Central Bank's seizure of Pena-linked Ueno Bank two days earlier froze the deposits of some three million people, including pensioners, and sparked angry demonstrations across the country.

Thousands of Paraguayans gathered outside Congress on Thursday to protest against the president, who is still technically in power as his resignation awaits legislative approval.

"Give back the money," AFP journalists heard them yelling. Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

"My family ran out of money, we don't have any cash. Santi (Pena) is a criminal, he has to go to jail," 21-year-old student protester Andres Maldonado told AFP.

World.title: Pope Leo on emotional South America tour weeks after cancer surgery
World.content:
LIMA - Pope Leo XIV heads to South America on Friday for an emotionally charged reunion with the continent that helped shape his priesthood, three weeks after undergoing lung cancer surgery.

The 71-year-old head of the Catholic Church will in 12 days visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in one of the most intense papal foreign trips in decades, meeting political leaders, prisoners, the poor, as well as old friends.

The Church's first US-born pope served for almost two decades in Peru as a missionary, forming a deep attachment to the continent. Leo said on Wednesday that he was looking forward to returning to those countries "so dear to me".

The head of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics said he hoped the trip would "strengthen faith, renew hope, (and) rekindle the fire of charity" in the countries, which share challenges from rising inequality and violence, to demographic falls and the decline of Catholicism.

Despite undergoing an operation on October 13 to remove a cancerous tumour, doctors have given him the all-clear to travel, and the Vatican said no special medical measures were necessary beyond the standard care on papal trips.

- Secular Uruguay -

Leo begins his trip in Uruguay, Latin America's most secular country -- and one of the wealthiest -- where a tight security operation is in place, with some 5,000 police officers and 1,000 soldiers mobilised.

He will be driven along Montevideo's waterfront promenade in a custom-made popemobile, before meeting left-wing President Yamandu Orsi and receiving the keys to the city.

"I have family members who plan to go to the waterfront to watch him pass," Janet Rodríguez, 47, told AFP.

"I won't be going, as I'm not religious. But it's great that someone of such importance is coming," she said.

World.title: Carrick fights for Man Utd job ahead of international break
World.content:
LONDON - Michael Carrick takes charge of Manchester United for what could be the last time against Aston Villa this weekend as he battles to save his job despite a morale-boosting midweek victory over Roma.

United's dramatic win in the Champions League gave the coach breathing space but he remains under intense pressure ahead of the international break.

Elsewhere in the Premier League, Manchester City will be seeking to avoid a rare third straight league defeat when they face Nottingham Forest as they try to keep pace with leaders Arsenal.

AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of the action:

Carrick's last chance?

When Manchester United's players trudged off at half-time against Roma on Tuesday, 2-0 down and seemingly out of ideas, Michael Carrick's fate appeared to be sealed.

Instead, his underperforming team somehow turned things around, with Matheus Cunha scoring two late goals in a 3-2 win at a feverish Old Trafford.

It ended a run of nine games without a victory -- United's longest winless run since the 1988/89 season.

Defender Diogo Dalot said he hopes the Roma result can kickstart their season.

World.title: Bear necessities: Indian techie builds wildlife alert
World.content:
MUMBAI - After his mother was killed in a bear attack in Kashmir, Indian software engineer Mudasir Ali developed an online early-warning system to help people in the Himalayan region avoid dangerous encounters with wildlife.

Ali created Wildping, a free website where users report sightings of animals such as Himalayan black bears and leopards, triggering alerts to people nearby.

The 33-year-old launched the platform in October, on the first anniversary of his mother's death.

She was among at least 50 people killed, with hundreds more mauled, in wildlife attacks in the territory since 2023, according to official data.

"Since then, I have always had it in my mind that I should use my skills to develop a technology that people living in these hotspots, where such incidents occur, can use to protect themselves," Ali told AFP.

World.title: Zuma-Sambudla's bid to have July unrest case dismissed rejected
World.content:
DURBAN - Duduzile Zuma-Sambudla’s application to have the case linked to the July 2021 unrest withdrawn has been dismissed by the Durban High Court.

Zuma-Sambudla appeared in court on Friday, where she is standing trial on allegations that she encouraged the July 2021 unrest following her father, former president Jacob Zuma’s, imprisonment.

The matter has been postponed to 17 May 2027 for legal argument.

World.title: Shakahola horror: Paul Makenzi sentenced to 200 years in prison
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Paul Makenzi sentenced to 200 years in prison, while his 28 co-accused received sentences of between 10 and 160 years for the murders of 191 people within Shakahola Forest. [Robert Menza, Standard]

The High Court in Mombasa has sentenced doomsday preacher Paul Makenzi to 200 years in prison for the murder of 191 people in the Shakahola massacre.

Justice Diana Kavedza Mochache also sentenced his 28 co-accused to prison terms ranging from 10 to 160 years.

The twenty-eight (28) co- accused persons were found guilty of all 191 murder counts last month involving the deaths of 190 children and one adult.

Justice Mochache said that the Good News International Church founder would serve 100 years for murder by starvation involving 183 murder counts of 182 children and the adult.

She said that he is to serve a further 100 years for murder by direct homicide involving child victims which resulted to an aggregate imprisonment of 200 years.

She said that some of Makenzi’s victims died from starvation whole autopsies on some of them showed that they died as a result of strangulation, suffocation and blunt force trauma. Cult leader Paul Makenzi is escorted by heavily armed police officers after his sentencing to 200 years in prison by the Mombasa High Court over the Shakahola massacre. [Robert Menza, Standard]

The judge said that her decision to impose the two sentences to be served consecutively was for the recognition of the distinction between the murder chargers and to punish them adequately.

His co-accused were handed 10 years to 160 years for the several counts with each one of them having a different level of culpability.

The Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions had asked the judge to hand the Makenzi, a death penalty over the lives lost through his actions and for his co-accused to serve sentenced to life in prison, but she declined.

In October, Justice Mochache convicted Makenzi and his co-accused over the murders of which occurred between January 2021 and September 2023.

She said that the accused persons took advantage of their victims by abusing spiritual authority and betraying them citing parents who has trusted them with the care of their children, some of whom wound up dead. Justice Diana Kavedza Mochache when she sentenced doomsday preacher Paul Makenzi to 200 years and his co-accused to between 10 and 160 years in prison over the murder of 191 people in the Shakahola massacre. [Robert Menza, Standard]

The judge cited Makenzi’s role in the killings saying witnesses had testified that he told his followers often that they would enter heaven through “punches and kicks” even if they were crippled adding that it demonstrates brutality on his part.

Justice Mochache said that the co-accused are eligible for an early release if they will have served half their sentences and undergone a program to deradicalize them while in prison.

In 2023, a human’s rights lobby group alerted authorities about the deaths and what followed with the exhumation of more than 400 bodies from shallow graves in the 800-acre Chakama Ranch in Kilifi County.

From this, more than 60 bodies were positively identified by their relatives and were released for burial and there remains many others that are unidentified and unclaimed.

World.title: Goon financiers should be cursed and sent to hell, Chief Justice Koome says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Chief Justice Martha Koome said goonism falls under serious organised crimes that goes against the Rome Statute and humanity. [Phares Mutembei, Standard]

Chief Justice Martha Koome now says those mobilising and financing goons should be cursed and thrown to hell.

Koome on Thursday said goonism falls under organised serious crimes that go against the Rome Statute and humanity.

She spoke at Kieganguru, Maara constituency, where she presided over the opening of the Maara law courts.

While calling on police to focus more on arresting the mobilisers and financiers, Koome said a time has come for the country to plead with God to protect the country and rescue the youth who are being misused and misled into organised gangs and goonism.

“Nobody gives birth to a child to be called a goon. Those organisers will go to hell, we curse them,” Koome said, adding, “If they will not go to hell they will meet God's justice. These are our children, and we reclaim them in the name of our Lord Jesus.”

According to her, the last time she checked, people are charged at the International Criminal Court with Organised crime.

She maintained that the best solution to the current goonism that wreaked havoc, especially in political meetings, is to arrest the organisers.

Koome said the courts cannot hold arrested goons without bail, yet the constitution grants them the right to bail or bond.

“When we arrest small people with petty crimes of causing disorder, the law allows us to release them on bail and bond, but when you bring the organisers, we will charge them under the Serious Crimes Act,” she said.

Koome said currently, the judiciary has gazetted a serious crimes division at the High Court to support Magistrates handling the cases.

“Let us look at the root cause of goonism across the country and rehabilitate those involved by getting them gainful employment,” she said.

Her sentiments, however, differ from those of Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen, who on Wednesday told the National Assembly that the judiciary was the weakest link in the fight against the menace.

Tharaka Nithi Governor Muthomi Njuki, in his remarks, supported Koome’s view of arresting the planners.

Njuki, who doubles up as the Council of Governors Chairperson, said politicians have had their time and organising goons against their opponents should not be condoned.

Using the analogy of a dog, Njuki said ‘every barking dog has an owner ’, and it is time serious action was taken against such characters at whatever level they are.

The county boss said CoG will work closely with county security teams to arrest the fast-rising menace and report all cases.

Security agencies have been under scrutiny regarding goons, with calls for their arrest and prosecution.

Earlier on, Koome and DCI boss Mohammed Amin differed on how to handle the goons during a National Council for Administrative Justice meeting as with the DCI boss also accusing the Judiciary of laxity and granting minor bail to arrested goons.

But Koome maintained the issue must be addressed lest it becomes a thorn in the flesh ahead of the 2027 elections.

World.title: IEBC warns UDA SG Hassan Omar over remarks on deceased voters
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

UDA Secretary General Hassan Omar meets Village Elders and Mabalozi wa Nyumba Kumi from Jomvu Sub-County’ on September 10, 2026. [Nehemiah Okwemba, Standard]

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has issued a stern warning to Senator Hassan Omar after finding him in breach of the Electoral Code of Conduct over remarks he made at a political rally in Mombasa, cautioning that any repeat offence could attract tougher sanctions.

In a determination released on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, the Electoral Code of Conduct Enforcement Committee (ECCEC) found Omar guilty of breaching paragraphs 6(k)(i) and 6(l) of the Electoral Code of Conduct.

The committee consequently issued the senator with a formal and strict warning and severe caution, directing him to comply with the electoral regulations for the remainder of the applicable election period.

Omar was further instructed to refrain from language or conduct that could reasonably be understood as encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice or undermining public confidence in the integrity of the ballot.

The decision follows investigations into remarks the senator allegedly made during a public rally in Mombasa on September 11, 2026, which raised concerns over the possibility of encouraging electoral malpractice.

According to the commission, Omar was summoned to appear before the committee on October 21, 2026, to respond to the allegations. He honoured the summons and appeared in person, accompanied by his lawyer, where he was given an opportunity to explain his remarks and present his defence.

In reaching its determination, the committee considered the context in which the statements were made, Omar's explanation that his words were intended figuratively to encourage voter registration and participation, his subsequent clarification and the absence of evidence linking the remarks to an actual electoral incident.

However, the committee maintained that the language used could not be excused by the explanation offered.

It observed that the impugned words, considered in their original Kiswahili form and ordinary meaning, invoked the use of biometric identification details belonging to a deceased person to facilitate voting in that individual's name.

The committee consequently found the remarks inconsistent with the obligation under paragraph 6(l) of the Electoral Code to reassure voters about the integrity of the ballot.

The warning places Omar on clear notice that any recurrence of similar conduct could attract more severe sanctions under the Electoral Code of Conduct and applicable laws.

“The determination places Hon. Hassan Omar on clear and unequivocal notice that the warning issued by the Committee is intended to mark a firm boundary against any recurrence of similar conduct,” IEBC stated.

The commission further emphasised that political leaders and other electoral stakeholders have a constitutional right to campaign, criticise, debate, persuade and participate in political discourse.

However, it cautioned that political expression must be exercised responsibly, warning that statements perceived as advocating, encouraging or normalising electoral malpractice could undermine public confidence in the electoral process.

“As Kenya prepares for the 2027 General Election, the Commission calls upon all political leaders, candidates, political parties, supporters and other electoral stakeholders to exercise responsibility, restraint and vigilance in their public utterances and conduct,” the commission said.

The determination comes as political activities gradually intensify ahead of the 2027 General Election, with the electoral body seeking to strengthen compliance with regulations governing political campaigns and public conduct.

IEBC maintained that enforcement of the Electoral Code should not be interpreted as an attempt to suppress legitimate political competition or freedom of expression.

Instead, it said the measures were intended to safeguard democratic participation and ensure that every Kenyan could exercise their right to vote without intimidation, manipulation or interference.

The commission reiterated its commitment to protecting the sanctity of the ballot, assuring Kenyans that every vote must be protected and counted in accordance with the law.

It warned that it would continue enforcing electoral regulations firmly, fairly and without fear or favour, as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum.

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.
