EGYPT · RESERVES

Key Facts The figure Net international reserves reached US$57.5 billion at the end of October 2026, a record.

The change Up US$152 million, or 0.27%, from US$57.348 billion at the end of September.

The mix Foreign currencies rose US$768 million to US$40.06 billion; gold fell US$613 million to US$16.84 billion.

The trend Reserves are US$7.4 billion above October 2025 and US$6.0 billion above the end of 2025.

Next watch The International Monetary Fund, a global lender, wants Egypt’s final loan reviews at its board before 15 December.

Egypt reserves reached a record US$57.5 billion at the end of October 2026, up US$152 million from US$57.348 billion a month earlier. The Central Bank of Egypt published the provisional figure on Thursday 5 November 2026.

Free daily brief — no card needed Get every Africa story in one morning email We build you a personalized brief around the topics you follow — free for 7 days. Love it? Your first month after that is US$1. Start my free brief Yes, email me my free daily brief — I can unsubscribe any time.

Reserves have risen for ten months in a row, since January 2026, and now stand US$7.4 billion above a year ago. For US readers, a fuller cushion means Egypt is better placed to pay for imports and debt.

What the Central Bank Reported

The Central Bank of Egypt, the country’s national bank, puts net international reserves at US$57.5 billion for the end of October 2026. The figure is marked provisional, so the bank can still adjust it later.

Gross official reserves, which count everything the bank holds, stood at US$57.502 billion. Net reserves, the figure analysts watch, were only US$2 million lower.

Foreign currencies made up US$40.06 billion of the total, or about 70%. Gold was worth US$16.843 billion, and special drawing rights, a reserve asset issued by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), US$599 million.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Egypt Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Egypt Reserves Rose Again

The central bank’s table shows where the gain came from: holdings of foreign currencies grew by US$768 million in October. A US$613 million fall in the value of gold offset most of that rise.

The table gives figures only and no reasons for the monthly move. The steady base underneath is money sent home by Egyptians working abroad.

Central Bank figures reported in October show remittances of about US$33.9 billion in January to August 2026, up 27.2% on a year earlier. August alone brought about US$4.2 billion, up 21.7%.

Those transfers arrive as hard currency through banks, so they feed the foreign-currency line of the table. Gold works differently, because its dollar value moves with the world gold price.

The Trend Since Last Year

Reserves stood at US$50.071 billion at the end of October 2025 and US$51.452 billion at the end of 2025. They have risen for ten months in a row, since January 2026, as our report on the September record showed.

Gold has been the swing factor. It peaked at US$21.502 billion in February 2026 and has since fallen to US$16.843 billion, while foreign currencies grew from US$30.69 billion to US$40.06 billion.

In Plain English, Who Is Who

The Central Bank of Egypt is the country’s national bank and publishes the monthly reserves table. Net international reserves are the foreign money and gold it can use quickly, after short-term claims are subtracted.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) is a global lender that has backed Egypt with a loan programme. Julie Kozack is the IMF’s communications director and speaks for the fund at press briefings.

What It Means for You

A larger cushion lowers the risk of a sudden currency crisis in Egypt, which matters if you hold Egyptian bonds or a fund that does. It also helps Egypt keep paying for imports such as food and fuel.

Egypt runs the Suez Canal, a route that carries cargo between Asia and Europe, so its finances matter to global shipping. Our guide to Egypt’s economy explains the pound, prices and the loan programme.

Almost 30% of the reserves is gold, so a fall in the gold price can cut the total even when dollar inflows hold up. Watch the foreign-currency line, not only the headline.

What Would Change It

A drop in remittances, tourism or Suez Canal income would slow the build-up, as would foreign investors selling Egyptian bonds. A lower gold price would also shrink the total.

IMF approval would bring fresh money, with Julie Kozack saying on Thursday 29 October 2026 that about US$2.3 billion is tied to the final review. The reviews are meant to reach the IMF board before the programme expires on 15 December.

What Is Not Known

The central bank’s table does not say whether gold fell in October because of price moves or sales. The bank can answer with its next monthly table, expected in early December.

It is open whether the IMF board will approve the final US$2.3 billion before the programme ends on 15 December 2026. IMF staff and the board decide, with the reviews due at the board before then.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How high are Egypt’s reserves?

Net international reserves were US$57.5 billion at the end of October 2026, a record. That is US$152 million above September’s US$57.348 billion.

What are Egypt’s reserves made of?

Foreign currencies were US$40.06 billion, gold US$16.843 billion and special drawing rights US$599 million. Foreign currencies are about 70% of the total and gold almost 30%.

Who reports the figure and how often?

The Central Bank of Egypt publishes a provisional table once a month. The October table came out on Thursday 5 November 2026.

Does this matter outside Egypt?

Yes, for holders of Egyptian bonds and for firms that ship through the Suez Canal. A larger cushion lowers the risk of a sudden currency shock.

Published Friday, 6 November, 6:30 a.m. ET (12:30 p.m. Madrid) · Source: SW Demoscopia poll, Polymarket, Spain’s official gazette (BOE), Rio Times research

A Poll That Breaks The Pattern

A poll published on 5 November by SW Demoscopia puts Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's Socialist Party (PSOE) narrowly ahead of the conservative Popular Party (PP), against most other recent private polls. It gives the PSOE 29.8% and the PP 29.1%, with Vox, a conservative nationalist party led by Santiago Abascal, on 16%.

The survey projects 126 seats for the PSOE, 118 for the PP and 62 for Vox in the 350-seat Congress of Deputies. A majority requires 176 seats.

On those numbers the PP and Vox together would hold 180 seats, barely above the threshold. Fieldwork was on 4 November, after the transport minister's resignation.

Our full coverage sits on the Spain Election 2026 hub. The poll gives no sample size.

Other Surveys Point The Other Way

Sigma Dos, a Spanish polling firm, interviewed voters on 29-30 October and found the PP on 31.1%, the PSOE on 24.6% and Vox on 19.3%. It projects 97 to 103 seats for the PSOE and 196 to 208 for the PP and Vox combined.

Sondaxe, another Spanish pollster, interviewed on 26-28 October and found the PP on 29.2%, the PSOE on 26.9% and Vox on 19.2%. Hamalgama Métrica, a Spanish polling firm, interviewed on 22-28 October and projects 137 seats for the PP, 106 for the PSOE and 70 for Vox.

The PolitPro aggregate, a weighted average of institutes, stood on 6 November at PP 29.8%, PSOE 26% and Vox 18.8%. It translates that into 128 seats for the PP, 112 for the PSOE and 81 for Vox.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, a crypto-based prediction market, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, the PP leader, was priced at 91.5% to become the next prime minister on 6 November at 6:22 a.m. ET, with Sánchez at 7.8% and Vox leader Abascal at 1.4%. About US$2.8 million has been traded on the market.

Feijóo stood at 84% on 3 November. Prices are bets rather than polls and can move quickly.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

File photo, undated: the Gran Vía, Madrid’s main shopping boulevard. (Photo: Felipe Gabaldón, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

The Calendar And The Backdrop

Spain votes on Sunday, 29 November, after Sánchez called a snap election on 5 October, three days after Congress rejected two housing decrees. The PP, Vox and Junts, a Catalan party, were among those who voted against, and the vote had been due in 2027.

The new Congress meets on 23 December, and only then can a new prime minister take office. A one-on-one debate between Sánchez and Feijóo is reported for Monday, 16 November, and a four-way debate is planned for Thursday, 26 November.

A high-speed train collision near Urda, in Toledo province, killed 69 people on 28 October. Transport Minister Óscar Puente resigned on 3 November and gave up leading the PSOE list for Valladolid.

Some outlets tie the PSOE's drop to about 100 seats in certain polls to the crash. His name stays on the printed ballot in Valladolid.

What It Means for US Readers

Spain's 29 November vote will decide whether one of Europe's remaining left-leaning governments survives. Polling averages and prediction markets both still point to a PP-led outcome, and Rio Times shows them side by side.

A single poll showing a Socialist lead is a reason to watch the next surveys, not yet a change in the race.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the SW Demoscopia result reflects a real Socialist recovery or is an outlier. The poll gives no sample size, and nearly all other private polls we reviewed show the PP ahead, while Spain's state polling institute (CIS) showed the PSOE ahead in October.

Broadcasters and times for the debates are not confirmed. Reports conflict on where the one-on-one is shown, and the PSOE and PP disagree over whether RTVE or Atresmedia hosts the four-way debate.

SW Demoscopia is the only poll we found fielded after Puente's resignation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which poll puts the Socialists ahead in Spain?

SW Demoscopia, published on 5 November, gives the PSOE 29.8% and the PP 29.1%. It contradicts most other private polls, which show the PP ahead.

When is Spain’s general election?

Spain votes on Sunday, 29 November 2026, for the Congress of Deputies and the Senate. The new Congress meets on 23 December, and only then can a new prime minister take office.

Who do prediction markets favor?

On Polymarket, Alberto Núñez Feijóo was priced at 91.5% to become the next prime minister on 6 November at 6:22 a.m. ET, against 7.8% for Pedro Sánchez. These are betting-market prices, not polls.

Is the Socialist lead real?

It is not known. The poll gives no sample size, and nearly all other private polls we reviewed show the PP ahead.

World.title: Turkey Closes Key Road for UN Climate Summit
World.content:
Key Facts When and where. COP31, the UN climate conference, runs Nov. 9-20 at the Antalya Expo Center in Turkey.

Leaders’ Summit. Nov. 11-12. The Leaders’ Road shuts 11:30 p.m. ET Nov. 10 to 4 a.m. ET Nov. 11 (7:30 a.m. to noon local).

Who Is Coming. Turkey says 91 heads of state and government have confirmed, up from 85 on Oct. 22. No independent count exists.

Time Gap. Antalya is 8 hours ahead of US Eastern time, so 9 a.m. there is 1 a.m. ET.

Published Friday, Nov. 6, 6:30 a.m. ET (2:30 p.m. Antalya) · Source: Turkish government and Antalya governor’s office statements, Rio Times research

What Is Fixed in the Calendar

COP31, the 31st UN climate conference, runs from Nov. 9 to Nov. 20, 2026, at the Antalya Expo Center in southern Turkey. Our full coverage sits in the dossier COP31 climate summit Antalya (leaders 11-12 Nov).

The leaders' summit is set for Nov. 11-12. Turkey holds the COP31 presidency, a role that chairs and steers the talks.

Environment Minister Murat Kurum serves as COP31 President. Australia's Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen is President of Negotiations, a role that runs the bargaining sessions.

President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan hosts the summit. Turkish officials outlined on Sept. 26 that he and UN Secretary-General António Guterres welcome the leaders, and Erdoğan, Guterres and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese then speak, with a gala dinner hosted by Erdoğan and his wife closing the first day.

What Has Changed on the Ground

Turkey said on Oct. 31 that 91 heads of state and government have confirmed, up from 85 cited by Kurum on Oct. 22. Brazil's presidency has confirmed that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will attend with Health Minister Alexandre Padilha.

The provincial governor's office said the "Leaders' Road," a stretch of the D-400 highway from the Belek Tourism Road junction to the Land of Legends junction, will be fully closed from 7:30 a.m. to noon local time on Nov. 11. That is 11:30 p.m. ET on Nov. 10 to 4 a.m. ET on Nov. 11, and EXPO 2016 Boulevard, the avenue serving the venue, will be limited to official vehicles and shuttle buses during the summit period.

Antalya Governor Hulusi Şahin said on Nov. 2 that preparations were complete to move to remote learning on Nov. 11 and 12 in seven districts: the five central districts (Muratpaşa, Kepez, Konyaaltı, Aksu and Döşemealtı) plus Serik and Manavgat, to ease traffic during the COP31 leaders’ summit, with the final decision resting with the national Education Ministry.

File photo: Anıtkabir in Ankara, Turkey’s capital. COP31 itself takes place in Antalya, on the southern coast. (Photo: Diego Delso, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

What Is at Stake

Negotiators are expected to focus on implementing earlier pledges, moving away from fossil fuels and climate finance for poorer countries. Turkey's presidency has named 10 action-agenda priorities, including zero waste, green industrialization and clean energy.

They sit on a separate track from the formal negotiations. The presidency has launched the Antalya Compact for Energy Efficient Buildings, which is open for endorsement by all countries that are parties to the UN climate convention.

The Venue and the Public Zone

The site covers about 1.1 million square meters, including a Blue Zone of 527,000 square meters for negotiations. A 582,000-square-meter Green Zone is meant for public activities with concerts, exhibitions and talks.

More than 45,000 people from 154 countries have applied to volunteer, and nearly 2,000 Turkish nongovernmental organizations and municipalities have sought to take part.

What It Means for US Readers

Antalya runs on Turkey time (UTC+3, three hours ahead of Greenwich), which is 8 hours ahead of US Eastern time after US clocks went back on Nov. 1, and 11 hours ahead of Pacific time. Our calculation: a 9 a.m. session in Antalya starts at 1 a.m. ET the same day.

We have not verified a public livestream. The organiser's site, cop31.tr, and the UN climate secretariat's (UNFCCC) site are the places to check for webcasts and schedules.

What Is Not Known

The organiser has not published, in the material we reviewed, an opening-ceremony or plenary start time. We could not read the official site cop31.tr directly, so the dates and venue rest on Turkish government statements and press reports.

The 91-leader figure is the Turkish government's own count, and we found no independent tally or confirmed list of who will attend. We also found no confirmed US delegation or White House announcement.

We found nothing on whether China's President Xi Jinping will attend. Attendance forecasts differ widely and we could not reconcile them.

We also found no prediction-market odds on COP31.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does COP31 start?

COP31, the UN climate conference, runs from Nov. 9 to Nov. 20, 2026, in Antalya, Turkey. The organiser has not confirmed an opening time.

When is the leaders’ summit?

The leaders’ summit is Nov. 11-12. The road to the venue closes from 7:30 a.m. to noon local time on Nov. 11, or 11:30 p.m. ET Nov. 10 to 4 a.m. ET Nov. 11.

How many leaders will attend?

Turkey says 91 heads of state and government have confirmed, up from 85 on Oct. 22. This is the government’s own figure, and we found no independent count.

How can US readers follow COP31?

Antalya is 8 hours ahead of US Eastern time. We have not verified a public livestream, so check cop31.tr and the UN climate secretariat’s site for webcasts.

World.title: Emilio and Elvis Zabaneh, Tersi Aguilar charged with human trafficking in Dangriga
World.content:
Emilio and Elvis Zabaneh, Tersi Aguilar charged with human trafficking in Dangriga

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Three members of the well-known Zabaneh family of southern Belize, including an 88-year-old businessman, his son and his son’s common-law wife, have been charged with human trafficking following disturbing allegations involving a Salvadoran woman recruited to work as a caregiver.

Emilio Quinonez Zabaneh, 88, his son Elvis Christian Zabaneh, 36, and Tersi Amini Aguilar, 34, appeared in the Dangriga Magistrate’s Court on Thursday, November 5, where they were each granted bail of $7,000.

The charges stem from a September 2023 investigation by the Belize Police Department’s Anti-Trafficking in Persons Unit.

According to police documents, the Salvadoran woman claims she was recruited by Emilio Zabaneh in El Salvador with the promise of earning US$500 monthly to care for him, along with accommodation and paid travel expenses.

However, after arriving in Belize on August 15, 2023, she allegedly experienced verbal abuse, sexual harassment, forced labour and threats of imprisonment.

The woman told investigators that Emilio demanded sexual acts, including sexual intercourse, which she refused. She alleged that he subsequently threatened to report her to immigration authorities and have her jailed.

She further claimed that Elvis withheld her passport despite repeated requests for its return and threatened to have her imprisoned if she attempted to leave the family’s Havana Street property.

According to the police summary of facts, the woman was fed only twice daily, made to sleep on a small sofa and permitted to shower only once a day.

She also alleged that Elvis and Aguilar required her to perform extensive household chores, including sweeping, mopping, ironing and cleaning bathrooms, despite her employment agreement being specifically for caregiving.

Although promised US$500 monthly, she reportedly received only BZ$150 during her stay, which she transferred to relatives in El Salvador.

On September 10, 2023, police conducted a rescue operation at the Zabaneh residence in Dangriga, removing the woman and placing her in the care of the Department of Human Services.

More than three years later, police formally arrested and charged the three accused.

Emilio faces one count of trafficking in persons for allegedly harbouring the woman through threats and coercion for the purpose of exploiting her through prostitution.

Elvis and Aguilar were jointly charged with a separate count of trafficking in persons for allegedly harbouring the woman through threats and coercion to compel her to perform forced labour.

The trio appeared before Senior Magistrate Mannon Dennison. Emilio was represented by attorney Andrew Bennett, while Elvis and Aguilar were represented by attorney David Morales.

No pleas were taken pending instructions from the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions on whether the cases will proceed summarily or on indictment before the High Court.

Each was granted bail of $7,000 with sureties and conditions restricting international travel and prohibiting contact with the complainant or her family.

The three are scheduled to return to court on November 18, 2026.

The allegations have not been proven in court.

World.title: AI could add US$48 million to Belize’s economy, study finds
World.content:
AI could add US$48 million to Belize’s economy, study finds

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Artificial intelligence could make Belize’s economy US$48 million larger within ten years, but the country has work to do to get its young people ready, according to a new study.

The Ayre Index, launched at the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting in Antigua and Barbuda, ranks Belize 35th out of 56 Commonwealth countries for youth AI readiness. Belize scored 42.8 out of 100, below the study’s readiness benchmark of 53. Only 15 Commonwealth countries reached that level.

The research, by the Ayre Think Tank founded by Antiguan Canadian entrepreneur Calvin Ayre, found strong internet access among young Belizeans. About 92.2% reported using the internet, 82.4% own a mobile phone and 4G coverage reaches 87% of the population. Belize scored 8 out of 10 for meaningful access.

But the picture changes when it comes to education and jobs. Belize scored just 2 out of 10 for education and training, with computing not recorded as part of the curriculum measure used. The study also found 22.5% of young people are not in employment, education or training.

Using International Monetary Fund scenarios, researchers estimate AI could lift Belize’s GDP by US$48 million after ten years. The conservative estimate is US$23 million, while the optimistic case reaches US$73 million.

Belize has about 112,000 young people aged 15 to 29.

World.title: International News: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigns amid banking crisis
World.content:
International News: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña resigns amid banking crisis

By Zoila Palma: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has announced his resignation amid a financial scandal surrounding Ueno Bank, which was shut down following a solvency crisis that left millions of customers unable to access their money.

Today, Peña announced his decision saying it was intended to protect the country’s stability, social peace and public institutions.

In a statement posted on social media, Peña said his priority was the security of Paraguayans who had entrusted their savings to the country’s financial system.

He also apologized to the public, acknowledging that history would ultimately judge the events surrounding his administration. Peña took office in August 2023 for a five-year term, CNN reports.

Shortly after his resignation announcement, Paraguay’s Chamber of Deputies unanimously voted to initiate impeachment proceedings against him during a special session.

The charges were brought by 35 opposition lawmakers and members of the ruling party, who accused the president of alleged serious and systematic dereliction of duty. The Senate will determine whether the impeachment proceedings advance or whether to accept his resignation.

The controversy erupted following the intervention of Ueno Bank, a private financial institution to which Peña has been linked and which reportedly received millions of dollars in public funds during his administration. Among the institutions that placed funds with the bank was the Social Security Institute (IPS), which manages pensions for most Paraguayan workers.

Paraguay’s Central Bank reported that Ueno Bank’s solvency ratio had fallen below 50 percent of the required minimum following adjustments to its financial statements during a regularization process.

The bank serves approximately 2.9 million customers in a country of 6.1 million people, and its closure resulted in thousands of customers having their savings frozen.

World.title: Belize advances development of National Employment Policy for 2027–2031
World.content:
Belize advances development of National Employment Policy for 2027–2031

By Zoila Palma: The Ministry of Immigration, Governance and Labour, through its Labour Department, is advancing the development of Belize’s National Employment Policy 2027–2031 through a three-day stakeholder consultation workshop held from November 3 to 5, 2026.

The workshop was organized in collaboration with the International Labour Organization (ILO), with funding from the European Union, and brought together national stakeholders to help shape the country’s employment priorities for the next five years.

The opening ceremony featured remarks from Chief Executive Officer Tanya Santos and CEO Valentino Shal of the Ministry of Rural Transformation, Community Development and Local Government.

Minister of Immigration, Governance and Labour Kareem Musa delivered the keynote address and officially opened the workshop. Abdelmalik Muhummed, Employment and Labour Market Policies Specialist with the ILO Decent Work Team and Office for the Caribbean, also introduced the objectives and consultation process.

Throughout the 3 days, participants examined eight key policy areas, including youth employment and the transition from school to work, women’s participation in the workforce, skills development, productivity, job quality, formalization and foreign labour. Discussions also addressed the inclusion of underrepresented groups, workforce development and labour market governance.

The final day focused on identifying policy priorities, institutional responsibilities, implementation gaps and the resources needed to put the proposed policy into action. The consultations provided an opportunity for stakeholders to share experiences, identify challenges and make recommendations toward developing a comprehensive employment framework that responds to Belize’s changing labour market.

The Ministry acknowledged the leadership of Labour Commissioner Rissela Dominguez Patt and the Labour Department, as well as the technical assistance provided by the ILO and financial support from the European Union.

Special recognition was also given to CEO Valentino Shal for his early vision and support in initiating the policy’s development.

World.title: Escape the winter cold with an Ambergris Caye vacation at Las Terrazas Resort and Residences
World.content:
Escape the winter cold with an Ambergris Caye vacation at Las Terrazas Resort and Residences

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): As winter approaches in North America, travellers looking to exchange freezing temperatures for sunshine, turquoise waters and Caribbean relaxation can find an inviting escape at Las Terrazas Resort and Residences on Ambergris Caye, Belize.

Located on one of Belize’s most popular island destinations, Las Terrazas offers a tropical retreat for couples, families and travellers seeking a memorable winter getaway.

Ambergris Caye is known for its beautiful Caribbean waters, access to the Belize Barrier Reef, snorkeling, diving, fishing and laid-back island atmosphere. Visitors can spend their days exploring the sea, enjoying local cuisine or simply relaxing beneath swaying palm trees.

This winter, Las Terrazas is making the experience even more attractive with three special vacation offers.

Stay four nights, get the fifth night free. Travellers booking a five-night getaway can enjoy the fifth night complimentary. The offer is advertised as valid through December 15, 2026.

Stay four nights and receive US$100 resort credit. Guests booking four consecutive nights or more can receive a US$100 resort credit per room, per stay, adding extra value to their island vacation.

Complimentary couples massage. Couples booking three consecutive nights or more can enjoy a complimentary 60-minute couples massage, making the resort an appealing option for romantic escapes.

Beyond the special offers, Ambergris Caye provides an excellent base for exploring Belize’s marine attractions, including snorkeling excursions and visits to the surrounding reef.

For travellers planning a December holiday or an early winter escape, the resort’s promotions offer several ways to enjoy more of Belize while adding value to their stay.

Visitors can explore the available packages and booking conditions at Las Terrazas Resort website: https://lasterrazasresort.com/offers.
