World.title: Ermistu defense park and ammunition depot alarm local residents
World.content:
Residents near Estonia's largest planned defense industry park are worried about safety, noise and environmental impact, particularly from an adjacent ammunition depot planned.

The Ermistu development covers 204 hectares of previously forested land near Pärnu. The ammunition depot will cover a further 100 or more hectares;, Defense Ministry says officials have met residents, with their safety being a priority.

The planning process has already been met with legal challenges, however.

One local resident, Külly Selberg, who lives in nearby Päraküla, said to "Aktuaalne kaamera": "If this entire complex is hit as a result of an accident or an attack, what will happen and what will be left of us?"

Selberg said no one had instructed villagers on how to act in the event of danger; the Ministry of Defense says officials have met residents in the surrounding towns of Tõstamaa, Audru and Pärnu.

Indrek Sirp, special adviser on defense industry development at the ministry, said ammunition production is subject to extremely strict regulations. "Safety is the number one priority. Safety must be ensured, as must security, which is why the area will be guarded and protected," Sirp said.

Sufficient separation between storage facilities, for instance, means these must also be located sufficiently far apart.

There are a total of 63 households within a 3km radius of the planned park.

Liina Käär, a resident of Lõuka village, chose to live in the Ermistu area due to its peace and quiet and clean air. However, even with construction only in its early stages, this has already changed: Power lines are being installed and roads built, and trucks often drive through the village, at some speed, she said.

Residents are also disturbed about plans for an open waste burning site and an ammunition testing ground. The Estonian Center for Defense Investments (RKIK) said most industrial waste will be burned in an enclosed incinerator, with open burning reserved for exceptional cases.

Ivar Kaldasaun, the RKIK's defense industry park portfolio manager, said regular detonations would not become a feature of life for residents local to Ermistu. Tests involving 5-10kg of explosives would be carried out on just three days in a year, he said. "It's not as though there will be loud explosions here every day."

Residents have also expressed concerned about the effects on the ecosystem of the Männiku River, which flows through the site. Since the summer the Environmental Board has been getting numerous reports that the water, a spawning ground for salmonids, is being polluted as a result of the work. The Board's deputy director general, Olav Avarsalu, said results show higher levels of pollution during heavy rainfall, when rainwater washes clay sediment into the river. "But so far, only one set of samples has shown levels exceeding the permitted limits," he said.

Construction of the main infrastructure at the defense park is scheduled to begin next summer.

Background:

The first four tenants of the Ermistu facility were named in October 2025 — Estonian firms Nitrotol, Frankenburg Technologies and Infinitum Strike, plus UK-based Thor Industries — producing mines and explosive charges, short-range air defense missiles, missile boosters and plastic explosives, with the state leasing land for up to 70 years and RKIK building the infrastructure.

Forest clearance on about 40 hectares of the roughly 200-hectare site was completed in February 2026, and phase two, the companies' own production facilities, was due to begin in the autumn.

Litigation is still running: the Päraküla Society, Roheline Pärnumaa, Eesti Metsa Abiks and 27 individuals are challenging the August 2025 spatial plan, and in July 2026 the Tallinn Administrative Court postponed its decision to take further evidence on noise, having found that the park's noise cannot be treated as national defense noise and must meet industrial noise standards.

The Ermistu park is one of three planned defense parks in Estonia, in the changed security situation. The other two are located at Ämari and Põhja-Kiviõli in Ida-Viru County

World.title: Police detain suspects in killing of elderly woman in Viljandi
World.content:
Police in Viljandi on Thursday evening found the body of a 77-year-old woman with signs of violence in the trunk of a car and detained three men, ages 48, 75 and 75, on suspicion of murder.

Margus Sass, head of the Viljandi Police Station, said police launched a search immediately after receiving a missing person report.

As officers searched the area around the woman's home, they discovered indications that a crime may have occurred there and expanded the search effort. Police used a service dog and a drone, while surface rescue personnel and divers from a special unit searched a pond near the woman's home.

Investigators also spoke with relatives and acquaintances, reviewed surveillance footage from nearby areas and businesses, and gathered information about the woman's movements on the day before her disappearance.

"Hommik Anuga" Autor/allikas: Ken Mürk/ERR

To locate both the woman and her vehicle, police appealed to the public and the media for assistance.

On Thursday evening, a member of the public reported seeing a vehicle matching the description in Viljandi. Officers dispatched to verify the tip located the missing woman's car parked outside an apartment building. The body of the 77-year-old woman, showing signs of violence, was found in the trunk.

Police suspect three men were involved in the crime. All three were detained Thursday evening in Viljandi with the assistance of a rapid response unit.

The suspects, ages 48, 75 and 75, were taken to the Viljandi Police Station for investigative procedures.

The investigation is being conducted by the South Prefecture and led by the South District Prosecutor's Office.

Prosecutor Andraš Tšitškan said preliminary information suggests the victim may have previously known at least one of the suspects.

At present, prosecutors are seeking the pretrial detention of the 48-year-old man, who is currently considered the principal suspect. According to prosecutors, he has previously been convicted multiple times of fraud and money laundering.

Evidence gathered during the investigation will be used to determine the role played by the other two men and whether there are grounds to seek their detention as well.

The motive for the crime, the suspects' roles and other circumstances will be established during the criminal investigation.

World.title: Gallery: Estonian National Museum puts its silver collection on display
World.content:
More than 400 goldsmiths worked in Estonia between 1918 and 1944, ranging from master craftsmen who owned their own businesses and workshops to artisans who fulfilled orders for larger companies. The Estonian National Museum's (ERM) new exhibition, "Estonian Silver Between the Wars," showcases the craftsmanship, aesthetic sensibility and creative diversity of the country's goldsmiths during that period.

"In a young, newly independent country, there really was an extraordinary range of objects that simply had to be made of silver. Perhaps it was partly a feature of those early years that even the prize for every milking competition had to be made of silver," said Maris Klaas, head of content at ERM.

"When we think of goldsmiths today, we primarily think of jewelry, but back then they produced an enormous range of everyday objects. You could say it's a lost world. What surprised me about this period was just how many objects were made featuring scenes of Estonia. Whether it was a cigar box, a spoon handle or a shot glass, they would be engraved with a view of an Estonian city — Tartu, Tallinn, Narva, Viljandi and so on. I would never have imagined that making such objects was so popular," said exhibition curator Riina Reinvelt.

The exhibition was preceded by several years of research, during which thousands of archival records were examined and objects held in various collections were studied. It is the most comprehensive overview to date of the goldsmiths of this period, their lives and their work.

"The assay office's archives were destroyed in 1944 and nobody knew which maker's mark belonged to whom. We haven't managed to find an object bearing every maker's mark we know of. There were none in museum collections or private collections. I also kept an eye on the osta.ee online marketplace and some objects were actually purchased there for the museum's collection precisely because they bore a maker's mark for which no examples had previously been found. I think more discoveries will emerge," Reinvelt said.

The exhibition "Estonian Silver Between the Wars: Well-Known and Lesser-Known Silversmiths, 1918–1944" is on display in the Estonian National Museum's gallery from November 6 through August 29, 2027.

World.title: Planet42 middleman charged with offering financial services without a license
World.content:
The District Prosecutor's Office for Economic and Corruption Crimes has sent a criminal case to court, charging well-known investor Jaak Roosaare with providing financial services without a license.

According to the charges, Roosaare raised money from the public between 2020 and 2024 through companies he managed, with the aim of lending it on to Inclusion OÜ, which operated under the Planet42 brand. Prosecutors allege that Roosaare's companies did not have the license required by the Estonian Financial Supervision Authority (FSA) to raise funds in this way.

Piia Enno, the prosecutor leading the proceedings, noted that investment intermediation and raising funds from the public are regulated for a reason.

"The licensing requirement is not a mere formality. Its purpose is to ensure that companies raising money from individuals meet the requirements set out in law. According to the charges, substantial amounts of money were raised from the public over several years in this case, despite the absence of the required license," Enno said.

According to the charges, a public investment blog and newsletter were among the channels used to raise funds and the companies managed by Roosaare received a total of more than €15 million from lenders.

"The prosecution therefore considers that these were not isolated private loan transactions, but rather activities for which the law requires a license from the FSA," Enno explained.

Between August 2020 and the end of May 2023, Roosaare signed at least 448 loan agreements with various Estonian companies on behalf of the businesses he managed. According to the charges, individual loans ranged from €1,000 to €90,000. Fundraising continued after May 2023, while interest payments were made until May 2024.

The money was then lent through these companies to Inclusion OÜ, which provided long-term car rental services in South Africa and Latin America under the Planet42 brand.

In late July 2024, Planet42 abruptly suspended all loan interest and principal repayments to its hundreds of Estonian creditors, citing severe financial pressure and a rapid liquidity crunch.

Criminal proceedings against Jaak Roosaare were launched following a criminal complaint filed by the Financial Supervision Authority.

ERR also attempted to contact Roosaare for comment, but his phone was switched off.

The criminal case has been sent to Harju County Court for trial.

World.title: Jude’s brother Jobe Bellingham gets England call-up
World.content:
London – Jobe Bellingham was named alongside older brother Jude in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the first time on Friday as Chelsea’s Cole Palmer missed out.

Fulham teenager Josh King is also handed his first call-up ahead of Nations League games against Croatia and Spain later this month.

Tuchel said Palmer “misses too many opportunities” to impress at international level after pulling out of England’s last squad due to injury.

The Chelsea star, who was not included for the World Cup, has been left out as Tuchel takes the chance to look at younger options with a place in the quarter-finals of the Nations League almost guaranteed

Jobe Bellingham has been rewarded for a strong start to his second season at Borussia Dortmund, where Jude also played for three seasons before moving to Real Madrid.

King has impressed despite Fulham’s struggles in the Premier League, while Liverpool’s 18-year-old winger Rio Ngumoha is also included.

England are second in group A3 after four games, with three wins and a defeat, against Spain at Wembley.

The Three Lions host Croatia, who they beat 7-0 last month, on Thursday before travelling to take on Spain with just one point needed to qualify for the knockout rounds in March.

Newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane is set to surpass Peter Shilton as England’s most capped male player after moving level with the former goalkeeper on 125 appearances against the Czech Republic last time out.

Squad in full:

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), Jason Steele (Brighton), James Trafford (Leeds)

Defenders: Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid/ESP), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Marc Guehi (Manchester City), Lewis Hall (Newcastle), Ezri Konsa, Ben White (both Arsenal), Djed Spence (Inter Milan/ITA), Jarell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen/GER)

Midfielders: Elliot Anderson (Manchester City), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid/ESP), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund/GER), James Garner (Everton), Josh King (Fulham), Myles Lewis-Skelly, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze (all Arsenal)

Forwards: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich/GER), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona/ESP), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest)

World.title: Auto sector propels growth in German factory output
World.content:
Frankfurt – A rebound in car production gave German factory output a bigger boost than expected in September, official data showed Friday, the latest sign Europe’s largest economy was gaining strength.

Auto sector production jumped around 17 percent from a month earlier following a sluggish period caused largely by factory holidays and plant maintenance over the summer.

It was nevertheless some rare good news from an industry that has been hard hit by fierce Chinese competition, falling demand and rising costs.

This helped lift overall industrial production by 0.7 percent for the month, said statistics agency Destatis, above analyst expectations of a far smaller increase.

The economy ministry said the data “helped offset the declines in industrial production seen in the middle of the year,” caused by factors like higher energy costs linked to the Middle East war and low water levels on rivers.

Germany’s economy is struggling to pull itself out of long decline driven by weakening demand for its exports, Chinese competition and a range of deep-rooted problems.

But the manufacturing powerhouse is expected to notch up its fastest growth for several years in 2026, in large part due to a public spending blitz on defence and infrastructure.

September’s factory data was also helped by the pharmaceutical sector, which registered eight percent growth.

But there were falls in the construction sector and in manufacturing of machinery and equipment, Destatis said.

Despite September’s positive data, Dirk Schumacher, chief economist at German public lender KfW, cautioned that the economy continued to face headwinds.

“There remains a long list of risk factors that could bring the industrial recovery to an end before it has even really got going,” he said.

“The nervousness in the financial markets regarding the further expansion of AI infrastructure is just one example of this.”

World.title: Iran exempts Iraq from Strait of Hormuz restrictions as oil exports rise
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iran has confirmed that Iraqi ships are free from its Strait of Hormuz restrictions, enabling them to transit through the crucial waterway despite the continuous interruptions caused by the regional strife.

On Tuesday, Amir Moqaddam, Deputy Head of the Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, stated that Iraq, China, India, and Qatar had been given exemptions, enabling their vessels to pass the strait.

The exemption is especially important for Iraq, which depends significantly on oil exports for government income and has had enormous difficulty since the Strait of Hormuz was essentially blocked with the commencement of the US-Israel war with Iran in February 2026.

According to maritime analytics company Kpler, Iraq’s crude oil exports via the strait surged from 1.69 million barrels per day in August to 2.65 million barrels per day in October, showing that export volumes had recovered despite the continuing violence.

Iran had earlier issued an exception for Iraqi vessels in April, citing Iraq as a neighboring nation with strong relations to Tehran. The most recent statement maintains that agreement.

While Iran intends to collect transit fees from some nations, it is unclear if Iraqi vessels would be obliged to pay.

The exception might bring significant relief to Iraq’s oil industry, allowing it to continue export profits while reducing economic pressures.

However, there is still concern about maritime security in the area, since the US maintains a separate naval embargo targeting boats entering or departing Iranian ports.

Although the Iranian exception permits Iraqi ships to pass through Tehran’s limitations, it does not guarantee safe passage in light of ongoing military tensions and assaults on commercial boats in the Gulf.

World.title: Beijing seeks to bolster AI shares
World.content:
Tokyo – After recent sharp drops for some Chinese tech stocks, Beijing is trying to prop them up — seeing the sector, and in particular AI, as a central strategic priority.

In August, buzzy Chinese startup Unitree, whose walking, dancing humanoids are often used by AI researchers trying to make robots act autonomously, went public.

Its shares skyrocketed on its Shanghai debut in August — but almost three months later they are down 40 percent from their peak that day.

Chinese chipmakers Moore Threads and MetaX — touted as challengers to US behemoth Nvidia — have both plunged by around 50 percent over the past six months.

Similar steep falls can be seen across Shanghai’s tech-focused Star50 index, China’s answer to Wall Street’s Nasdaq, which is down only around six percent over the same period.

Volatility on Wall Street hasn’t helped — the Nasdaq plunged 5.5 percent on Thursday — with fears that the vast sums spent on AI infrastructure will not translate into big profits.

However, the Chinese government is taking steps.

Officials this week reactivated liquidity-injection tools aimed at encouraging share purchases while boosting the trading volume of state-backed investment funds, according to local media reports.

On Tuesday, net capital inflows into nine exchange-traded funds (ETFs), commonly used by Beijing to prop up the market, reached 120 billion yuan ($18 billion) — a near-record, according to Bloomberg data, targeting tech stocks in particular.

The Financial Times also reported this week that Chinese regulators had told banks to halt company listings in an attempt to boost market liquidity.

“Chinese technology shares have been under significant pressure, with investors concerned about weak domestic demand, intense competition and disappointing earnings,” said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets.

However, now “fresh policy support, lower valuations and hopes of improving sentiment are encouraging investors to revisit a sector that has struggled for much of the year”, she added.

– Packed to the rafters –

Overall, tech investors in China remain optimistic, said Ajin Jin, partner at Shanghai-based investment firm Kunquan.

“In both Beijing and Shanghai, weekly roadshows are still taking place, and every single one is packed to the rafters, with people even sitting in the aisles,” he said.

Li Daxiao, one of China’s most prominent investment gurus, also said “the burgeoning development of the industry is unstoppable” and should be clearly distinguished from “share price fluctuations”.

“Technology shares have been affected by external risks and have fallen in tandem with their counterparts in the US, Japan and South Korea,” he told AFP.

Stephen Inness of SPI Asset Management said that “a state-backed effort would add to steps taken by China last month to stabilise its equity market”.

However, he warned the measures “have so far proved insufficient against the backdrop of a weak domestic economy and doubts over AI earnings”.

World.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto’ set for blockbuster return after 13 years
World.content:
Paris – Fans of the violent “Grand Theft Auto” video game franchise are just two weeks away from getting their hands on the latest edition, which has taken almost a decade to make and has become the most expensive title in history.

The franchise allows players to act out gangster fantasies — shooting up bars, crashing cars — in fictional renderings of US cities where the soundtrack piped through in-game radio is almost as important as the cutting-edge visuals.

GTA VI, which comes 13 years after its predecessor, is expected to break sales records when it lands on November 19 thanks in part to a monumental marketing campaign that kicked off in late 2023 with the first official trailer.

“It is going to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time,” Chris Dring of The Game Business outlet told AFP.

The previous edition, GTA V, is still the second-biggest selling game ever — it took just three days to rack up $1 billion in sales, two days less than the movie “Avengers: Endgame”.

The budget of GTA VI has reportedly ballooned to over $1 billion — far higher than any other game or film — and projections have it on track to make several billion in its first week, which would smash all records for any cultural product.

– ‘Top creators’ –

‘GTA VI’ has two main protagonists, former drug-runner Jason and newly released ex-con Lucia, who try to survive in Vice City, a reimagining of Miami.

Lucia is the first playable woman character in a main edition of the almost 30-year history of a franchise.

During the 1990s and 2000s the game’s graphic depictions of sex, violence and misogyny became notorious — tabloid media outrage boosting the title’s notoriety and helping sales to skyrocket.

Rockstar Games has spent eight years developing the sixth edition, a process beset by difficulties including the leak of development footage and code for the game online in 2022.

But expectations are sky-high.

“They’ve spent a long time on this game, but they are probably the top game entertainment creators in the world,” said Dring.

Analysts expect the game to have an impact on the entire video game sector, including on console sales and accessories.

Several other studios delayed the release of new games to avoid being caught in the hype cycle around GTA VI.

Analysis firm Sensor Tower said the game had already generated around $750 million from pre-sales.

Surveys suggested almost one-third of the 49 million people who use PS5 and Xbox Series consoles in the United States intended to buy the game.

“The purchase intent that we’re seeing on ‘Grand Theft Auto’ is far away above any other game we’ve ever tracked,” said Mat Piscatella of consultancy Circana.

“For me, it’s the game of the decade,” Jocelin Lebeau, 39, a gamer who works for the French military, told AFP at a recent event in Paris. “I’m ready to buy it sight unseen.”

World.title: Carrick fights for Man Utd job ahead of international break
World.content:
London – Michael Carrick takes charge of Manchester United for what could be the last time against Aston Villa this weekend as he battles to save his job despite a morale-boosting midweek victory over Roma.

United’s dramatic win in the Champions League gave the coach breathing space but he remains under intense pressure ahead of the international break.

Elsewhere in the Premier League, Manchester City will be seeking to avoid a rare third straight league defeat when they face Nottingham Forest as they try to keep pace with leaders Arsenal.

AFP Sport looks at three talking points ahead of the action:

Carrick’s last chance?

When Manchester United’s players trudged off at half-time against Roma on Tuesday, 2-0 down and seemingly out of ideas, Michael Carrick’s fate appeared to be sealed.

Instead, his underperforming team somehow turned things around, with Matheus Cunha scoring two late goals in a 3-2 win at a feverish Old Trafford.

It ended a run of nine games without a victory — United’s longest winless run since the 1988/89 season.

Defender Diogo Dalot said he hopes the Roma result can kickstart their season.

“Nights like this can change momentum, can change seasons, and I think this win is going to give us confidence for the next games,” he said.

But the brutal reality is that United could be bottom of the Premier League when they kick off on Sunday if results go against them.

Whatever the outcome, the international break will give the club’s hierarchy an opportunity to consider their long-term options.

Villa’s Spanish manager, Unai Emery, was tipped as a potential candidate for the Old Trafford hot seat but reports suggest he is close to signing a new deal with the Birmingham club.

Two-way title race?

Manchester City know that even if they keep pace with Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain.

The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules — with a huge points deduction one potential punishment.

Arsenal appear to be the only other serious contender for the title, having the happy knack of winning even when below par.

On paper, both clubs face a straightforward task this weekend, though City’s trip to Nottingham Forest could be trickier than it looks.

Opta’s “expected points” table, which orders the Premier League based on expected goals for and against, has Oliver Glasner’s team in third — a remarkable 16 places higher than they are in the real table.

Arsenal, who host struggling Hull, have won 18 of their past 19 Premier League games against promoted sides.

Things looking up for Spurs

The doom and gloom around Tottenham has lifted after a three-game winning streak in the Premier League under manager Roberto De Zerbi.

Less than three weeks ago Spurs, without a single win, propped up the division. They are now comfortably placed in mid-table.

Defender Archie Gray credits the spirit of the squad for the turnaround, which has the club just four points behind fourth-placed Chelsea.

“We all get on really well and you can see that out there on the pitch,” he told SpursPlay. “Even with the celebration(s), all the subs are running to the players and they are little things that mean so much to us. That’s the most important thing and why we’ve been improving.”

Daniel Farke’s Leeds are winless in their past five Premier League games and have scored just twice during that run, slipping to 12th in the table.

World.title: Israel faces new era of sinking US support after election
World.content:
Jerusalem – Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s brash campaign posters are still up on Israeli public buses — images of him, US President Donald Trump and soaring warjets that laud the two leaders attacking Iran together.

Neither is now advertising the state of the two countries’ alliance.

A week after an inconclusive election for Netanyahu, Americans overwhelmingly rejected Trump and chose a Congress led by Democrats who want a tougher approach to Israel, whether on Iran, Gaza or settler violence in the occupied West Bank.

The back-to-back elections look to many observers like a turning point, with Israel no longer able to take for granted the cover of the world’s most powerful country.

“This is a new era. The confluence of the Gaza war and the war with Iran have really changed how mainstream Americans — not people particularly concerned with the Israeli-Palestinian conflict — see Israel,” said Yael Sternhell, an expert on the United States at Tel Aviv University.

Vice President JD Vance, assessing why his Republicans fared poorly, listed four ways to bring voters back, including ending the Iran war and changing “our relationship with Israel”.

Trump did not disagree. Just as voting was underway Tuesday, Trump said he had agreed with Netanyahu to end the $3.8 billion in annual US military aid to Israel by the end of this year, explicitly tying the decision to the US political mood.

Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister who has served on and off for nearly two decades, had eagerly sought Trump’s endorsement but also acknowledged his country’s growing isolation.

In the final days of the campaign, he suggested Israel turn to cryptocurrencies to circumvent international sanctions he expected would intensify.

Netanyahu has not commented on the US election or Trump’s aid remarks.

Amit Segal, a journalist known for his proximity to Netanyahu, posted that the political situation in the United States marked a “catastrophe” for Israel.

– Can Eisenkot restore the alliance? –

Opposition contender Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to cobble together a coalition to oust Netanyahu, has cast himself as capable of repairing relations.

In an English-language statement, the former military chief said he believed in “liberal values” and also wanted to work “closely and constructively” with Trump.

Yair Golan, the main left-wing leader inside Eisenkot’s bloc, called for Israel to restore a bipartisan approach destroyed by Netanyahu who he said promoted a “destructive Israeli narrative of eternal war and authoritarian rule”.

Netanyahu boasted in his campaign about standing up to Democratic presidents including Barack Obama, who remains a hero for many Democrats. Netanyahu openly aligned with Republicans a decade ago to attack Obama’s diplomacy on Iran.

“Netanyahu certainly rubs Democrats the wrong way and has made every effort to alienate them,” Sternhell said.

“But Eisenkot can’t just be a nicer man to receive a softer approach from this new Congress,” she added. “He’s going to need new policies.”

She said Eisenkot would likely enjoy Israeli public support for cracking down on extremist settlers, who have attacked Palestinians in the West Bank with virtual impunity.

But Israel has shifted to the right, with wide initial support for the Gaza war.

– Broadening criticism of Israel –

The new Congress will include progressive Democrats such as Abdul El-Sayed, the first Muslim elected to the Senate, who describe the devastation in Gaza as genocide, an assertion rejected by Israel.

Netanyahu “made a bet not only on the Republicans but almost personally on Trump”, said Eli Kowaz, senior policy director of the Economic Cooperation Foundation, an Israeli think tank that backs a two-state solution with the Palestinians.

“These results show that bet had an expiry date,” Kowaz said. “Also, for the first time, really, I think there’s a realisation that it isn’t only about the Democrats. It’s a problem with the relationship with America.”

Without US assistance, Israel still has its own major arms industry and retains a clear edge fighting non-state actors such as Hamas and Hezbollah, said Ehud Eilam, a former researcher for the Israeli defence ministry.

But he said Israel would need to rely more on cheaper artillery or non-sophisticated bombs, further increasing risks of civilian casualties that have enraged international opinion.

“Israel can adjust to a new strategic reality of losing much and even all US military aid, but it will be tough for Israel. It will require Israel to consider hard choices such as taking huge loans or raising taxes,” Eilam said.

Kowaz said that Eisenkot, aware of politics in Washington, was trying to show he is interested in regional stability and strategic agreements and not just “an indefinite state of war”.

“He is definitely laying out a different vision for Israel’s relationship with the United States.”

World.title: Tech firms suffer bloodbath as US midterms fuel AI fears
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian tech firms suffered a bloodbath Friday as investors tracked a collapse on Wall Street fuelled by fears that Democrats will ramp up regulations of the AI industry following their blowout victory in this week’s US midterm elections.

Trading boards were a sea of red in early business, with Seoul and Tokyo taking the brunt of the selling as traders fled to the hills amid uncertainty about a sector that had pushed stock markets to record highs just five months ago.

While the historic “blue wave” in Tuesday’s vote had been initially welcomed on hopes it could put pressure on President Donald Trump to wind down his war against Iran, fears about the impact on the AI buildout soon came to the fore.

Data centres have faced broad opposition from US voters across the political spectrum, and many midterm winners have pledged to put the brakes on such projects.

Analysts said investors were also spooked by a call from progressive US Senator Bernie Sanders for a national moratorium on their building.

The results compounded already heightened fears about the hundreds of billions firms had pumped into the sector and when they would see a return, while the recent spike in borrowing costs also fuelled concerns about their financial position.

The eye-watering rally in many companies’ valuations had also caused unease on trading floors.

Michael Hewson at MCH Market Insights said investors were selling up because of “concerns that we might see greater opposition to AI buildout plans, with the results in Texas prompting concerns that politicians in the state might target Elon Musk’s Tesla and SpaceX due to his support for Trump”.

New York’s Nasdaq plunged 5.5 percent in its worst day — percentage-wise — since April last year when Trump unveiled his wide-ranging global tariffs. The S&P 500 tanked more than four percent and the Dow more than three percent.

Bloomberg said the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had collapsed around 16 percent this week, putting it on course for its worst run since April last year.

Trump blamed the collapse on the Democrats, writing on Truth Social: “The Stock Market crashed today because the Dumocrats had a big Tuesday — So sad to see, you only have yourselves to blame! President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

The heavy selling continued in Asia.

Seoul plunged almost nine percent at one point, with chip giant SK hynix off 10 percent while rival Samsung was eight percent down.

The Kospi more than doubled between the end of December and mid-June, when it hit a record, and has since then lost almost 50 percent.

Tokyo dived seven percent as Kioxia and SoftBank gave back more than 10 percent, with Advantest more than eight percent lower.

TSMC’s seven-percent drop dragged Taipei’s Taiex around eight percent lower.

Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney and Singapore were all down more than one percent, with Wellington and Manila also in the red.

“The blood is in the streets, folks,” said Neil Wilson at Saxo Markets.

“The fear is a total momentum unwind as Democrats pace the frontier and kibosh data centre buildout… this looks totally overdone but the nature of sell-everything of this market means we need to look for some stability first.”

The mood was also dampened by a fresh lift in oil prices, extending Thursday’s gains after plunging on the midterm results amid hopes for an end to the Iran war.

Traders were keeping eyes on developments in the crisis after US and Iranian leaders had indicated progress earlier in the week.

US jobs data is also due later in the day, following broadly positive readings earlier in the week.

World.title: '1,800 fake AI books, inflated prices': Periyar library pits CM Vijay against DMK
World.content:
Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday accused the previous

government of corruption in the purchase of books for Coimbatore's Periyar Knowledge World, days after allegations emerged that nearly 1,800 fake AI-generated books had been bought at inflated prices.

Vijay credited writer and professor

with exposing the alleged irregularities and said he deserved to be commended.

The controversy has also drawn in the Congress, with state party president Manickam Tagore demanding a comprehensive probe into the purchases. The demand puts the DMK, the Congress's former ally, under pressure to answer allegations of wrongdoing during its tenure.

The DMK, meanwhile, has accused the Vijay government of trying to take credit for a project built under its rule and covering up the name of its 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme at the newly inaugurated centre.



What are the allegations against DMK

The controversy centres on the purchase of books for Periyar Knowledge World, also known as Periyar Arivulagam, a library and science centre in Coimbatore.

Writer Perumal Murugan reportedly flagged alleged irregularities in the procurement process. Citing his allegations, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president Manickam Tagore claimed that nearly 1,800 fake, AI-generated books from Agalvilakku Pathippagam were purchased at inflated prices.





He also alleged that the books carried fabricated author and publisher details.

In a letter to Vijay, Tagore sought a comprehensive investigation into the alleged multi-crore corruption. He demanded that the disputed books be removed, those responsible identified and arrested, and similar purchases at other state-run libraries examined.

The Congress leader's intervention is politically significant because the allegations concern the previous DMK government, with which the Congress was previously allied.

His demand puts the spotlight on the DMK's record in office even as the party faces attacks from the ruling TVK.

Vijay calls DMK 'fountainhead of corruption'

Vijay seized on the allegations to launch a sharp attack on the DMK, accusing it of turning the institution into what he described as a centre of corruption.

Hitting out at the opposition party, the chief minister called it the "fountainhead of corruption" and alleged that its claims of building the institution after careful scrutiny had been undermined by the book procurement controversy.

"The DMK has engaged in corruption in a slightly different way, turning Coimbatore Periyar Knowledge World itself into a world of corruption," the ruling TVK founder alleged in a statement.

He further claimed that the DMK had a history of corruption, including in the awarding of tenders, and said the party would not be forgiven by future generations of Tamil Nadu.

"That the DMK is a party which built a very huge world of corruption for themselves is getting exposed one after the other," he alleged.

Vijay's remarks came on the day he inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam, which houses a library, a digital library and a planetarium.

Stalin defends the project

The DMK has sought to highlight the institution as a major project completed under its 'Dravidian Model' government.

Party president and former chief minister

visited the centre on Wednesday along with Dravidar Kazhagam president K Veeramani. He expressed satisfaction over its completion and urged students and young people to visit the facility to understand the principles and ideals of the Dravidian movement and Periyar.

Stalin said nearly 99.75% of the work had been completed and suggested that the project could have been abandoned had it been left unfinished.

"Fortunately, the Periyar Knowledge Centre has reached the stage of near completion. Had the project been left halfway, the current govt would have dropped the project and had brought it to a closure. Thankfully, it has escaped that fate," he remarked.

He also expressed hope that other library projects would be completed and opened to the public, saying such institutions could encourage reading and help younger generations understand Tamil Nadu's social reform movements.

Udhayanidhi targets CM Vijay

The DMK's criticism of the Vijay government has also focused on an alleged attempt to remove the previous regime's imprint from the institution.

Leader of Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly

Udhayanidhi Stalin

welcomed the inauguration of the centre but alleged that the name of the DMK government's 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme had been covered up at the premises.

In a post on X, Udhayanidhi said the facility had been built at a cost of Rs 290 crore under the previous government's 'Dravidian Model' and accused the TVK of taking credit for projects initiated by the DMK.

"Those who habitually 'stick their own labels' (take credit) on the schemes of our government have, this time, gone as far as covering up the name 'Naan Mudhalvan' (I am the First/Leader) at the Periyar Knowledge World. In this regimeâled by a 'cheap' chief minister obsessed with sticking his own labelsâwhat is the reason for not only undermining the 'Naan Mudhalvan' scheme but also refusing to even accept its name?" he said.

Questioning the alleged move, Udhayanidhi asked whether the word 'Mudhalvan' reminded the ruling party only of the DMK's leadership, or whether it did not want students to become leaders and top achievers.

"Instead of running a 'circus'âby covering up names given by our government, cancelling schemes, and then performing U-turns by 'cancelling the cancellations'âthis 'dummy' chief minister should focus on governing in the interest of the people."

While the Congress is seeking an investigation into the alleged book purchases, Vijay has used the allegations to target the DMK, which is accusing his government of erasing its contribution to the institution.

World.title: 'Inviting death': Jharkhand tribal leader dies by suicide after emotional Facebook Live post
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Jharkhand Tribal leader Nisha Kumari Bhagat was found dead at her residence in Ranchi on Friday, hours after allegedly going live on Facebook and speaking about threats she faced for raising her voice against the Jharkhand government and alleged land brokers.

Police suspect suicide, though the exact circumstances surrounding her death are yet to be established, according to the news agency PTI.

In the nearly 11-minute video, which was available on her Facebook profile, Bhagat is seen crying and alleging that speaking out against the "Hemant Soren government and its land brokers meant inviting death".

The video ends abruptly, with the camera apparently getting blocked by a green object.



Ranchi City Superintendent of Police Paras Rana told PTI that Bhagat's body was found hanging from a ceiling fan in a room at her house. Her body has been sent to the Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) for a post-mortem examination.

"Prima facie, it appears that she died by suicide after going live on social media. The exact reason behind the incident is yet to be ascertained," another police official said, adding that a detailed investigation has been launched.





Leader of the opposition Babulal Marandi expressed grief over Bhagat's death and alleged that she had been harassed for standing up for tribal rights.

Describing her as a young tribal leader who fought for her community, Marandi claimed that Bhagat had held chief minister Hemant Soren, the officer-in-charge of Pithoria police station and Ajay Tirkey responsible for her death in her video.

Sanjiv Kaura:

Aruna Lohia Goenka:

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Aruna Goenka for Times Foundation as part of the Knowledge Sharing Series and published by Times Internet's Spotlight team.

In this Diwali edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with iImpact catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka about abundance, one of the five pillars of her YASHA philosophy. From the paradox of wealthy people who feel poor to the extraordinary power of love, gratitude and consciousness, the conversation explores why prosperity begins not with what we possess, but with how we experience life.Diwali is a celebration of prosperity. But you seem to believe that abundance has very little to do with how much money we have.!(Laughs) Oh, Sanjiv! Money is wonderful. I have nothing against it.! But abundance is not a number in your bank account. Abundance is a feeling. And at its heart, it is a feeling of love. You can have very little and feel wonderfully abundant. Equally, you can possess extraordinary wealth and still feel desperately poor. Because poverty, too, can be a feeling.So, theoretically, I could be a billionaire and still be poor?(Smiles) Not theoretically, Sanjiv. Quite possibly! You can rule the world and still lack consciousness. You can have power over millions of people and yet have no mastery over your own mind. What good is owning the world if you wake up every morning feeling that something is missing? The opposite of abundance is not necessarily poverty. Sometimes, it is the inability to recognise what we already have.Take the example of Rajat Gupta, the former global head of McKinsey. Despite extraordinary professional success, he has spoken about feeling relatively poor when comparing himself with people whose wealth was vastly greater. Imagine that! A man who had reached the pinnacle of professional achievement could still experience a sense of not having enough!But isn't that rather difficult when the world constantly reminds us that somebody else has more?You have identified one of the greatest enemies of abundance: comparison. We look at someone else's house, car, career, success or lifestyle, and suddenly what made us happy yesterday seems inadequate today.! (Laughs) Isn't that extraordinary? Nothing has actually been taken away from us. Yet we have somehow managed to make ourselves feel poorer.! Comparison can turn abundance into scarcity without changing a single thing in our lives.You often speak about consciousness. But how does one actually develop an abundant consciousness?Begin by recognising what already exists in your life. Your health. Your relationships. The ability to learn. The opportunity to serve. The sunrise you did not have to purchase. The love you did not have to earn through a financial transaction. (Laughs) Imagine if the uUniverse started sending us invoices for sunlight, fresh air and the affection of our loved ones! We might suddenly discover that we are much wealthier than we thought. But gratitude is only the beginning. Abundant consciousness also means recognising possibilities where others see limitations, and opportunities to contribute where others see only competition.You mentioned love. Why is love so central to your understanding of abundance?Because love changes our relationship with the world. When we operate from scarcity, we ask, "What can I get?" When we operate from abundance, we begin asking, "What can I give?" Love, compassion, kindness and encouragement are extraordinary forms of wealth. And unlike many material possessions, sharing them does not diminish what we have. A candle loses nothing by lighting another candle. And on Diwali, isn't that a particularly beautiful thought?But surely we cannot tell someone struggling to feed their family that poverty is merely a feeling?Absolutely not! That would be both insensitive and wrong. Material deprivation is real. Hunger is real. Lack of healthcare, education and opportunity is real. We have a collective responsibility to address them. When I say poverty can also be a feeling, I am speaking about the inner experience of scarcity, not denying economic hardship. In fact, an abundant consciousness should make us more conscious of other people's suffering, not less. True abundance is not indifference to poverty. It is the determination to ensure that others can also flourish.Is there a danger that gratitude might make people complacent? If I feel I have enough, why strive for more?(Laughs) Sanjiv, gratitude is not retirement from ambition.! Be grateful for what you have while remaining excited about what you can create. The difference is whether your ambition comes from fear or possibility. Scarcity says, "I must achieve more because I am not enough." Abundance says, "I am grateful for who I am, and excited about what I can become." Contentment and ambition are not enemies. One gives us peace; the other gives us purpose.How does this philosophy of abundance connect with your YASHA vision for Viksit Bharat 2047?YASHA brings together Yuva, Anna, Shiksha, Hunar and Abundance. To me, aAbundance is also the spirit that connects the other four. What is the purpose of educating our children if they grow up believing that success means defeating somebody else? What is the purpose of developing skills if we do not use them to create opportunities for others? What is the purpose of prosperity if it does not lead to shared wellbeing?Imagine 1.4 billion people with an abundant consciousness. People who recognise their own possibilities, celebrate the success of others and contribute whatever they can to the nation. A Bharat where we do not measure our happiness by how much more our neighbour possesses, but by how much better we can make life for one another.One final Diwali message?This Diwali, light a lamp in your home. But also light one within your consciousness. Let it illuminate gratitude where there was comparison, love where there was fear,and possibility where there was scarcity. Don't wait to become wealthy to feel abundant. Feel abundant, and use that consciousness to create wealth - for yourself, for others and for Bharat.Because when 1.4 billion people begin to think, feel and act with abundance, Viksit Bharat 2047 will be much more than an economic achievement. It will be a flourishing of human consciousness. And that, Sanjiv, is what I call the magic of the Universe.

World.title: EC gives voters excluded from draft electoral rolls in 7 states another chance to apply
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Election Commission (EC) on Friday announced that voters excluded from the draft electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in seven states will be given another opportunity to have their names included in the final electoral rolls.

The directive applies to electors who were issued enumeration forms but were left out of the draft rolls after being categorised as Absent, Shifted, Dead or Duplicate (ASDD). The seven states covered are Delhi, Maharashtra, Haryana, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland.

The EC has also directed officials to put in place a monitoring mechanism to ensure that no eligible voter is denied the opportunity to be included in the final electoral rolls, while simultaneously preventing duplicate enrolments.



"In cases where such an elector who was marked as ASDD and consequently whose name does not appear in the draft electoral roll, has shifted the place of residence within the state, such elector is not required to submit Form-8, instead he/she shall submit enumeration form along with the statement enclosed herewith as Annexure-C (indicating the new address and the assembly constituency)," the EC said in a statement.





The poll body also clarified that electors who have already submitted Form-6 for fresh enrolment during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise need not submit the enumeration form and accompanying statement again. Their applications will be processed in accordance with the Commission's clarification dated November 3.

"Partially filled enumeration forms in respect of all such ASDD electors would be generated afresh in ERO dashboard in ECINET.

The DEOs/EROs shall make all possible efforts to contact such electors through the concerned Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and ensure delivery of the enumeration forms either physically or through electronic means such as WhatsApp, e-mail or SMS, wherever contact details are available," the Commission stated.

The EC further directed BLOs to coordinate with Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of various political parties to reach out to the affected electors. This would include house-to-house visits, enquiries with neighbours, family members and Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs), as well as contacting voters through available phone numbers wherever feasible.

World.title: SC ends decades-old power tussle, Himachal to get 11,973 MU from Punjab, Haryana
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday settled a decades-old inter-state dispute over unpaid electricity dues from Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) projects, directing Punjab and Haryana to provide Himachal Pradesh with 11,973 million units (MU) of electricity over 20 years.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, accepted the Centre's proposal to clear the outstanding dues through an energy-based settlement instead of a cash payment.

The settlement follows a 2011 Supreme Court verdict that recognised Himachal Pradesh's entitlement to a 7.19 per cent share in the electricity generated by the Bhakra Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects.



The dues date back to 1966, but Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the state's outstanding share for the period before November 2011.

Under the arrangement approved by the top court, Punjab and Haryana will provide the electricity over 20 years. The settlement also factors in an adjustment of around Rs 420 crore towards Himachal Pradesh's share of the historical capital costs incurred in building the dams. As a result, the hill state will not have to make any separate payment to Punjab or Haryana.





The Centre had earlier proposed that the 13,066 MU in outstanding electricity dues be paid over 15 years, at the rate of 871 MU annually during the lean seasons between October and March. However, the states could not agree on the proposed timeline.

Punjab initially opposed the 15-year arrangement and later sought to extend the payment period to 30 years. Himachal Pradesh, on the other hand, wanted the dues cleared within 10 years.

The Supreme Court's decision to settle the matter over 20 years brings an end to the prolonged disagreement over the payment schedule.

The original electricity arrears were calculated at 13,066 MU by the Central Electricity Authority (CEA). The Centre's proposal had also factored in Himachal Pradesh's liability towards the capital costs of the Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects.

According to a report by PTI, the proposal says that Himachal Pradesh's liability was assessed at Rs 420.7 crore, comprising Rs 249.2 crore payable to Punjab and Rs 171.5 crore to Haryana.

This represented the state's 7.19 per cent share of the composite of Punjab's outstanding loan-servicing costs for the projects since 1966-67.

The Centre had suggested setting off this liability against a portion of the electricity arrears. At the proposed rate of Rs 3.85 per unit, around 1,093 MU would have been adjusted against the capital cost liability.

The proposal also provided for the distribution of electricity arrears between Punjab and Haryana in the inter-state ratio of 58:42 for the Bhakra Nangal project and 60:40 for the Beas projects.

However, since the states could not reach a consensus on the applicable electricity rate, the Centre recommended settling the dues in energy terms.

What was the 2011 Supreme Court verdict?

The Supreme Court's 2011 decision fixed Himachal Pradesh's share in the BBMB projects at 7.19 per cent. Punjab's share was set at 51.80 per cent, while Haryana was allocated 37.51 per cent. Rajasthan's share largely remained unchanged, and Chandigarh's share was fixed at 3.50 per cent.

The verdict also specified when Himachal Pradesh's entitlement would take effect for the three projects. The state was entitled to a share in the Bhakra project from November 1, 1966, the Dehar project from November 1977 and the Pong Dam project from January 1978.

The BBMB has been providing Himachal Pradesh with its 7.19 per cent share of electricity from these projects since November 1, 2011, PTI reported, citing sources.

However, Punjab and Haryana had not cleared the outstanding dues for the earlier period, amounting to 13,066 MU.

How did the dispute reach the Supreme Court?

The dispute dates back to the reorganisation of Punjab under the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966. Himachal Pradesh maintained that, as a successor state, it was entitled to a 7.19 per cent share in the BBMB projects and their electricity generation.

After efforts to resolve the disagreement between the neighbouring states failed, Himachal Pradesh approached the Supreme Court in 1996 through an original suit.

It sought recognition of its entitlement to a share in the projects and the payment of the corresponding arrears.

The Centre subsequently attempted to settle the matter outside court. However, with no agreement emerging between the states, the Supreme Court passed a decree on September 27, 2011, upholding Himachal Pradesh's 7.19 per cent entitlement.

The latest order accepting the Centre's energy-based settlement provides a mechanism to clear the accumulated dues and closes a dispute that has remained unresolved for decades.

World.title: OBC creamy layer row: SC protects past jobs, promotions but leaves pending cases open
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Friday clarified that its March 11 ruling on determining the creamy layer status of Other Backward Class (OBC) candidates would not reopen completed appointments, promotions or seniority positions.

The top court said cases that are still pending would be examined individually by the courts, based on their merits and the candidates' eligibility.

A bench of Justice Pamidighantam Sri Narasimha and Justice R Mahadevan delivered the ruling while hearing an application filed by the Centre seeking clarity on how the March 11 judgment should be implemented. The Court also extended the deadline for compliance with its earlier directions by eight weeks.



The clarification comes after the Centre raised concerns that applying the March 11 ruling retrospectively could unsettle years of government recruitments, service allocations and admissions to educational institutions.

Centre flags concerns over past recruitments

In its application, the government argued that applying the revised interpretation to past cases could affect appointments and admissions made under the rules and eligibility criteria in force at the time.





It warned that this could create uncertainty over OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.

âRetrospective or belated application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the relevant time and may create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression.

It may also affect admissions to Central and State educational institutions, universities and professional institutions.

The Applicant therefore respectfully submits that the temporal operation of the Judgment requires clarification so as to avoid unsettling completed selections, appointments and admissions and the consequential rights arising therefromâ, the plea stated as per LiveLaw.

The Centre said more than 5.69 lakh reserved vacancies, including 3.70 lakh OBC vacancies, were filled in Central government ministries, departments and their subordinate offices between 2016 and 2025.

These recruitments were conducted under the August 8, 1993 Office Memorandum and subsequent government instructions.

It argued that retrospective implementation could also necessitate a review of service allocations made through Civil Services Examinations since 2012. This could potentially lead to changes in the services and cadres allotted to officers already in government service, affecting their seniority and promotion prospects.

The government also flagged possible complications in recruitment examinations conducted by the Railways, banks, Department of Posts and paramilitary organisations. It said similar disputes could arise in 18 States and Union Territories that follow the 1993 guidelines.

The Centre further pointed out that candidates who become eligible for technical services several years after an examination might no longer meet the prescribed physical and medical standards.

It also warned that reopening admissions granted to lakhs of students in universities and professional institutions could create difficulties, particularly where there are no provisions for additional seats.

Dispute over salary-based creamy layer criteria

The clarification application stems from the Supreme Court's March 11 judgment on how the creamy layer among OBC candidates should be identified.

The Court had ruled that a parent's salary alone cannot be used to determine whether an OBC candidate belongs to the creamy layer.

The nature and category of the post held by the parents must also be taken into account.

The dispute centred on two government instructions, the Office Memorandum issued on August 8, 1993, and a subsequent clarification dated October 14, 2004.

The 1993 memorandum laid down the criteria for identifying the OBC creamy layer. It did not make a parent's salary the sole basis for exclusion from reservation benefits. Under the applicable Income/Wealth Test, salary and agricultural income are excluded from the income calculation, while the status and category of the parent's post remain relevant under the prescribed criteria.

The 2004 clarification dealt with employees working in organisations such as public sector undertakings (PSUs), banks, universities and private companies, where the equivalence of their posts with government positions had not been established. It provided for consideration of parents' salary income in such cases.

The Supreme Court held that the 2004 clarification could not introduce a new condition that was not part of the original 1993 policy.

It also observed that treating children of PSU and private-sector employees differently from those of similarly placed government employees could amount to hostile discrimination and violate Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution, which guarantee equality before the law and equal opportunity in public employment.

Centre seeks time to frame uniform mechanism

The government has maintained that it is not challenging or seeking a review of the March 11 judgment.

Instead, it wants clarity on when the ruling should apply and how its directions should be implemented.

The Centre has sought two years to consult stakeholders, establish equivalence between posts in non-government organisations and government positions, and develop a uniform mechanism for determining creamy-layer status in cases where such equivalence has not been established.

It has also asked the SC not to disturb completed selections, appointments, service and cadre allocations, seniority positions and admissions made under the eligibility rules applicable at the time.

The government has separately sought clarity on candidates who were already participating in examinations or recruitment processes when the March 11 judgment was delivered.

In a separate interim application, the Centre sought permission to proceed with service allocation for 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in the Civil Services Examination 2025, using the existing 1993 framework while the clarification application remained pending.

World.title: Massive fire at car showroom in south Delhi; seven injured, 12 rescued
World.content:
A massive fire broke out at a Kia car showroom in south Delhi's Saidulajab area on Friday (November 6, 2026), gutting several vehicles and leaving seven people injured, while around 12-15 others were rescued, an official said.

The fire has been brought under control and a search operation is under way inside the building to ascertain whether anyone else is trapped or if there are any casualties, Deputy Magistrate Lakshya Singhal said.

"Around 3.45 pm, we received information that a Kia showroom opposite the metro station had caught fire. The fire department, police and other agencies were immediately mobilised. The SDM and the SHO also reached the spot," Mr. Singhal said.

VIDEO | Delhi: Fire breaks out at a showroom in the Saiyad Ul Ajaib area of Saket. South Delhi DM Lakshya Singhal says, "At around 3:44 pm, we received a call stating that a massive fire had broken out at the Kia showroom in front of Saket Metro Station. As soon as the fire broke out, the Fire Department, Police Department, Traffic Police and CATS Ambulance were all alerted. At the same time, instructions were received from the Chief Minister that a rescue operation must be launched immediately and all possible efforts should be made to save people's lives. Following the instructions, the rescue operation was conducted effectively. Approximately 12 to 15 people were rescued. Around seven people are injured and are undergoing treatment at Max Hospital and Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital. So far, there are no reports of any casualties or fatalities. The building is being searched again. The Chief Minister is also personally monitoring the entire situation continuously." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) November 6, 2026

Seven people sustained injuries in the incident, of whom four were admitted to MAX Hospital and three to Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital, he said.

Around 12-15 people were rescued from the building, with stairs placed against adjoining buildings to evacuate those trapped on the upper floors. Local residents also helped in the rescue operation, Singhal said.

"As of now, there have been no casualties. The building is being searched to rule out any casualties," he said, adding that teams from the fire department, police, revenue department, Delhi Disaster Management Authority (DDMA), ambulance services and CATS were involved in the operation.

The Delhi Fire Services received a call about the blaze at around 3.47 p.m. and initially rushed 10 fire tenders to the spot. Several teams of the Delhi Police and fire department were deployed to contain the flames.

Thick plumes of black smoke billowed from the showroom, rising high into the sky and visible from a considerable distance. Several cars parked inside the showroom were engulfed in flames as the fire spread across the premises.

The incident also led to a crowd gathering near the showroom, with several passersby stopping to record the blaze on their mobile phones. A traffic jam-like situation was witnessed on the adjoining road, prompting police personnel to disperse onlookers and facilitate the movement of emergency vehicles.

The cause of the fire is yet to be ascertained.

World.title: Karmabhoomi Express catches fire in Punjab, 4 coaches affected, 1,500 passengers escape unhurt
World.content:
More than 1,500 passengers had a narrow escape after a fire broke out in the Karmabhoomi Express near Sarai Banjara railway station in Punjab’s Patiala district on Friday (November 6, 2026), engulfing three coaches and partially damaging a fourth, officials said.

The train, travelling from Amritsar to West Bengal’s New Jalpaiguri, was immediately brought to a halt after the fire was detected, and the affected coaches were detached from the rest of the train to prevent the blaze from spreading.

No casualty or injury was reported.

According to officials, the fire broke out on the Rajpura-Sirhind railway section when the train was passing near Sarai Banjara railway station.

Eyewitnesses and local residents who rushed to the spot said thick smoke could be seen billowing into the sky as the coaches caught fire.

The passengers rushed out of the affected coaches and managed to escape safely.

#WATCH | Rajpura, Punjab: Fire breaks out in 4 coaches of Karmabhumi Express in the Ambala division; no casualties reported Northern Railway CPRO Himanshu Shekhar Upadhyay stated that the train stopped safely after its safety system was triggered near Sarai Banjara station. The fire is being brought under control; senior officials are on-site, and no injuries have been reported. — ANI (@ANI) November 6, 2026

Senior railway officials, who reached the spot, said the fire initially broke out in one coach but spread to other coaches due to strong winds.

“Initially, it was one coach, but as wind was blowing at speed (and as fire spread), a total of four coaches were affected,” Ambala Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) Vinod Kumar Bhatia told reporters.

Three general coaches were primarily affected by the fire, while a fourth coach suffered minor damage, Senior Divisional Commercial Manager of Ambala Division of Northern Railways Yashanjit Singh said.

The train was unreserved, Mr. Singh said, adding that alternate arrangements had been made to ensure passengers reached their destination safely by another train.

Asked about the cause of the fire, Mr. Singh said, “It is a matter of inquiry.”

Mr. Bhatia said both overhead equipment (OHE) lines were shut down after the fire was detected. The guard and loco pilot separated the affected coaches from the rest of the train to prevent the blaze from spreading.

The guard also informed the control room, following which trains operating on other lines were regulated, he said.

The cause of the fire will be investigated, officials said.

World.title: Bus carrying kids to school crashes in France, leaving 2 dead and 16 injured
World.content:
An intercity bus that was carrying children and teenagers to school crashed on Friday (November 6, 2026) morning in eastern France, killing one minor and one young adult, French authorities said.

The Prefecture in the Ain region said one minor and one young adult were killed, while 16 people were injured, including three seriously.

Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot said on X that he was heading to the site following “a serious bus accident” near the small town of Lent, in a rural area north-east of Lyon.

“An accident involving an intercity bus occurred near Lent, France, with multiple casualties reported,” the prefecture said in a statement. Emergency services and law enforcement officers have been deployed to the scene, it said.

News broadcaster BFM TV reported that the passengers included children travelling to middle and high schools in the area. A photo from the scene showed the bus had veered off the road and landed in a ditch.

“It is always a difficult moment when our students, our children, are victims of an accident like this. My thoughts, and those of the Government and the entire education community, are with the families,” Education Minister Edouard Geffray told reporters on the sidelines of a visit to a high school in the Paris region.

World.title: Ecological restoration project launched
World.content:
DHARA, an initiative aimed at ecological restoration, climate resilience, digital monitoring and community livelihoods, was launched in Mayiladuthurai on Friday.

The initiative was launched by Anita Humanitarian Foundation, under its ‘nature purity economy approach.’ The State government has provided one acre of land for DHARA’s initial pilot project, under which ecological restoration, field technologies, community participation and environmental measurement would be developed and tested for wider application.

Site documentation, tree identification and digital mapping would begin soon. Each tree would be given a unique Tree ID, with its location and relevant records mapped online, according to a press release from the foundation.

World.title: Mettur level
World.content: The storage at the Mettur Dam stood at 58.18 feet on Friday against the full reservoir level of 120 feet. The inflow was 10,872 cusecs and the discharge 1,000 cusecs.

World.title: Top news of the day: GRAP-3 curbs imposed in Delhi-NCR as air quality worsens; Election Commission offers fresh chance to electors left out of SIR rolls in Delhi, six States; and more
World.content:
GRAP-3 curbs imposed in Delhi-NCR as air quality worsens

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) on Friday (November 6, 2026) announced Stage three of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) in Delhi and NCR, as the air quality edged closer to the ‘severe’ category in Delhi. GRAP is a set of short-term emergency measures aimed at reducing air pollution and is divided into four stages, depending on the level of air pollution that exists at a particular time or is predicted for the near future.

Voters in SIR states can now refill Enumeration Forms to get back in final list instead of Form 6

Voters who have been marked as Absent, Shifted, Dead and Duplicate (ASDD) in the seven States where the SIR process is on at present can now fill the Enumeration Form again to get back into the list instead of resorting to Form 6 which is used for registration of first time voters. These electors were marked absent as their Enumeration Forms had been issued but not received back, resulting in their exclusion from the Draft Electoral Rolls during the ongoing SIR exercise.

Supreme Court refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal’s 10-year sentence in 2013 rape case

The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) declined to suspend the 10-year prison sentence imposed on journalist Tarun Tejpal by the Goa Bench of the Bombay High Court in a 2013 rape case. The court, however, agreed to hear his appeal challenging the High Court’s August verdict overturning his acquittal by a trial court in Goa.

Form 8 must be decided during SIR; deletion without hearing denies vote: Bombay HC

The Goa bench of The Bombay High Court held that removal of an elector’s name from the roll without a hearing denies the citizen the right to vote. The Bench delivered the judgment on a petition by six members of the Salgaonkar family that an Electoral Registration Officer must decide a Form 8 application while Special Intensive Revision is underway. The Bench also ordered the Election Commission of India to restore the six names, and to set aside the rejection of their Form 8 applications.

Supreme Court notice to KPCC office-bearers on contempt plea for social media post against CJI

Noting that the judicial restraint is not an institutional weakness and attempts to undermine judicial authority will be dealt with with an iron hand, the Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) sought responses from Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) office-bearers on a plea to initiate contempt proceedings against them for a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India Surya Kant.

No split in National Conference, genuine issues will be addressed: Farooq Abdullah

Ruling National Conference (NC) president Farooq Abdullah on Friday (November 6, 2026) ruled out any split in the party and assured a step-by-step approach to address the “genuine issues” raised by the 17 disgruntled legislators during a two-hour meeting with the top leadership in Srinagar.

Burst green crackers, stick to specific timings: Delhi Government appeals to citizens

Ahead of Diwali, the Delhi Government has appealed to the public to comply with the Supreme Court’s directions on the sale and use of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during a limited window around the festival. The district magistrate (East) said in an order, “Bursting of green firecrackers will be permitted only on November 7 and 8, between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m., and 8 p.m. and 10 p.m. Bursting firecrackers outside these prescribed timings is strictly prohibited.”

IAF hands over 39.5-acre sports complex land to Centre

The Indian Air Force has handed over 39.5 acres of land housing a sports complex, a swimming pool and other amenities to the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, an official said on Friday (November 6, 2026). The move comes days after the Land and Development Office (L&DO) under the Ministry issued notices to the facility to return the land on Lok Kalyan Marg.

Periyar Arivulagam books row: People of Tamil Nadu will never forgive DMK for corruption, says CM Vijay

Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday (November 6, 2026) said the people of Tamil Nadu would never forgive the DMK, which had made a history of “looting and indulging in corruption” in the name of Periyar E.V. Ramasamy and Tamil.

Federal judge orders 14-day delay on any work beginning on Trump’s monumental arch

A federal judge late on Thursday (November 5, 2026) blocked the Trump administration from breaking ground on a towering memorial arch for 14 days. The temporary restraining order by U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan, halting the work, represents a major setback for one of President Donald Trump’s most prominent projects in his vision to remake Washington.

IND vs NZ second ODI: Pace heavy India looks to extend advantage over New Zealand

India’s inexperienced yet promising four-pronged pace attack will be looking to maintain its upper hand over New Zealand’s batters and dictate proceedings to ensure that the visitors’ lead is extended when the two sides clash in the second ODI in Wellington on Saturday (November 7, 2026).

Tanvi Patri signs off with silver at Youth Olympics

Tanvi Patri fought hard before going down to China’s Zhang Yi Xin in a gruelling three-game final, but she nonetheless scripted history by becoming the first Indian woman shuttler to win an individual silver at the Youth Olympics in Dakar. In a gripping summit clash that lasted an hour and 22 minutes, the 15-year-old Indian saved six match points and had three opportunities to seal the title. But she eventually lost 21-15, 13-21, 24-26 to the reigning world junior champion on Thursday night.

World.title: Telangana Govt stares at financial burden to fund Rythu Bharosa or crop compensation
World.content:
The Telangana Government is staring at a huge financial burden in the coming days to meet the commitments in the agriculture sector.

At a time when the revenue receipts during the first half of the financial year (2026-27) are not up to the expectations, the government is facing the prospect of announcing investment support to farmers either in the form of Rythu Bharosa or as compensation to farmers for not opting for water-intensive crops like paddy in view of the El Nino weather phenomenon.

₹30,000 crore special assistance package sought

The government sought ₹30,000 crore special assistance package from the Central Government for providing relief to various affected sections including farmers for whom it proposed to provide direct crop loss compensation. Though the request initially was for ₹20,000 crore package, it was enhanced by ₹10,000 crore in view of the anticipated severity of El Nino — which is expected to last till next rainy season.

The Finance department has a tough task on hand for mobilising the required resources in the coming months as the revenue receipts were not matching expectations. The total receipts at the end of the first half of the fiscal are pegged at ₹92,013 crore which is just 38.14% of the ₹2.41 lakh crore receipts projected for the fiscal in the budget estimates. Borrowings contributed to a major chunk of the receipts at ₹44,612 crore by September end and the amounts raised through auction of securities in October took the total borrowings to nearly ₹50,000 crore.

All eyes are now on the quantum of relief that would be extended by the Central Government as it would be crucial in determining the amount of compensation that would be offered to farmers.
