World.title: Uzbekistan's TMK, Japan's Marubeni discuss joint industrial center
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 6. Uzbekistan's Technological Metals Complex (TMK) has proposed establishing a joint industrial and technology center in the country with Japan's Marubeni Corporation to expand the processing of critical minerals and exports of higher-value products during a meeting in Tashkent on Friday, November 6.

According to TMK, the proposal was discussed during a meeting between representatives of TMK and Marubeni, a major Japanese trading and investment company, focused on expanding trade, investment and technological cooperation in the critical minerals sector.

Under the proposed initiative, TMK would provide infrastructure at its existing technology parks, while Japanese partners would contribute technologies and investment to support the development of advanced mineral processing facilities.

The project is intended to strengthen Uzbekistan's domestic capacity to process raw materials into finished products for international markets, moving further along the value chain.

Marubeni expressed particular interest in purchasing products manufactured by TMK. The parties also discussed potential arrangements for developing a joint project.

Following the meeting, the sides agreed to maintain working-level discussions to advance the proposed initiatives and identify opportunities for practical cooperation.

Marubeni Corporation is one of Japan's major integrated trading and investment companies, with business operations spanning energy, metals and mineral resources, chemicals, food products, infrastructure, transportation and industrial machinery. The company operates globally, connecting suppliers and customers through international trade, investment and project development.

World.title: Azerbaijan, UN discuss cooperation, regional development prospects (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 6. On November 6, Jeyhun Bayramov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Azerbaijan, met with Li Junhua, UN Under-Secretary-General for Economic and Social Affairs, who is currently on a visit to the country.

According to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the meeting focused on the current state and prospects of cooperation between Azerbaijan and the UN, Azerbaijan’s contribution to multilateral diplomacy, as well as issues on the global and regional agendas.

The parties noted with satisfaction Azerbaijan’s active role in cooperation with the UN, as well as its steps to help address global challenges. In this context, particular emphasis was placed on Azerbaijan’s chairmanship, the initiatives it has put forward, the high-level events it has hosted, and the results achieved within the framework of the Non-Aligned Movement, COP29, the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP), the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA), the World Urban Forum (WUF), and other international platforms.

Emphasizing the importance of the successful hosting of the UN Summit on Innovation in Public Administration in Azerbaijan on November 5–6, the minister highlighted the efforts being made to promote Azerbaijan’s experience in the field of innovative public administration at the international level, particularly the “ASAN Khidmet” model, and to expand its application in various countries.

The minister provided information on Azerbaijan’s contribution to the implementation of the UN Sustainable Development Goals by 2030, the measures being taken in this regard at the national level, as well as the donor and humanitarian activities carried out to support the international development agenda.

The importance of expanding regional cooperation between Azerbaijan and the countries of Central Asia, as well as the significance of the C6 format, was emphasized. In this context, discussions touched on strengthening transport and logistics links, effectively utilizing the potential of the Middle Corridor, expanding trade and investment ties, energy security, green energy, digital transformation, and the development of regional transit capabilities.

Minister Jeyhun Bayramov briefed the other side on the large-scale reconstruction and development efforts being carried out by Azerbaijan in the territories liberated from occupation, as well as on measures to ensure the return of former internally displaced persons to their homelands, the creation of modern infrastructure, and the economic reintegration of these territories. In addition, attention was drawn to the serious hindrance posed by the threat of landmines and unexploded ordnance left over from the period of Armenian occupation to the process of reconstruction and development, human safety, and sustainable development.

The parties also exchanged views on existing global and regional threats and challenges affecting international peace and security, the promotion of economic and social development, as well as other issues of mutual interest within the framework of the United Nations.

World.title: Uniper plans to increase 2026 dividend by 7% to 321 million euros
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 6. German energy company Uniper plans to propose a dividend totaling 321 million euros, or 0.77 euros per share, for the 2026 financial year at its 2027 Annual General Meeting, the company said on November 6.

The proposed payout, subject to sufficient final net income under German GAAP and shareholder approval, would represent a 7-percent increase compared with the 300 million euros (0.72 euros per share) distributed for the 2025 financial year. The planned increase is supported by the company's ongoing implementation of its strategy and expectations of continued profitable growth.

“With our strategy and planned investments, we are laying the foundation for the earnings growth we expect in the coming years. We want our shareholders to participate in this growth. Our dividend policy provides a clear, long-term outlook for this: We aim for a steadily growing dividend,” Uniper CEO Michael Lewis said.

Uniper continues to advance its strategic transformation in response to key developments in the European energy market, including growing energy security requirements, decarbonization efforts and rising electricity demand driven by electrification and artificial intelligence.

The company's strategy focuses on flexible power generation, expanding renewable energy capacity, developing its gas and LNG business, and investing in renewable and low-carbon gases.

Düsseldorf-based Uniper is a European energy company with global reach, employing approximately 7,000 people. It plays a key role in ensuring Europe's energy security, particularly in its core markets of Germany, the United Kingdom, Sweden and the Netherlands.

With 18.5 gigawatts of power generation capacity, Uniper is a major provider of reliable electricity. The company is also a leading gas trader and one of Northwestern Europe's largest LNG importers, with a diversified procurement portfolio supporting security of supply.

Uniper's investments in renewable energy, hydrogen and other low-carbon energy sources contribute to the transformation of the energy system.

In Germany, the company supplies energy and related services to approximately 1,000 municipalities and industrial customers. It is also the country's largest operator of gas storage facilities and hydropower plants.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Jordan agree to expand trade and investment cooperation
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 6. Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Jordan's King Abdullah II bin Al-Hussein have discussed expanding bilateral trade, investment and cultural cooperation during a meeting on the sidelines of the Aqaba Process gathering in Astana, Kazakhstan on Friday, November 6.

According to the presidential press service, Mirziyoyev highlighted the growing importance of the Aqaba Process, an initiative launched by King Abdullah II, amid emerging global security threats.

The leaders reviewed progress in implementing agreements reached during previous high-level meetings and discussed prospects for further developing bilateral relations.

They noted the positive momentum in exchanges and contacts between the two countries in recent years, including the launch of direct air services, the holding of a meeting of the joint intergovernmental commission and the establishment of a bilateral Business Council.

The sides agreed to further strengthen cooperation, with particular emphasis on expanding trade and economic ties, attracting investment and developing cultural and humanitarian exchanges.

Additionally, Mirziyoyev and King Abdullah II exchanged views on the schedule of upcoming high-level bilateral events and other issues on their agenda.

The Aqaba Process is an international initiative launched by King Abdullah II in 2015 to strengthen cooperation among countries in combating terrorism and violent extremism. It brings together heads of state, security officials, military representatives and international organizations to coordinate responses to evolving security threats.

World.title: Azerbaijan records 7.5% growth in active VAT payers by November
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 6. The number of active value-added tax (VAT) payers in Azerbaijan rose by 7.5% as of November 1, 2026, compared to the same date last year, according to the State Tax Service under the Ministry of Economy.

According to the data, as of November 1, 2026, the number of active taxpayers had increased by 5.4% from the beginning of the year to 905,579, while the number of active VAT payers rose by 7.5% year-on-year to 62,779.

Over the same period, the number of active business facilities increased by 6.8% to 248,695.

Chief of Staff of the Ministry of Economy Elvin Jamalov said that one of the most reliable indicators of the formalization of the economy is the number of registered taxpayers and business facilities. He made the remarks while presenting the draft law "On the State Budget of Azerbaijan for 2027" at its first reading during a meeting of the Parliament's Committee on Economic Policy, Industry and Entrepreneurship.

"Since 2018, the number of active taxpayers has doubled, the number of VAT payers has increased 3.5 times, and the number of active business facilities has grown 1.7 times. This process has continued this year as well," he added.

He recalled that in the first nine months of 2026, tax revenues reached 107.2% of the forecast for the reporting period, including 102.9% in the non-oil and gas sector, while 80.6% of the annual tax revenue forecast had already been met.

"Tax revenues increased by 9.4%, while non-oil and gas tax revenues rose by 12.6%, exceeding the nominal growth rate of non-oil and gas GDP (7.6%). The private sector accounts for 75% of revenues from the non-oil and gas sector.

The share of non-oil and gas tax revenues in the state budget's non-oil and gas revenues exceeded 63%.

Mandatory state social insurance contributions increased by 8.5%, reaching 5 billion manats ($2.9 billion), with the forecast fulfilled by 105.6%. Amid the formalization of the labor market, the sustained growth in social insurance contributions in recent years has made a significant contribution to strengthening the financial sustainability of the State Social Protection Fund. In particular, the share of budget allocations in the fund's revenues fell from 36% in 2018 to 20% in the first nine months of this year," he noted.

World.title: Three detainees scale Banksia Hill Detention Centre roof
World.content:
Three detainees at Perth's Banksia Hill Detention Centre have scaled the facility's roof, almost a year after the last major incident at the centre.

Aerial footage from Friday evening showed damage to the centre, including two windows, part of the roof and an air conditioning unit.

One of the detainees threw what appeared to be a brick to the ground at one stage.

Officers in riot gear are seen responding. (ABC News)

At other points, the detainees were sitting on the roof talking to each other.

Staff, including some with riot shields, watched on as others spoke to the detainees.

Aerial footage shows some damage to the centre. (ABC News)

"The department can confirm there are three young people on the roof at Banksia Hill with staff monitoring the situation," a Department of Justice spokesperson said just after 6pm.

"There is no risk to the wider public."

Banksia Hill is the state's main youth detention facility, usually holding boys and girls aged between 10 and 17 years old.

At least six young people scaled the roof of the facility in late November last year, with three remaining there overnight.

It appears extra fencing has been added to some parts of the roof of the facility since that incident.

Detainees on roof of Banksia Hill Detention Centre The remaining three detainees who were on the roof of Perth's Banksia Hill juvenile detention centre come down.

There have been a number of riots at the site in recent years, including one in 2023, which then-premier described as a "form of terrorism" and which was ended when armed guards pointed weapons at the heads of teenagers.

It came amid years of dysfunction in the state's youth justice system, which has since largely been resolved.

Work is continuing on a new $156 million youth detention facility located alongside Banksia Hill to provide support for the most high-risk detainees, which is expected to open in 2028.

The government has been working on a $67 million project for "upgrades and urgent works" at the facility, which is due to be completed this year.

World.title: Threatening, sexist messages scrawled on balloons left at MP's office
World.content:
A South Australian government MP says threatening, sexist and abusive messages scrawled on balloons — at least one of which contained powder — were left outside her office, in an incident that is being investigated by police.

Labor MP Jayne Stinson said staff arriving at her electorate office on Marion Road at Plympton this morning initially thought someone must have sent her balloons for her birthday.

But she said that upon closer inspection the matter "turned dark pretty quickly", when it became obvious the messages included "threats on my safety and my life".

She said the balloons had been left at the front of her office and in the car park.

"There were messages threatening to burn me, there were messages calling me swear words — sexist names," Ms Stinson said.

Jayne Stinson says sexist abuse and the words "stop the chop" had been left on several of the balloons. (Supplied)

SA Police has confirmed it is investigating the matter, noting it had come amid "an increase in threats directed towards elected representatives, candidates and others involved in public life".

Ms Stinson, who is the member for Badcoe in Adelaide's inner south-west, said several of the balloons had the words "stop the chop" scrawled upon them — a slogan associated with a public campaign opposed to government projects in the state's parklands.

"My staffer thought he was cleaning up and popped one of the balloons and got covered in powder, which of course is very frightening for someone," Ms Stinson said.

"Obviously at that point I told him to call the police, and the police arrived."

Jayne Stinson says she has previously faced threats and attempted physical assaults. (ABC News)

SA Police said while there were no injuries reported and no damage to property, "there was a threatening message left on one of the balloons, which police are investigating".

"Officers remind the community that threatening, intimidating or menacing behaviour is not acceptable and may constitute a criminal offence," police said in a statement.

"The current political and social environment has seen an increase in threats directed towards elected representatives.

"Everyone has the right to express their views peacefully and respectfully, however any conduct intended to cause fear, alarm or intimidation will be taken seriously and investigated by police."

The Plympton incident comes at a time of considerable public discussion about the safety of elected officials, prompted by alleged Wangaratta attack on federal MP Helen Haines.

Police say the incident has come amid increasing threats on elected officials. (Supplied)

Ms Stinson said she understood police were searching for two people believed to have left the balloons at her office.

"I don't know who has done this … [but] my message to those people is front up and let [police] know what you've done," she said.

"Protesting is fine, voicing your concerns to your MP is not just fine but encouraged — I welcome that — but when it steps over the line … that's just not on, that's not part of democratic exchange and it absolutely does not help people get what they want."

Ms Stinson said she had previously faced threats and attempted physical assaults during her two terms in office, and said she felt "really upset for my staff".

"They shouldn't have to come to work and deal with that," she said.

"They should feel safe in the workplace."

In a statement, Adelaide Park Lands Association president Mat Monti — who has been campaigning to stop trees being cut down in the parklands — said the targeting of Ms Stinson's office was "completely unacceptable".

"Jayne Stinson should not be made to feel unsafe just for doing her job," they said.

"By all means disagree with her position or decision, but this sort of intimidation has no place in our politics."

World.title: Alleged stalker who threatened to kill jockey Michelle Payne denied bail
World.content:
Legendary Melbourne Cup-winning jockey Michelle Payne has lashed an accused stalker who allegedly bombarded her with "disgusting" death threats and sexualised slurs.

Craig Langford, a 51-year-old man from Werribee, allegedly hurled the violent threats at Payne in a series of Instagram messages last week.

A court heard Mr Langford, who was on bail for other alleged offending when he allegedly sent the abusive texts over the course of three days, threatened to kill Payne and called her a slut, a pig and a dog.

Payne, the first woman to win the Melbourne Cup, told the ABC the level of violence detailed in Mr Langford's alleged threats was "unimaginable".

"You can't have people out there if they're going to make those comments. They don't deserve their freedom," Payne said.

"It's disgusting to think that someone could think they could treat you like that."

Michelle Payne rode Prince of Penzance to victory in the Melbourne Cup in 2015. (AAP: Julian Smith)

Mr Langford was denied bail in the Wyndham magistrates court today after prosecutors told the court they held "grave concerns" for Payne's physical safety and mental health after the alleged death threats left her in a state of shock.

"The victim is a well-known public figure and can easily be tracked and located," the court heard.

Prosecutors said Mr Langford had made "threats of lethal violence" that included wishing Payne and her family dead.

The court heard detectives did not know the motive behind Mr Langford's menacing messages to Payne and that he did not know her personally.

Judge says accused poses unacceptable risk to community

Police raided the Werribee home where Mr Langford had been living with his stepfather and mother, where they seized his mobile phone to download and analyse its data.

Following his arrest, Mr Langford denied sending the messages and claimed he did not use Instagram when interviewed by police.

The court heard Mr Langford told investigators he knew who Payne was and did not like her but had refused to elaborate further.

Police say Craig Langford denied sending the messages and told them he did not use Instagram when interviewed. (Reuters: Thomas White/File)

Mr Langford's defence counsel told the court he would have "next to zero" access to a computer or smartphone if he was bailed, and that his stepfather would report him to police if he breached any orders imposed on him.

The court also heard Mr Langford cared for his unwell and elderly stepfather and his wheelchair-bound mother.

But a magistrate deemed Payne's accused stalker an unacceptable risk to the community, saying: "Stalking has a significant impact on those people subjected to it."

Mr Langford, who sat in the dock flanked by custody officers, looked directly ahead as he was remanded in custody.

The alleged death threats and abuse are the latest challenge for the retired Payne, whose father, legendary horseman Paddy Payne Sr, died in September at age 90.

They are also not the first time Payne has dealt with alleged stalking.

Victorian man Peter Widdowson pleaded guilty to stalking Payne and fellow jockey Nikita Beriman when he mailed the pair parcels filled with toys, books and letters in 2022.

Payne rode New Zealand-bred Thoroughbred Prince of Penzance when she became the first woman to win the Melbourne Cup in 2015.

Mr Langford will return to court next month.

World.title: Ex-partner of disgraced author Craig Silvey speaks of 'great betrayal'
World.content:
The ex-partner of disgraced novelist Craig Silvey has spoken of suffering a "betrayal" and how she and their three young children are "secondary victims" of his crimes.

Writer Clare Testoni, who separated from Silvey after 13 years in the wake of his arrest on child exploitation charges, posted a statement online on yesterday evening, telling of "the hardest year of my life" since his arrest in January this year.

How Craig Silvey ended up behind bars Author Craig SIlvey's conviction on child exploitation material charges leaves a generation of book lovers feeling "great betrayal".

Silvey was jailed this week for seven months for possessing and distributing graphic images and videos of child exploitation

In sentencing him, Judge Hayley Cormann said the material he possessed and his communications about it were "repulsive" and "degrading".

Ms Testoni's statement detailed her increasing distance from Silvey over the past six years, and their eventual estrangement when she learned of his crimes.

'Great betrayal'

She described what Silvey did as a "great betrayal".

"The father of my children and my partner of 13 years revealed himself not to be the man I thought he was," Ms Testoni wrote.

"While I was aware he was stressed and his mental health was suffering I had no idea what was truly going on.

"I had seven month old twins, a three year old, I had been drowning in motherhood and in his growing absence."

Ms Testoni expressed her sorrow for those whose abuse was depicted in the material Silvey shared.

Craig Silvey arrives at court for his sentencing on Monday. (ABC News: Cason Ho)

"I’m especially sorry for the victims," she wrote.

"All children deserve to be safe and loved. That is what I hope to provide for my girls."

'Secondary victims'

Her statement came days after Silvey posted his own 9,000-word essay online in which he tried to explain what led to his offending, outlining his own sexual abuse as a child and his anguished mental state.

Ms Testoni, who is understood to have moved from Fremantle to New South Wales after separating from Silvey, said this year had been the hardest of her life.

"With little children and no employment, this betrayal came at the time in my life when I was most financially and socially vulnerable," she wrote.

"It is hard to rebuild friendships after escaping a toxic relationship when you are the sole parent to three under four.

Craig Silvey jailed over 'most depraved' child exploitation material Disgraced Australian author Craig Silvey is jailed by a Perth judge after admitting he distributed graphic images of adults abusing children over a messaging service.

" It is harder still while being followed by the Daily Mail on your way to Centrelink. "

"We separated as soon [as I] learned of his crimes but he remains the father of our children.

"Reconciling how he will be in their lives is an ongoing project that I don’t think anyone else can understand until it happens to them.

"We are secondary victims in this. We have suffered greatly."

Silvey 'a shadow'

Ms Testoni said she had become increasingly estranged from Silvey as his writing career blossomed.

"Craig has already been a shadow that occluded me at times in my career," she wrote.

"He supported many of my endeavours with enthusiasm but in the last six years he had stopped reading my work when I shared it with him, discouraged me from continuing my PhD when we had our first child, and generally prioritised his own more lucrative career over mine.

"This is an old story badly re-told again and again.

"I hope to tell a new story going forward."

World.title: Woman rescues baby koala from grips of python in Brisbane
World.content:
A Brisbane wildlife rescuer has saved a baby koala from the deadly grip of a python after coming across the pair while out for a bushwalk.

Nell was walking her dog in Whites Hill Reserve at Camp Hill, when she heard a commotion, about 15 metres off the footpath.

"I heard a lot of birds, so I ran over and that's when I saw the joey look me dead in the eyes panicked and the mum was scratching at a python as she tried to get it off her baby."

"She was really distressed," she said.

That's when Nell jumped into action and scooped up the joey, before she started to unravel the snake.

"I didn't know if the baby was breathing or had broken ribs or anything in that moment, I just picked it up and started unravelling," Nell said.

The koala and the cub embraced after the rescue. (Supplied: @behappy.golucky)

"It all happened so quickly … and all of a sudden I've got the snake in one hand and then the joey clutching onto my left shoulder crying."

The rescuer said a man walking nearby stopped to offer his help but was not thrilled when she tried to hand over the snake.

She said she asked him to hold the snake, but he very quickly said no and offered to hold her dog instead.

Nell said she put the snake into a small tree while she checked the freed joey for injuries before reuniting it with mum who had stayed close by throughout the ordeal.

"I made sure its limbs were moving correctly and that it was breathing ok … then I walked up to the tree that its mum was in and it went straight up to her."

Nell was walking with her dog Pluto when they saw the koala in the snake's clutches. (Supplied: @behappy.golucky)

"I then walked with the snake wrapped around my arm until I felt it was far enough that it wasn't going to come back and do the same thing," she said.

Nell said the python was about a metre-and-a-half in length and believes it would have killed the baby koala but not been able to swallow it.

" I came back about an hour or two later and saw the mum and her baby cuddling and they looked so happy. "

"That was the best feeling in the world … the snake was fine and can find a smaller meal somewhere else."

Nell said she wanted to post the video to create more awareness about the endangered species and the challenges they face.

World.title: Asofa-Solomona leaps into crowd, apologises after 'frightening' Gallen KO
World.content:
A furious Nelson Asofa-Solomona has leaped into the crowd in sensational scenes following his knockout victory over fellow former NRL star Paul Gallen in Sydney.

Gallen, returning to the ring for the final time, was knocked out with 10 seconds remaining in the first round of their five-round heavyweight bout at the TikTok Entertainment Centre.

The 45-year-old was hit with a thunderous right that sent him back against the ropes, before four devastating upper cuts, the last of which was landed despite Gallen already being down.

As Gallen lay stricken on the ropes in considerable distress, Asofa-Solomona leaped onto the corner ropes to celebrate his win.

Then, incredibly, the 200cm, 137.5kg giant leaped over the ropes and ran to someone in the crowd.

Footage appeared to show the former Storm forward swing a wild punch towards a spectator, who was later led out the building by police.

Nelson Asofa-Solomona was bated by someone in the crowd, and lowered himself to challenge them directly. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

"I just want to apologise for what I did, I acted like a bloody idiot," Nelson Asofa-Solomona said in the ring.

"I just got in a bit of the heat of the moment.

"I should not behave like that, I'm sorry."

Gallen, meanwhile, who surrendered a 20cm height advantage and more than 33kg in weight, was able to sit up.

He was later shown laughing with his shaken son in the dressing room, seemingly recovered.

Former world champion Tim Tszyu said the knockout was "frightening", while Gallen's former Sharks teammate Michael Ennis was in a state of shock at the sheer violence meted out on his friend.

Paul Gallen was left stricken in terrifying scenes. (Getty Images: Darrian Traynor)

"That was really hard," Ennis said.

"It was really hard to watch."

George Rose, promoter of No Limit Boxing, did not criticise Asofa-Solomona, but was

"One thing that we love with our shows is that we like to make it a safe and enjoyable and entertaining experience for everyone," Rose said on Main Event.

"We want to make sure that it's something that people can be a part of and feel safe to come and enjoy."

Earlier in the night, Paris Olympian and Commonwealth Games medallist Callum Peters, despite being slightly off colour, maintained his unbeaten record with a unanimous points win against rugged Colombian Juan Diego Ortiz.

Meanwhile Paulo Aokuso delivered a statement knockout to beat Mobin Khahrazeh in the second round of their IBF Inter-Continental light heavyweight title fight.

Follow all the action from the TikTok Entertainment Centre in Sydney in our live blog.

World.title: 18yo, teenagers arrested over Calder Highway pursuit
World.content:
An 18-year-old described as the ringleader behind a series of alleged youth crimes in Victoria's north-west has been remanded in custody.

Lucky Tambo, 18, from Manor Lakes in Melbourne's south-west, has been charged with speeding in a dangerous manner, multiple thefts of vehicles and burglary.

Police told the court CCTV captured five youths, aged 13 to 18, breaking in to Sunraysia Community Health Services at 10:30pm on October 26 before rifling through drawers and Mr Tambo using a hammer to force open a safe to steal five car keys.

Damage to the doors of Sunraysia Community Health Services on October 26. (Supplied: Steve Scott)

Cameras also captured each co-accused driving off in a stolen car. All five cars were later recovered from various locations across Mildura.

A second incident involved the theft of a 2021 MG HS wagon from a driveway in Belmont, near Geelong, on November 5.

Police allege Mr Tambo and four youths were involved in a high-speed chase along the Calder Highway on Thursday.

Eight videos from phones belonging to the youths have been seized by police. One allegedly shows Mr Tambo driving the stolen vehicle at speeds of 158 kilometres per hour.

Police said another showed a 17-year-old, who had been charged with dangerous driving, being pursued by police at speeds of 175km/h.

The pursuit began after roadside police spotted the car speeding at 146km/h at Culgoa, 320km from Melbourne.

Lucky Tambo's matter was heard at the Mildura Magistrates' Court. (ABC News: Wade Stephens)

The prosecution said during attempts to intercept the car, the 17-year-old driver allegedly began overtaking trucks and driving on the wrong side of the road, causing several near misses with oncoming vehicles.

Police used stop sticks to puncture the car's tyres outside Ouyen, and the teenagers ran into nearby paddocks before being arrested with help from the police air wing.

Some younger co-accused from the two incidents have been interviewed and released pending inquiries while others are yet to be found.

Leading Senior Constable Fleur Royds told the court Mr Tambo was "the eldest offender, he was the only adult, with children as young as 13, acting as a ringleader to them".

A magistrate described the allegations as "very serious", and ordered a youth justice assessment to explore the potential for supported bail.

Mr Tambo will return to court on November 20.

His 17-year-old co-accused has been granted bail with strict conditions, and will face court on December 6.

World.title: Court grants Kumanjayi Little Baby's mother 20-year full no-contact DVO
World.content:
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander readers are advised that this article contains the image of an Indigenous person who has died, used with the permission of her family.

The father of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby has been handed a jail sentence of more than three years for aggravated assault, for offences committed against the girl's mother.

Appearing in the Alice Springs Local Court this afternoon dressed in a brown zip-up jacket and faded cargo pants, Raphael Granites pleaded guilty to two counts of aggravated assault against his former partner on April 9 and April 22 this year.

The court heard the 30-year-old was taken into custody on April 23, two days before his daughter disappeared from a town camp on the outskirts of Alice Springs.

In April, police and volunteers searched the area around an Alice Springs town camp for the missing little girl. (ABC News: Will Green)

Kumanjayi Little Baby's disappearance triggered widespread searches in the town, involving hundreds of volunteers, but her body was found in bushland five days later.

Jefferson Lewis, 47, has been arrested and charged with her murder.

Kumanjayi Little Baby went missing from the Old Timers town camp. (Supplied: NT Police)

In court today, prosecutor Gigi Dadds told the court the entirety of Raphael Granites's offending towards the five-year-old's mother on April 9 "happened in the presence of their two children".

The court heard it involved him spitting on the mother, along with threats to knock her out and stomp on her head.

"The victim, as contained in the statement of facts, was so fearful that she contacted the women's shelter by email for help," she said.

" The threatened applications of force, while threats, were extremely violent and plainly made with the intention of being intimidating and in circumstances where he was very close … and had the ability to enact those threats, again in front of the children. "

Ms Dadds told the court the assault on April 22, which hospitalised his partner, happened when Granites was aware she did not want to continue the relationship.

"She remained on the ground in a vulnerable position. [There were] the two applications of force, which were on a vulnerable part of her body, being her face, and she sustained injuries to her lips, cheek and eye region," Ms Dadds said.

The prosecutor also read a victim impact statement to the court.

"When Raphael punched me into my face, it was painful; my cheek was stinging and really sore. My lip was also split and I could taste blood," the woman wrote in her statement. "At the time of the assault, it was painful, and for about a week later it was still sore and swollen. My eye was still black when my baby girl was missing. "I felt scared because I thought Raphael was going to hurt me more because he has hurt me lots of other times before and is always intimidating me and making me feel threatened."

After her death, mourners left tributes for Kumanjayi Little Baby outside the Old Timers town camp. (ABC News: Will Green)

The victim also requested the court send Granites to live with family in WA after he served a court order in the Northern Territory.

"That way I know that I'm safe and I don't need to keep looking over my shoulder everywhere I go," she wrote. "I think Raphael needs to stay in jail to learn a lesson and to do some sort of men's programs so he knows that it is not okay to keep assaulting women."

Granites's defence lawyer Jackson Meaney asked the judge to consider that the 30-year-old had "experienced childhood exposure to domestic violence".

"The cycle, unfortunately, has continued in Mr Granites's case," Mr Meaney said.

He added Granites had experienced "periods in his life where he's very positively contributed to his community", telling the court his client had been employed at the Yuendemu store and spent 20 months without offending before he travelled to Alice Springs.

The five-year-old girl's alleged murder rocked Alice Springs and many surrounding remote communities. (ABC News: Michael Franchi)

Mr Meaney pointed to extended family and friends who were in court to support the defendant, including senior Warlpiri elder Robin Granites Japanangka, and argued any potential term of imprisonment should include time under supervision in the community.

"Following the loss of his father, Robin Granites has played a really central role as that man in his life that has cultural authority and provides guidance and support to Raphael," Mr Meaney said.

"Mr [Robin] Granites has attended court on numerous occasions in support of Raphael, during the course of two applications for bail that were brought largely on compassionate basis for Raphael to be able to attend to his family during those tragic moments following the news of the loss of a young child and at the time that the funeral occurred.

Kumanjayi Little Baby remembered at funeral service Hundreds of members of the Alice Springs community have turned out dressed in pink to mourn Kumanjayi Little Baby at her funeral today.

"It has been an incredibly difficult process for my client whilst he's been in custody, largely separated from his family and his community, going through that process of grieving the loss of a very young child in circumstances that will be difficult to understand."

In sentencing, Judge Jonathan Bortoli said he gave weight to "the difficult conditions on remand" given "the absolutely tragic loss of your daughter".

He also noted Granites's guilty pleas had saved "the complainant, who is a vulnerable person herself, from having to come in court to give evidence".

Kumanjayi Little Baby's funeral took place in Alice Springs in August. (ABC News: Emma Masters)

But Judge Bortoli stated "almost all of your offending essentially has been against the same victim" and that the offending "shows a concerning pattern of behaviour and attitude towards your partner and women in general".

"Eight priors of aggravated assault, eight breaches of domestic violence orders and one threat and charge, all in relation to the same victim," he said.

" In light of your history, I must make a realistic assessment of your prospects of rehabilitation, despite the supports that are said to be offered to you, and I find that at this stage they can only be described as poor. "

Raphael Granites was sentenced to three years and two months in prison, backdated to April 23 this year.

The judge said that term included restoring Granites's suspended sentence for "a violent offence against the same victim", 14 months imprisonment for the aggravated assault on April 9, and 16 months for the offence on April 22.

He will be eligible for parole in June 2028.

Kumanjayi Little Baby review finds extensive failings An independent review into the NT child protection department's conduct surrounding Kumanjayi Little Baby before her alleged murder has revealed extensive failings.

"In terms of the domestic violence order then, Mr Granites, I do agree a full no-contact order is appropriate," Judge Bortoli said.

"I'm going to make that for a very lengthy period given your extensive history. There will be a 20-year full no-contact domestic violence order.

"You are not to approach, contact or remain in her company, that is directly or indirectly, so you can't even do it through family or friends."

Granites was ordered to communicate through legal or nominated parties to make arrangements to see his son.

"I can only express my hope that when you are released that you leave her alone and have nothing to do with her," Judge Bortoli said.

"And if you do have another partner in the future that you have learned from this."

World.content:
NationalVictoriaCrime Man dead after stabbing in Melbourne CBD Alexander Darling November 6, 2026 — 11:21pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. One man in dead and another is in hospital after an apparent late-night stabbing in Melbourne’s CBD. Police were called to a restaurant in Frederick Way near Queen Victoria Market shortly after 8pm where they found a man with stab wounds. CPR was performed, but the man was declared dead at the scene. A short time later, a second man in his 30s was located nearby with a suspected stab wound and was taken to hospital. Police near the scene of the fatal stabbing which happened in a small laneway near Queen Victoria Market. Alexander Darling Police established two crime scenes about 100 metres apart, with major roads closed soon after the incident in an area of the city which is home to a large community of Chinese students and tourists.



The incident lit up social media apps with one user of RedNote, a Chinese social networking site, claiming to have heard from witnesses of the incident. “They say a delivery driver went inside to pick up an order, and while he was there, some random guy outside deliberately pushed his e-bike over,” the user wrote. Police closed streets in the north-west corner of the city following the incident. Alexander Darling “When the rider realised and went out to confront him, the other guy suddenly pulled out a knife and stabbed it right in his chest. “This is a huge wake-up call for all of us delivering food in Melbourne.”



Footage circulating on social media platform WeChat seen by this masthead shows a man in a bicycle helmet and a high-vis vest slumped against a wall in a restaurant on Frederick Way, being helped by a woman, with a trail of blood on the floor in front of him. Police set up two crime scenes about 100 metres apart. Alexander Darling The incident came on the same day that three people were stabbed in Melbourne’s south-east, sending a nearby primary school into lockdown. Emergency services were called to a home on Woodlee Street in Dandenong about 11.30am after three people were found with injuries believed to be stab wounds.



The incident resulted in a 28-year-old woman being rushed to hospital with life-threatening injuries, while two men, 26 and 35, were treated for serious but non-life-threatening injuries. Police said they were still in the early stages of understanding what had happened, with family violence detectives investigating. They said the three people injured were known to each other. Acting Inspector Rebecca Hall said on Friday afternoon that Dandenong North Primary School, on nearby Cleeland Street, was placed into lockdown after the incident. Police and SES at the scene in Dandenong on Friday afternoon. Nine News “The children were prevented from coming to the street, so they didn’t witness anything,” she said. “Parents have been notified about how to pick up their children.”



Hall said it was too early to confirm many details about the incident, including exactly how the people were known to each other, if a weapon had been recovered and whether the incident happened inside the house on Woodlee Street or outside. Be the first to know when major news happens.

World.title: New wave of bomb threats hits European flights, media outlets
World.content:
Updated WorldEuropeAviation New wave of bomb threats hits European flights, media outlets Updated November 6, 2026 — 11:19pm ,first published November 5, 2026 — 7:57pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Bomb threats were issued to media outlets across Europe on Friday, as passenger flights around the continent received a wave of similar threats for the third time this week. Irish national broadcaster RTE and the Independent newspaper evacuated their respective office after receiving threats on Friday morning local time. Hours later, British broadcaster Sky said it had received a security threat also. Members of the Irish Armed Response Unit outside the RTE offices in Donnybroook, Dublin. RTE News The bomb threat emailed to Irish broadcaster RTE claimed to be from the same group behind a wave of bomb threats issued to passenger flights around Europe this week, an RTE reporter said on air, reading excerpts from the email. The excerpts read on air did not name the group.



Meanwhile, hoax threats are again disrupting dozens of passenger flights across Europe on Friday, after similar threats on Thursday led to unplanned landings by some planes and prompted fighter jets to escort or intercept others, a dramatic escalation after an initial wave on Tuesday. No explosive devices have been found and all planes have landed safely. Danish police said on Friday they were investigating threats directed at air traffic at Copenhagen airport, but that their immediate assessment was that there had been no danger to passengers. The airport said it was “operating normally”. Czech police said they had registered bomb threats to flights departing from and arriving in Prague. An airport spokesperson said they concerned four inbound and five outbound flights, but that no explosive devices had been found and no flights had been cancelled or diverted as a result. Loading



Shortly afterwards, an Italian airport authority source said a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome had been diverted to Venice and landed there safely. The French prime minister’s office said four new bomb threats had been made to aircraft flying over French territory, and that all had landed safely. A bomb alert on a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon prompted a security operation when it landed, CNN Portugal reported. On Thursday, more than a dozen bomb threats forced unplanned landings by some planes and prompted fighter jets to escort or intercept others, in a dramatic escalation after an initial wave during the week. The highly unusual spate of bomb threats affected nearly 30 flights by the end of Thursday (Friday AEDT), after at least seven flights and a cruise ship also received hoax threats on Tuesday.



No government has said who was behind the threats, and no claim of responsibility has been verified. Security experts said it could be individuals acting on personal grievances or copycats, but also that it had the hallmarks of a more co-ordinated “hybrid attack”. “When it comes to a situation like this or even other sabotage attacks, it’s really hard to prove there’s a certain country behind it. But it does fit in the modus operandi,” said Eric Schouten, head of aviation security group Dyami. Many European officials have accused Russia of masterminding sabotage and hybrid attacks since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. These are often inexpensive to carry out, easily deniable and not expected to trigger an armed response. Planes on the tarmac after multiple flights bound for Prague received bomb threats on Thursday. Getty Images Denmark, Poland and Romania, all affected by the disruptions, have previously accused Moscow directly of being behind hybrid attacks, while Germany blamed Russia for an August attack on Leipzig Airport.



Britain, which has in the past blamed Russia, linked Iran to a suspected plot against a US air base. Both Russia and Iran have denied those accusations. An airport source in Italy told Reuters that an email with the subject line “Threat report” had been sent to several addresses for airlines, airport operators and airport service providers at Rome’s Fiumicino and Milan’s Malpensa airports. The email, which claimed it was from “fighters of the Male State”, said devices had been placed on inbound flights from Helsinki and Dublin, and they would explode in 60 minutes. “Today your sky will be red,” it said. Reuters could not independently confirm who had sent the email, and there was no immediate indication of who was behind the other threats across Europe.



The path of flight EI402 going from Dublin to Rome, after it was diverted following a bomb threat. FlightRadar24 Vladislav Pozdnyakov, a Russian blogger who set up an anti-feminist movement called the Male State in 2016 that was later banned in Russia, said that the group no longer existed and was not involved in any way. “Anyone currently orchestrating provocations within European Union countries under the banner of this ‘brand’ is acting in their own self-interest – essentially flying someone else’s flag,” he wrote on his popular Telegram channel. In France, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu’s office said he had sent fighter jets to intercept an Aer Lingus flight from Dublin to Rome and escort it to an air force base at Evreux after the pilot did not co-operate with authorities as expected. Lecornu’s office gave no reason for the pilot’s behaviour. Bulgaria’s Air Force said its fighter jets had escorted three airliners to the ground. One Ryanair flight from London to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria’s second city. Romania’s intelligence agency said a KLM flight to Tel Aviv with a layover in Bucharest had received a bomb threat.



Passengers wait at Vaclav Havel Airport in Prague after bomb hoaxes caused travel disruptions across Europe. Getty Images Spanish police said three emailed threats came in within 20 minutes involving two Air Europa departures from Madrid to Paris and four inbound Iberia flights from Rome and Milan. Several aircraft were halted or returned to their stands in Madrid, and passengers disembarked as the aircraft were inspected. In Warsaw, a LOT flight to Paris was stopped as it taxied toward take-off, and passengers were transferred to another plane, while Danish police said they searched two planes in Copenhagen. Other flights that received threats, including EasyJet, Finnair, LOT, Wizz Air, Ryanair and Air Serbia services to Prague, Sofia, Vienna, Brussels, Bucharest, Rome and Milan, landed as scheduled, some after military escorts. Elena Pala, a passenger on a Wizz Air flight from Milan, described what happened when the plane landed in Bucharest, Romania.



“First, they took us a long way from the terminal … far away on the runway. The plane was surrounded by fire trucks, ambulances and anti-terrorist units,” she told Digi TV. “I asked what was happening. They said it was an emergency issue. That is all they said,” Pala added. Joji Waites, director of flight safety for the British Airline Pilots’ Association, said airlines did not act on threats unless assessors rated them credible. Departing passengers were philosophical. “We still have to get around. So, well, we just have to deal with it as best we can,” said Spaniard Lucia Parga. Another traveller, Gabriele Franzese, added: “You can’t worry too much about every piece of news. If the plane crashes, so be it. If it’s meant to happen, it’ll happen anyway.”



Eliran Almog, chief executive of aviation cybersecurity firm Cyviation, said the hoaxes could both disrupt operations and let the perpetrators observe how airlines, airports, and authorities respond. “These aviation threats are also occurring in the same period as cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems across Europe,” Almog said. “Different essential services are experiencing disruption that carries economic costs and can undermine public confidence.” This week, unidentified hackers shut down fridges in supermarkets in several European countries for the second time, also affecting French blood banks. World.title: Former Cronulla Sharks star knocked out in first round
World.content:
Nelson Asofa-Solomona claims a racial taunt prompted him to lash out at a spectator in the moments after his devastating first-round knockout win over Paul Gallen.

Asofa-Solomona landed a straight right and two uppercuts that left Gallen sprawled on the canvas for several minutes, raising serious concerns about his health. The former NSW skipper eventually recovered sufficiently to congratulate Asofa-Solomona on the victory, but was rushed to hospital shortly afterwards.

Loading

Just moments after inflicting the final blow, the former Melbourne Storm forward leapt out of the ring to lash out at a spectator. He appeared poised to unleash a roundhouse right before pulling the punch.

“I looked into the crowd, and someone was making an ape gesture,” Asofa-Solomona said.

“I stood on the ropes, and it looked like someone threw something at me, so I just lost my temper. As I said, if I could have my time back, I would handle it differently, because that behavior isn’t acceptable. At the same time, what that person did with that gesture isn’t acceptable either.

“I think it was a mix of everything. The adrenaline was there, but I also don’t tolerate that kind of nonsense. Once I saw it, I just saw red. But like I said, if I could do it over, I wouldn’t do that again.”

Paul Gallen is knocked out by Nelson Asofa-Solomona. Getty Images

Gallen, at the age of 45, was no match for the bigger and younger man. “Big Nelson” was 15 years younger and 33 kilograms heavier, with a decided reach advantage that he exploited during the opening exchanges.

With the final seconds of the opening round ticking down, Asofa-Solomona landed a series of sickening blows. Two straight right hands, followed by four uppercuts all hit flush, with the last punches landing as Gallen was canvas bound.

“It’s pretty emotional,” Asofa-Solomona said. “I guess the build-up and everything - words were said.

“He’s the crossover heavyweight king. I remember watching him as a young kid growing up. Even when we were playing against each other, I admired what he did, because it’s not a road that everyone walks, you know? It’s a scary one.

“You get a lot of your ego from footy, and you have this character you want to uphold. When you step into the ring, you feel a bit exposed in there.”

Asofa-Solomona said that he was concerned about the welfare of Gallen after seeing him lie motionless on the canvas.

“Yeah, for sure,” he said. “Once things settled down, it kind of hit me what had just happened. Anyone who has been in that position knows that when things get heated, situations can quickly turn for the worse.

“I’m happy I got the win, but if I could have my time back regarding what happened at the end, I would change it.”

World.content:
PropertyNewsLuxury property Five of the best period homes for sale in Sydney Shona Hendley November 6, 2026 — 7:45pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. With great character, ornate features and spacious rooms, period homes can often tell a wonderful story and offer benefits for today’s lifestyle too. From Victorian terraces to Edwardians, here are five of the best period homes for sale in Sydney right now. 60 Willoughby Street, Kirribilli NSW Spanning three levels, this period 1880s home overlooks Careening Cove and has a commanding street presence.



The home has been refurbished but still has many of its original features, including leadlight windows, architraves, high ceilings, a wraparound balcony and fireplaces. There are north-facing gardens, a sandstone wine cellar and tasting room, and a plunge pool. Other features include its harbourside location opposite the foreshore and close to the ferry and train, plus public and private schools, and lift access from the three-car garage. 51 Boyce Street, Glebe NSW



Located in the tightly held Toxteth Estate on a tree-lined street, this c. 1880 freestanding Victorian blends its distinctive period design with contemporary updates. Period features include its facade, high ceilings, parquet floors, formal lounge and dining rooms and fireplaces. An indoor-outdoor flow links the two private courtyards to the open-plan family rooms and kitchen, which has stone benchtops and a walk-in pantry. The home is close to Glebe Village, Foreshore Parklands, the Fish Market, light rail and Tramsheds, and includes rear lane parking. 7 Wallace Street, Balmain NSW



Part of a landmark Victorian Italianate row dating back to c. 1887, this Balmain terrace showcases quality craftsmanship. The ornate six-metre-wide facade and north-facing Juliet balconies set the tone. Period features are evident throughout the three-storey home, including the elegant entry hall, custom wainscoting, 3.4-metre-high ceilings, original floorboards and fireplaces. Luxury architectural firm Luxitecture’s updates are showcased in the Calacatta marble gas kitchen, featuring Gaggenau and Miele appliances and a cocktail bar with custom joinery. Outside, a north-facing entertainer’s courtyard is filled with greenery.



18 Cobden Street, Enfield NSW This Enfield Victorian has been extensively updated into a modern, luxurious family home. The original facade remains, as do the high ceilings and bay windows. With nine bedrooms and four bathrooms across two levels and a north-east to rear aspect, the floor plan offers ample space and flexibility for multigenerational families or investors.



Other features include off-street parking for up to seven vehicles, an in-ground swimming pool, covered al fresco dining for outdoor entertaining, and a location close to schools, parklands, shops, and accessible transport links to Burwood and the CBD. 32 Jersey Road, Paddington NSW This double-storey Paddington terrace has received a contemporary extension. With a concrete slab and double brick additions, the updates also include the Carrara Bianco kitchen with custom shaker cabinetry, a 2.5 metre island, a concealed appliance station and quality appliances.



Natural light fills the interior through a series of skylights; it features herringbone floors, detailed skirtings/architraves, underfloor heating and heated towel rails in the bathrooms. Outside, there is low -maintenance Futurewood composite decking, outdoor gas fitting and power, and landscaping in the rear yard.

World.title: As one Sydney icon faces an uncertain future, another is born
World.content:
NationalNSWNote From The Editor As one Sydney icon faces an uncertain future, another is born Jordan Baker November 6, 2026 — 7:45pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

My first job after finishing school was behind a perfume counter at David Jones’ Elizabeth Street store. I couldn’t believe my luck; to me, the DJs ground floor, with its art deco chandeliers and French cosmetic houses, was the most elegant place in Sydney. Wearing black from head to toe, I’d spray scents from Balenciaga or Givenchy onto the wrists of well-heeled matrons from the eastern suburbs. They’d hand me their David Jones card and walk away with their houndstooth bag. Sydney’s well-heeled came to shop at the DJs perfume counter. Bloomberg DJs advertised for casuals to fill Christmas shifts every year, timed perfectly with the end of the HSC. When my turn came, I had rushed to apply. We had always been a David Jones family (Mum wouldn’t shop at Grace Bros, which was taken over by Myer). As a kid, my mother, grandmother, great-grandmother and I would take the double-decker bus to town a few times a year; three of the party would have their DJ cards primed and the fourth had high hopes of a milkshake at the cafeteria. DJs was where mum would buy my “good” dress. It was where – like the Herald’s deputy national editor Stephanie Peatling – I was fitted for my first bra. It was where I learnt about working life, while clocking on and off at the staff entrance with an army of ladies (and the odd gentleman) in black. DJs was masterful at curating a deep and abiding loyalty. You weren’t a David Jones shopper; you were a David Jones person. And yet a decade or so ago, I stopped shopping there. Online ordering was easier. I could find the same brands elsewhere. Children grew out of their clothes too fast to warrant much investment in their wardrobes. And it appears I am not alone; this week, amid declining sales and mounting losses, David Jones was put into administration. Luxury brands, which for decades gave DJs its cache, ripped their products from its shelves.





From the outset, the museum has been controversial. When Mike Baird originally proposed it, the plan was to sell off the Powerhouse’s Ultimo site. Amid backlash, that plan was shelved. The decision to build the new museum was interrogated by two parliamentary inquiries (one described it as a thought bubble). Most recently, in August, Powerhouse Parramatta’s chief executive stepped down pending a procurement and governance investigation. Over a decade, the Herald has reported in great depth on the difficult birth of Powerhouse Parramatta. Now, it’s here; our readers can follow tomorrow’s opening ceremony on our live blog and get a glimpse of the exhibitions that, from tomorrow, they can visit themselves. I’d particularly recommend a piece by Linda Morris, to be published tomorrow morning, on the person who will be conspicuously absent from the celebrations. Some think the Powerhouse, with its enormous halls that can house new exhibits every few years, is brilliant and innovative; others worry it will be an expensive, visually striking white elephant. We will hear the verdicts of experts and visitors alike over the next few days, but ultimately, history will judge the museum – and those who drove it – by how it is embraced by the people of Sydney, both now and in the years ahead. We’ll share our view soon, but we’re keen to hear what you think, too. Get a weekly wrap of views that will challenge, champion and inform your own.

World.title: Labor flags corruption risks for widening police DV powers
World.content:
PoliticsQueenslandQueensland government Labor flags corruption risks for widening police DV powers Matt Dennien November 6, 2026 — 7:39pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Queensland’s Labor opposition has raised major concerns with a government push to expand police on-the-spot domestic violence order powers, urging greater safeguards as an LNP-controlled committee rubber-stamped the bill for passage through parliament. In a statement of reservation attached to the committee report, released on Friday, Labor MPs highlighted a submission from the Crime and Corruption Commission warning of the inherent risk of such powers and unwinding of a key oversight measure. A separate government-controlled committee has also greenlit another bill which would place significant new limits on who can lodge objections to mining lease applications, and whether those objections will be heard by the state’s Land Court. The Victims’ Commissioner has also urged a long-awaited Police Integrity Unit be “established as soon as possible to enhance victim and community confidence”. Michelle Smith The Crisafulli government introduced the bill to expand the police powers in September, citing criticism from police that an initial scheme established late last year, and due for review within two years but not yet subject to one, was too onerous to be of use.



Most existing restrictions around use of the “police protection directions” would be removed, and directions will be able to be issued for up to three years, rather than one. Previous powers acting as a stop-gap until a matter could be urgently heard in court will be repealed. Issuing a direction will be a requirement when releasing a person from custody, unless that person is deemed to be most in need of protection, and any direction “in error” will be able to be scrubbed from a person’s domestic violence history. “There is no clear rationale for the change in policy position from 2025 ...” Crime and Corruption Commission submission Police will still have to file a direction with a court in certain circumstances, such as when there are related proceedings under way. The bill will also increase penalties for repeat breaches of domestic violence orders, and expand a statewide electronic monitoring trial. The corruption watchdog’s submission to education, arts and communities committee consideration of the bill noted the proposed removal of exclusions barring police from issuing a direction when another officer is involved as either the alleged perpetrator or victim.



This had been done, according to explanatory notes at the time, “to ensure DFV [domestic and family violence] matters involving police are heard by a court and are not handled internally,” the watchdog noted. Related Article Queensland government Police handed new powers to issue on-the-spot domestic violence orders “The Bill removes the protection this exclusion provides,” acting chair Kathryn McMillan wrote. “There is no clear rationale for the change in policy position from 2025, nor provision for additional safeguards to manage the potential risks that may arise in circumstances where a police officer is involved in a DFV matter.” McMillan said there were inherent corruption risks associated with discretionary police powers around issuing such directions when an officer is involved, and said dumping safeguards appeared at odds with calls from the 2022 Richards Inquiry – including for a new police integrity unit.



Labor MPs noted a submission from the Victims’ Commissioner also highlighted that outstanding work, and urged that the unit be “established as soon as possible to enhance victim and community confidence in police integrity”. Related Article Queensland government ‘Fossil fuel free-for-all’: Queensland to block ‘activists’ from objecting to mining leases “The Attorney-General [Deb Frecklington] has now had more than two years, and the government is still only considering the recommendation,” the Labor MPs wrote, noting they supported reforms giving police better support to protect victims survivors and the community. “Again, these steps need to be based in the evidence, and they must be carefully balanced with the inherent risks that are associated with responding to domestic and family violence and they need to have victim survivors front and centre. “This bill, without additional safeguards, does not appear to meet that threshold.”



The committee recommended the bill pass as drafted. The committee leading consideration of the government’s mining objection overhaul suggested one change to allow objections from neighbouring councils. Labor MPs, along with Traeger MP Robbie Katter, also issued statements of reservation in the report on that bill, citing the removal of pathways for community involvement in decision-making. Parliament returns for its next three-day sitting week on November 17. The government, with its majority, does not require votes of the Opposition or crossbench to pass laws. World.title: It’s a New Zealand election with a twist. What’s at stake?
World.content:
WorldOceaniaWorld elections It’s a New Zealand election with a twist. What’s at stake? Felicity Lewis November 6, 2026 — 7:30pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

New Zealanders head to the polls on Saturday in an election dominated by the cost of living, how to handle a more uncertain world, and a young party leader vying to become a new “kingmaker”. Aucklander Qiulae Wong, 38, was a consultant at KPMG last year when she saw a job  to lead a political party called Opportunity, according to The Financial Times. “Wong sees a chance to upend New Zealand’s political landscape, arguing that voters are disillusioned with ‘the Chrises’,” the paper suggests. Left to right: NZ PM Chris Luxon, Opportunity leader Qiulae Wong and the Labour Party’s Chris Hipkins. Fairfax Media The “two Chrises”, as they are widely known, are Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, 56, former head of Air New Zealand, and former Labour PM Chris Hipkins, who briefly replaced Jacinda Ardern after she resigned as leader in 2023. Since winning most seats in that year’s election, Luxon’s centre-right National Party has governed in a coalition with the ACT (Association of Consumers and Taxpayers) and New Zealand First, led by political veteran and former kingmaker Winston Peters.



In opposition, Hipkins and the centre-left Labour Party have formed a broadly progressive bloc with the Greens and Te Pati Māori (the Māori Party), whose members include Hana-Rawhiti Maipi-Clarke, known – and censured – for her trademark Haka performances in parliament. Opportunity, previously The Opportunities Party (TOP), was founded in 2016 by economist Gareth Morgan and has never won a seat in parliament. It says it is neither left- nor right-wing but wants to act as a “political circuit-breaker”, working constructively with both sides of politics. Photo: Getty Images ‘We still want to grow successful businesses and have a strong economy, but we think we can do that in a way that looks after nature and looks after people.’ Qiulae Wong, Opportunity leader



Unlike Ardern, who became PM at 37 in 2017, Wong was new to politics before last year. She says Opportunity’s supporters want “a more aspirational” vision for New Zealand’s future. Rebuilding trust in politics, including by delivering long-term solutions, is part of its pitch. Its core supporters, the mother of two told Bloomberg, are people like her – “future-focused Millennials; a lot of young parents who have grown up between this old-fashioned kind of economy, which is very extractive of nature and all about individual pursuit of wealth, and see that we need to do things differently. Loading “We still want to grow successful businesses and have a strong economy, but we think we can do that in a way that looks after nature and looks after people.” New Zealand has a unicameral parliament (it abolished its upper house in 1951) and holds elections every three years. Under its mixed-member proportional voting system, smaller parties can end up shaping who forms government.



Polling shows a slender margin between the ruling Nationals and Labour, with neither likely to form a majority, while Opportunity seems set to pass the 5 per cent threshold that would entitle it to seats and could deliver the balance of power. Qiulae Wong talks with a market seller while campaigning in October. Getty Images “You’ve got a left and a right bloc,” Connor Graham, a research fellow at Lowy Institute, says, “and neither coalition is consistently polling over 50 per cent, in a way that would lead to them having a majority government. The lion’s share of those remaining votes would go to Opportunity – and that’s sort of your teal,” he says, referring to the Australian independents. Wong, whom The Economist has described as a “millennial centrist”, has outlined five “bottom lines” should her party hold the balance of power: to “bring down bills for Kiwi households” by taking action on anticompetitive behaviour and reforming rules on lobbying and political donations. She also has a 10-year plan for funded health care, seeks an end to bottom fish-trawling in some ocean areas, and a recommitment to the Paris Agreement on climate change.



Wong has also pitched a land value tax of 1.75 per cent annually on residential ​land and 0.5 per cent on rural land, which her party says would fund broader tax changes. Christopher Luxon on the campaign trail this week. Getty Images Luxon has said his party would not partner with Opportunity, while Hipkins has said Labour is more aligned with Opportunity than the National Party. “Opportunity have remained pragmatic,” says Lowy’s Connor Graham, “and said, ‘we are going to negotiate with whoever has the most votes if we get our 5 per cent’. So it could be quite an interesting situation on the weekend where we have two blocs somewhere in the mid- to high-40s, then one kingmaker independent teal party with five strict non-negotiables.” Labour’s Chris Hipkins poses for a selfie this week. Getty Images



The Green Party, led by Chloe Swarbrick and Marama Davidson, is also enjoying some of the strongest polling in its history, reports The New York Times, with support at about 14.5 per cent. Meanwhile, unemployment is at its highest since 2015, and New Zealand’s economy has barely grown in three years. Housing affordability, rents and a shortage of social housing remain major concerns. Ageing public assets have also raised questions about how to pay for better infrastructure. New Zealand is also juggling deep trade links with China against security ties with Australia, the US and other Western partners. Connor Graham says the parties’ stances differ markedly on issues such as whether to explore technology co-operation under the AUKUS Pillar Two agreement (the part that does not involve nuclear submarines). This election will be defining for how the nation engages with a fast-changing world order and the shape of its longstanding “independent foreign policy mantra”, he says. It has resonance for Australia, too, he contends, “which is also wrestling with its place in a changing world, with its closest ally, the US, particularly unpredictable.” With wires Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.content:
NationalVictoriaCrime Man dead after stabbing in Melbourne CBD Alexander Darling November 6, 2026 — 11:21pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. One man in dead and another is in hospital after an apparent late-night stabbing in Melbourne’s CBD. Police were called to a restaurant in Frederick Way near Queen Victoria Market shortly after 8pm where they found a man with stab wounds. CPR was performed, but the man was declared dead at the scene. A short time later, a second man in his 30s was located nearby with a suspected stab wound and was taken to hospital. Police near the scene of the fatal stabbing which happened in a small laneway near Queen Victoria Market. Alexander Darling Police established two crime scenes about 100 metres apart, with major roads closed soon after the incident in an area of the city which is home to a large community of Chinese students and tourists.



The incident lit up social media apps with one user of RedNote, a Chinese social networking site, claiming to have heard from witnesses of the incident. “They say a delivery driver went inside to pick up an order, and while he was there, some random guy outside deliberately pushed his e-bike over,” the user wrote. Police closed streets in the north-west corner of the city following the incident. Alexander Darling “When the rider realised and went out to confront him, the other guy suddenly pulled out a knife and stabbed it right in his chest. “This is a huge wake-up call for all of us delivering food in Melbourne.”



Footage circulating on social media platform WeChat seen by this masthead shows a man in a bicycle helmet and a high-vis vest slumped against a wall in a restaurant on Frederick Way, being helped by a woman, with a trail of blood on the floor in front of him. Police set up two crime scenes about 100 metres apart. Alexander Darling The incident came on the same day that three people were stabbed in Melbourne’s south-east, sending a nearby primary school into lockdown. Emergency services were called to a home on Woodlee Street in Dandenong about 11.30am after three people were found with injuries believed to be stab wounds.



The incident resulted in a 28-year-old woman being rushed to hospital with life-threatening injuries, while two men, 26 and 35, were treated for serious but non-life-threatening injuries. Police said they were still in the early stages of understanding what had happened, with family violence detectives investigating. They said the three people injured were known to each other. Acting Inspector Rebecca Hall said on Friday afternoon that Dandenong North Primary School, on nearby Cleeland Street, was placed into lockdown after the incident. Police and SES at the scene in Dandenong on Friday afternoon. Nine News “The children were prevented from coming to the street, so they didn’t witness anything,” she said. “Parents have been notified about how to pick up their children.”



Hall said it was too early to confirm many details about the incident, including exactly how the people were known to each other, if a weapon had been recovered and whether the incident happened inside the house on Woodlee Street or outside. Be the first to know when major news happens.
